title: American Stories
zh: 美国经典短篇小说：欧·亨利、马克·吐温、爱伦·坡、杰克·伦敦……用简化英语慢速朗读，分段中文翻译。
credit: 听力内容来自 VOA Learning English《American Stories》，公共领域，learningenglish.voanews.com

lessons.title: Paul Bunyan
lessons.sum: 美国伐木工人传说中的巨人英雄保罗·班扬：一出生就要五只大鸟抬着，翻个身就引发地震；他养了一头蓝色的大牛“宝贝”，挖出五大湖，开辟森林，留下了许多夸张又好笑的故事。

lines.en: Today we tell a traditional American story called a "tall tale." A tall tale is a story about a person who is larger than life. The descriptions in the story are exaggerated – much greater than in real life. This makes the story funny. Long ago, the people who settled in undeveloped areas in America first told tall tales. After a hard day's work, people gathered to tell each other funny stories.
lines.zh: 今天我们讲一个传统的美国故事，叫作“荒诞故事”（tall tale）。荒诞故事讲的是一个比真人更了不起的人物。故事里的描写都很夸张——比现实大得多，所以很好笑。很久以前，在美国未开发地区定居的人们最先讲起了荒诞故事。辛苦干完一天活，人们聚在一起互相讲好笑的故事。

lines.en: Each group of workers had its own tall tale hero. Paul Bunyan was a hero of North America's lumberjacks, the workers who cut down trees. He was known for his strength, speed and skill. Tradition says he cleared forests from the northeastern United States to the Pacific Ocean.
lines.zh: 每一群工人都有自己的荒诞故事英雄。保罗·班扬是北美伐木工人——也就是砍树的工人——心中的英雄。他以力气大、速度快、本领强而出名。传说他把从美国东北部一直到太平洋的森林都清理了出来。

lines.en: Some people say Paul Bunyan was the creation of storytellers from the middle western Great Lakes area of the United States. Other people say the stories about him came from French Canada.
lines.zh: 有人说保罗·班扬是美国中西部五大湖地区的讲故事的人创造出来的。也有人说关于他的故事来自法属加拿大。

lines.en: Early in the twentieth century, a writer prepared a collection of Paul Bunyan stories. They were included in a publication from the Red River Lumber Company in Minnesota. It is not known if the stories helped the company's sales, but they became extremely popular.
lines.zh: 二十世纪初，一位作家整理了一本保罗·班扬故事集，收录在明尼苏达州红河木材公司的一份刊物里。不知道这些故事有没有帮公司多卖木材，不过它们变得非常受欢迎。

lines.en: Here is Shep O'Neal with our story about Paul Bunyan.
lines.zh: 下面请谢普·奥尼尔为我们讲保罗·班扬的故事。

lines.en: Many years ago, Paul Bunyan was born in the northeastern American state of Maine. His mother and father were shocked when they first saw the boy. Paul was so large at birth that five large birds had to carry him to his parents. When the boy was only a few weeks old, he weighed more than 45 kilograms.
lines.zh: 很多年前，保罗·班扬出生在美国东北部的缅因州。他的父母第一次看到这个孩子时都惊呆了。保罗生下来就太大了，得五只大鸟才能把他抬到父母身边。才几个星期大，他就重达 45 公斤以上。

lines.en: As a child, Paul was always hungry. His parents needed 10 cows to supply milk for his meals. Before long, he ate 50 eggs and 10 containers of potatoes every day.
lines.zh: 小时候，保罗总是饿。他的父母需要 10 头奶牛才能供上他喝的奶。没过多久，他每天要吃 50 个鸡蛋和 10 桶土豆。

lines.en: Young Paul grew so big that his parents did not know what to do with him. Once, Paul rolled over so much in his sleep that he caused an earthquake. This angered people in the town where his parents lived. So, the government told his mother and father they would have to move him somewhere else.
lines.zh: 小保罗长得太大了，父母不知道拿他怎么办。有一次，保罗睡觉时翻来覆去，竟然引发了地震。这惹恼了他父母所住镇上的人们。于是政府告诉他的父母，必须把他搬到别的地方去。

lines.en: Paul's father built a wooden cradle -- a traditional bed for a baby. His parents put the cradle in waters along the coast of Maine. However, every time Paul rolled over, huge waves covered all the coastal towns. So his parents brought their son back on land. They took him into the woods. This is where he grew up.
lines.zh: 保罗的父亲做了一个木头摇篮——一种传统的婴儿床。父母把摇篮放在缅因州沿岸的海水里。可是保罗每翻一次身，巨浪就会淹没所有的沿海城镇。于是父母又把儿子带回陆地，带进了树林。他就是在那里长大的。

lines.en: As a boy, Paul helped his father cut down trees. Paul had the strength of many men. He also was extremely fast. He could turn off a light and then jump into his bed before the room got dark.
lines.zh: 还是个男孩时，保罗就帮父亲砍树。保罗有好多个人加起来的力气。他还快得惊人：他能关掉灯，在屋子变黑之前跳上床。

lines.en: Maine is very cold for much of the year. One day, it started to snow. The snow covered Paul's home and a nearby forest. However, this snow was very unusual. It was blue. The blue snow kept falling until the forest was covered.
lines.zh: 缅因州一年中大部分时间都很冷。有一天，开始下雪了。雪盖住了保罗的家和附近的一片森林。可这场雪很不寻常——它是蓝色的。蓝色的雪一直下，直到把整片森林都盖住。

lines.en: Paul put on his snowshoes and went out to see the unusual sight. As he walked, Paul discovered an animal stuck in the snow. It was a baby ox. Paul decided to take the ox home with him. He put the animal near the fireplace. After the ox got warmer, his hair remained blue.
lines.zh: 保罗穿上雪鞋，出门去看这奇景。走着走着，他发现一只动物陷在雪里。那是一头小公牛。保罗决定把它带回家。他把小牛放在壁炉边。小牛暖和过来以后，毛还是蓝色的。

lines.en: Paul decided to keep the blue ox and named him Babe. Babe grew very quickly. One night, Paul left him in a small building with the other animals. The next morning, the barn was gone and so was Babe. Paul searched everywhere for the animal. He found Babe calmly eating grass in a valley, with the barn still on top of his back. Babe followed Paul and grew larger every day. Every time Paul looked, Babe seemed to grow taller.
lines.zh: 保罗决定留下这头蓝牛，给它取名叫“宝贝”（Babe）。宝贝长得飞快。一天晚上，保罗把它和别的动物一起关在一间小屋里。第二天早上，牲口棚不见了，宝贝也不见了。保罗到处找。他发现宝贝正在一个山谷里悠闲地吃草，背上还驮着那间牲口棚。宝贝跟着保罗，一天比一天大。保罗每看它一眼，它好像都又长高了。

lines.en: In those days, much of North America was filled with thick, green forests. Paul Bunyan could clear large wooded areas with a single stroke of his large, sharp axe.
lines.zh: 那时候，北美大部分地方都是茂密的绿色森林。保罗·班扬挥一下他那把又大又锋利的斧子，就能清出一大片林地。

lines.en: Paul taught Babe to help with his work. Babe was very useful. For example, Paul had trouble removing trees along a road that was not straight. He decided to tie one end of the road to what remained of a tree in the ground. Paul tied the other end to Babe. Babe dug his feet in the ground and pulled with all his strength until the road became straight.
lines.zh: 保罗教宝贝帮他干活。宝贝非常有用。比如，有一条路弯弯曲曲，保罗很难清除路边的树。他决定把路的一头拴在地里剩下的一个树桩上，另一头拴在宝贝身上。宝贝双脚蹬地，用尽全身力气拉，直到把路拉直了。

lines.en: In time, Paul and Babe the Blue Ox left Maine, and moved west to look for work in other forests. Along the way, Paul dug out the Great Lakes to provide drinking water for Babe. They settled in a camp near the Onion River in the state of Minnesota.
lines.zh: 后来，保罗和蓝牛宝贝离开缅因州，往西去别的森林找活干。一路上，保罗挖出了五大湖，好让宝贝有水喝。他们在明尼苏达州洋葱河附近的一个营地住了下来。

lines.en: Paul decided to get other lumberjacks to help with the work. His work crew became known as the Seven Axemen. Each man was more than 2 meters tall and weighed more than 160 kilograms. All of the Axemen were named Elmer. That way, they all came running whenever Paul called them.
lines.zh: 保罗决定找别的伐木工来帮忙。他的工作队被称为“七斧手”。每个人身高都超过 2 米，体重都超过 160 公斤。七斧手全都叫埃尔默。这样，保罗一喊，他们就全都跑过来了。

lines.en: The man who cooked for the group was named Sourdough Sam. He made everything -- except coffee -- from sourdough, a substance used in making sourdough bread.
lines.zh: 给大家做饭的人叫“酸面团山姆”。除了咖啡，他什么都用酸面团做——酸面团是做酸面包用的一种发酵面团。

lines.en: Every Sunday, Paul and his crew ate hot cakes. Each hot cake was so large that it took five men to eat one. Paul usually had 10 or more hot cakes, depending on how hungry he was. The table where the men ate was so long that a server usually drove to one end of the table and stayed the night. The server drove back in the morning, with a fresh load of food.
lines.zh: 每个星期天，保罗和他的工人们都吃热煎饼。每张煎饼都大得要五个人才能吃完一张。保罗通常要吃 10 张甚至更多，看他有多饿。工人们吃饭的桌子太长了，上菜的人通常开车到桌子另一头，还得在那儿过一夜，第二天早上再拉着一车新鲜食物开回来。

lines.en: Paul needed someone to help with the camp's finances. He gave the job to a man named Johnny Inkslinger. Johnny kept records of everything, including wages and the cost of feeding Babe. He sometimes used nine containers of writing fluid a day to keep such detailed records.
lines.zh: 保罗需要有人帮营地管账。他把这份工作交给一个叫约翰尼·墨水手的人。约翰尼什么都记账，包括工钱和喂宝贝的花费。为了记这么详细的账，他有时一天要用掉九瓶墨水。

lines.en: The camp also was home to Sport, the Reversible Dog. One of the workers accidentally cut Sport in two. The man hurried to put the dog back together, but made a mistake. He bent the animal's back the wrong way. However, that was not a problem for Sport. He learned to run on his front legs until he was tired. Then, he turned the other way and ran on his back legs.
lines.zh: 营地里还住着“可翻转的狗”斯波特。一个工人不小心把斯波特砍成了两半。那人赶紧把狗拼回去，却拼错了——他把狗的后背弯反了。不过这对斯波特不是问题。它学会了先用前腿跑，跑累了，再翻个身用后腿跑。

lines.en: Big mosquitoes were a problem at the camp. The men attacked the insects with their axes and long sticks. Before long, the men put barriers around their living space. Then, Paul ordered them to get big bees to destroy the mosquitoes. But the bees married the mosquitoes, and the problem got worse. They began to produce young insects. One day, the insects' love of sweets caused them to attack a ship that was bringing sugar to the camp. At last, the mosquitoes and bees were defeated. They ate so much sugar they could not move.
lines.zh: 营地里的大蚊子是个麻烦。工人们用斧子和长棍攻击这些虫子。没多久，他们在住处周围设了屏障。后来保罗命令他们弄来大蜜蜂消灭蚊子。可蜜蜂和蚊子结了婚，问题更糟了——它们开始生小虫子。有一天，这些虫子因为爱吃甜食，去攻击一艘给营地运糖的船。最后，蚊子和蜜蜂终于被打败了：它们吃了太多糖，动都动不了了。

lines.en: Paul always gave Babe the Blue Ox a 35-kilogram piece of sugar when he was good. But sometimes Babe liked to play tricks. At night, Babe would make noises and hit the ground with his feet. The men at the camp would run out of the buildings where they slept, thinking it was an earthquake.
lines.zh: 宝贝表现好的时候，保罗总会奖给它一块 35 公斤的糖。不过宝贝有时也爱搞恶作剧。夜里，它会发出声响，用脚跺地。营地里的人以为地震了，纷纷从睡觉的屋子里跑出来。

lines.en: When winter came, Babe had trouble finding enough food to eat. Snow covered everything. Ole the Blacksmith solved the problem. He made huge green sunglasses for Babe. When Babe wore the sunglasses, he thought the snow was grass. Before long, Babe was strong and healthy again.
lines.zh: 冬天来了，宝贝很难找到足够的食物。到处都被雪覆盖。铁匠奥利解决了这个问题：他给宝贝做了一副巨大的绿色太阳镜。宝贝戴上太阳镜，就以为雪是草。没过多久，宝贝又变得强壮健康了。

lines.en: One year, Paul's camp was especially cold. It was so cold that the men let their facial hair grow very long. When the men spoke, their words froze in the air. Everything they said remained frozen all winter long, and did not melt until spring.
lines.zh: 有一年，保罗的营地特别冷。冷得工人们都把胡子留得很长。人们一说话，话语就在空中冻住了。他们说的每句话整个冬天都冻着，直到春天才化开。

lines.en: Paul Bunyan and Babe left their mark on many areas. Some people say they were responsible for creating Puget Sound in the western state of Washington. Others say Paul Bunyan and Babe cleared the trees from the states of North Dakota and South Dakota. They prepared this area for farming.
lines.zh: 保罗·班扬和宝贝在许多地方留下了印记。有人说西部华盛顿州的普吉特湾就是他们造出来的。也有人说是保罗·班扬和宝贝清除了北达科他州和南达科他州的树木，为那里的农业做好了准备。

lines.en: Babe the Blue Ox died in South Dakota. One story says he ate too many hot cakes. Paul buried his old friend there. Today, the burial place is known as the Black Hills.
lines.zh: 蓝牛宝贝死在了南达科他州。有个故事说它是吃了太多煎饼。保罗把这位老朋友埋在了那里。今天，那块墓地就是有名的黑山。

lines.en: Whatever happened to Paul Bunyan? There are lots of stories. Some people say he was last seen in Alaska, or even the Arctic Circle. Another tradition says he still returns to Minnesota every summer. It says Paul moves in and out of the woods, so few people ever know that he is there.
lines.zh: 保罗·班扬后来怎么样了？说法很多。有人说最后一次看到他是在阿拉斯加，甚至是在北极圈。另一种说法是他每年夏天还会回明尼苏达州。据说保罗在树林里出出进进，所以很少有人知道他在那儿。

qs.q: What is a "tall tale"?
opts: a funny story with exaggerated descriptions
qs.a: a funny story with exaggerated descriptions
qs.why: "The descriptions in the story are exaggerated."

qs.q: What color was Babe the ox?
qs.a: blue
qs.why: Babe the Blue Ox — 蓝牛宝贝。

qs.q: Why did Babe think the snow was grass?
qs.a: He wore green sunglasses.
qs.why: "He made huge green sunglasses for Babe."

gloss: 可翻转的，两面都能用的

lessons.title: Pecos Bill
lessons.sum: 美国西部牛仔传说：佩科斯·比尔小时候从马车上摔下，被郊狼养大，以为自己是野兽；后来他成了最了不起的牛仔，骑美洲狮、拿响尾蛇当套索、骑着龙卷风降雨，最后和新娘一起被弹上了月亮。

lines.en: Today we tell a traditional American story called a "tall tale." A tall tale is a story about a person who is larger than life. The descriptions in the story are exaggerated – much greater than in real life. Long ago, the people who settled in undeveloped areas in America first told tall tales. After a hard day's work, people gathered to tell each other funny stories.
lines.zh: 今天我们讲一个传统的美国故事，叫作“荒诞故事”。荒诞故事讲的是一个比真人更了不起的人物，故事里的描写都很夸张，比现实大得多。很久以前，在美国未开发地区定居的人们最先讲起了荒诞故事。辛苦干完一天活，人们聚在一起互相讲好笑的故事。

lines.en: Pecos Bill was a larger than life hero of the American West. No one knows who first told stories about Pecos Bill. Cowboys may have invented the stories. Others say Edward O'Reilly invented the character in stories he wrote for the Century Magazine in the early 1900s. The stories were collected in a book called "The Saga of Pecos Bill," published in 1923.
lines.zh: 佩科斯·比尔是美国西部一位传奇英雄。没人知道最早是谁讲起佩科斯·比尔的故事。可能是牛仔们编的；也有人说是爱德华·奥赖利在 20 世纪初为《世纪杂志》写故事时创造了这个人物。这些故事后来收进了 1923 年出版的《佩科斯·比尔传奇》一书。

lines.en: Another writer, James Cloyd Bowman, wrote an award-winning children's book called "Pecos Bill: The Greatest Cowboy of All Time." The book won the Newbery Honor in 1938.
lines.zh: 另一位作家詹姆斯·克洛伊德·鲍曼写了一本获奖童书《佩科斯·比尔：史上最伟大的牛仔》，这本书在 1938 年获得了纽伯瑞银奖。

lines.en: Pecos Bill was not a historical person. But he does represent the spirit of early settlers in the American West. His unusual childhood and extraordinary actions tell about people who believed there were no limits to what they could do. Now, here is Barbara Klein with our story.
lines.zh: 佩科斯·比尔不是真实的历史人物，但他代表了美国西部早期拓荒者的精神。他不寻常的童年和非凡的事迹，讲的是那些相信自己无所不能的人。下面请芭芭拉·克莱因为我们讲这个故事。

lines.en: Pecos Bill had one of the strangest childhoods a boy ever had. It all started after his father decided that there was no longer enough room in east Texas for his family.
lines.zh: 佩科斯·比尔的童年大概是所有男孩里最奇怪的。这一切要从他父亲认定东得克萨斯已经容不下他们一家开始。

lines.en: "Pack up, Ma!" he cried. "Neighbors movin' in 50 miles away! It's getting too crowded!"
lines.zh: “收拾东西，孩子他妈！”他喊道，“50 英里外都有邻居搬来了！太挤了！”

lines.en: So they loaded up a wagon with all their things. Now some say they had 15 children while others say 18. However many there were, the children were louder than thunder. And as they set off across the wild country of west Texas, their mother and father could hardly hear a thing.
lines.zh: 于是他们把所有家当装上马车。有人说他们有 15 个孩子，也有人说 18 个。不管有多少个，孩子们吵得比打雷还响。他们出发穿越西得克萨斯的荒野时，父母几乎什么都听不见。

lines.en: Now, as they came to the Pecos River, the wagon hit a big rock. The force threw little Bill out of the wagon and he landed on the sandy ground. Mother did not know Bill was gone until she gathered the children for the midday meal. Mother set off with some of the children to look for Bill, but they could find no sign of him.
lines.zh: 他们来到佩科斯河边时，马车撞上了一块大石头。这一撞把小比尔甩出了马车，落在沙地上。妈妈直到召集孩子们吃午饭时才发现比尔不见了。她带着几个孩子去找比尔，可一点踪迹也没找到。

lines.en: Well, some people say Bill was just a baby when his family lost him. Others say he was four years old. But all agree that a group of animals called coyotes found Bill and raised him. Bill did all the things those animals did, like chase lizards and howl at the moon. He became as good a coyote as any.
lines.zh: 嗯，有人说比尔被家人弄丢时还是个婴儿，也有人说他四岁了。但大家都同意，是一群叫郊狼的动物发现并养大了比尔。比尔做郊狼做的一切事，比如追蜥蜴、对着月亮嚎叫。他成了一只不比谁差的郊狼。

lines.en: Now, Bill spent 17 years living like a coyote until one day a cowboy rode by on his horse. Some say the cowboy was one of Bill's brothers. Whoever he was, he took one look at Bill and asked, "What are you?"
lines.zh: 比尔像郊狼一样生活了 17 年，直到有一天，一个牛仔骑马经过。有人说那个牛仔是比尔的哥哥之一。不管他是谁，他看了比尔一眼就问：“你是什么东西？”

lines.en: Bill was not used to human language. At first, he could not say anything. The cowboy repeated his question. This time, Bill said, "varmint."
lines.zh: 比尔不习惯人类的语言，起初什么也说不出来。牛仔又问了一遍。这次比尔说：“害兽（varmint）。”

lines.en: That is a word used for any kind of wild animal.
lines.zh: 这个词指任何一种野生动物。

lines.en: "No you aren't," said the cowboy.
lines.zh: “不，你不是。”牛仔说。

lines.en: "Yes, I am," said Bill. "I have fleas."
lines.zh: “是，我是。”比尔说，“我身上有跳蚤。”

lines.en: "Lots of people have fleas," said the cowboy. "You don't have a tail."
lines.zh: “很多人身上都有跳蚤，”牛仔说，“你又没有尾巴。”

lines.en: "Yes, I do," said Bill.
lines.zh: “有，我有。”比尔说。

lines.en: "Show it to me then," the cowboy said.
lines.zh: “那你给我看看。”牛仔说。

lines.en: Bill looked at his backside and realized that he did not have a tail like the other coyotes. "Well, what am I then?" asked Bill.
lines.zh: 比尔看了看自己的屁股，发现自己并没有像别的郊狼那样的尾巴。“那我到底是什么？”比尔问。

lines.en: "You're a cowboy! So start acting like one!" the cowboy cried out. Well that was all Bill needed to hear. He said goodbye to his coyote friends and left to join the world of humans.
lines.zh: “你是牛仔！那就像个牛仔的样子！”牛仔喊道。这就是比尔需要听到的全部了。他告别了郊狼朋友们，去加入人类的世界。

lines.en: Now, Pecos Bill was a good cowboy. Still, he hungered for adventure. One day he heard about a rough group of men. There is some debate over what the group was called. But one storyteller calls it the "Hell's Gate Gang."
lines.zh: 佩科斯·比尔是个好牛仔，可他还渴望冒险。有一天，他听说有一伙粗野的人。这伙人叫什么名字有些争议，不过有位讲故事的人管他们叫“地狱之门帮”。

lines.en: So Bill set out across the rough country to find this gang of men. Well, Bill's horse soon was injured so Bill had to carry it for a hundred miles. Then Bill met a rattlesnake 50 feet long. The snake made a hissing noise and was not about to let Bill pass. But after a tense minute, Bill beat the snake until it surrendered. He felt sorry for the varmint, though, and wrapped it around his arm.
lines.zh: 于是比尔出发穿越荒野去找这伙人。没多久比尔的马受了伤，他只好扛着马走了一百英里。接着比尔遇到一条 50 英尺长的响尾蛇。那蛇发出嘶嘶声，不肯让比尔过去。紧张地对峙了一分钟后，比尔把蛇打得服了软。不过他可怜这条“害兽”，把它缠在了自己胳膊上。

lines.en: After Bill walked another hundred miles, he came across an angry mountain lion. There was a huge battle, but Bill took control of the big cat and put his saddle on it. He rode that mountain lion all the way to the camp of the Hell's Gate Gang.
lines.zh: 比尔又走了一百英里，遇到一头愤怒的美洲狮。一场大战之后，比尔制服了这只大猫，给它装上马鞍，一路骑着它到了地狱之门帮的营地。

lines.en: Now, when Bill saw the gang he shouted out, "Who's the boss around here?"
lines.zh: 比尔一看到这帮人就大喊：“这儿谁是老大？”

lines.en: A huge cowboy, 9 feet tall, took one look at Bill and said in a shaky voice, "I was the boss. But you are the boss from here on in."
lines.zh: 一个 9 英尺高的大个子牛仔看了比尔一眼，声音发抖地说：“以前我是老大。从现在起你是老大。”

lines.en: With his gang, Pecos Bill was able to create the biggest ranch in the Southwest. Bill and his men had so many cattle that they needed all of New Mexico to hold them. Arizona was the pasture where the cattle ate grass.
lines.zh: 有了这帮人，佩科斯·比尔建起了西南部最大的牧场。比尔和手下的牛多得要整个新墨西哥州才装得下，亚利桑那州就是牛吃草的牧场。

lines.en: Pecos Bill invented the art of being a cowboy. He invented the skill of throwing a special rope called a lasso over a cow's head to catch wandering cattle.
lines.zh: 佩科斯·比尔发明了做牛仔的本领。他发明了把一种叫“套索”的特殊绳子甩到牛头上、套住走散的牛的技巧。

lines.en: Some say he used a rattlesnake for a lasso. Others say he made a lasso so big that it circled the whole Earth.
lines.zh: 有人说他用一条响尾蛇当套索。也有人说他做了一个大得能绕地球一圈的套索。

lines.en: Bill invented the method of using a hot branding iron to permanently put the mark of a ranch on a cow's skin. That helped stop people from stealing cattle. Some say he invented cowboy songs to help calm the cattle and make the cowboy's life easier. But he is also said to have invented tarantulas and scorpions as jokes. Cowboys have had trouble with those poisonous creatures ever since.
lines.zh: 比尔发明了用烧红的烙铁在牛皮上永久烙下牧场标记的方法，这有助于防止有人偷牛。有人说他还发明了牛仔歌，用来安抚牛群，让牛仔的生活轻松些。不过据说他也发明了狼蛛和蝎子来开玩笑。从那以后，牛仔们就一直被这些有毒的家伙困扰。

lines.en: Now, Pecos Bill could ride anything that ever was. So, as some tell the story, there came a storm bigger than any other. It all happened during the worst drought the West had ever seen. It was so dry that horses and cows started to dry up and blow away in the wind. So when Bill saw the windstorm, he got an idea. The huge tornado kicked across the land like a wild bronco. But Bill jumped on it without a thought.
lines.zh: 佩科斯·比尔什么都能骑。所以，有人这样讲：有一次来了一场史无前例的大风暴。那是西部有史以来最严重的旱灾，干得马和牛都开始干枯，被风吹走。比尔看到这场风暴，想到了一个主意。巨大的龙卷风像一匹野马一样在大地上横冲直撞，比尔想都没想就跳了上去。

lines.en: He rode that tornado across Texas, New Mexico and Arizona, all the time squeezing the rain out of it to save the land from drought. When the storm was over, Bill fell off the tornado. He landed in California. He left a hole so deep that to this day it is known as Death Valley.
lines.zh: 他骑着那股龙卷风穿过得克萨斯、新墨西哥和亚利桑那，一路把雨从龙卷风里挤出来，把大地从旱灾中救了出来。风暴结束时，比尔从龙卷风上摔了下来，落在加利福尼亚。他砸出一个深坑，深到今天人们都叫它“死亡谷”。

lines.en: Now, Bill had a horse named Widow Maker. He got that name because any man who rode that horse would be thrown off and killed, and his wife would become a widow. No one could ride that horse but Bill.
lines.zh: 比尔有一匹马叫“寡妇制造者”。它之所以叫这个名字，是因为任何骑它的男人都会被甩下来摔死，他的妻子就成了寡妇。除了比尔，没人能骑这匹马。

lines.en: And Widow Maker, in the end, caused the biggest problem for Pecos Bill. You see, one day Bill saw a woman. Not just any woman, but a wild, red-haired woman, riding a giant catfish down the Rio Grande River.
lines.zh: 而最后给佩科斯·比尔惹出最大麻烦的，正是“寡妇制造者”。你看，有一天比尔看到一个女人——不是普通的女人，而是一个狂野的红发女人，正骑着一条巨大的鲶鱼顺着格兰德河而下。

lines.en: Her name was Slue-foot Sue. And Bill fell in love with her at first sight. Well, Bill would not rest until he had asked for her hand in marriage. And Slue-foot Sue accepted.
lines.zh: 她叫“滑脚苏”。比尔对她一见钟情。比尔不向她求婚就不罢休。滑脚苏答应了。

lines.en: On their wedding day, Pecos Bill dressed in his best buckskin suit. And Sue wore a beautiful white dress with a huge steel-spring bustle in the back. It was the kind of big dress that many women wore in those days — the bigger the better.
lines.zh: 婚礼那天，佩科斯·比尔穿上他最好的鹿皮衣服。苏穿着一件漂亮的白裙子，后面有一个巨大的钢弹簧裙撑。那时很多女人都穿这种大裙子——越大越好。

lines.en: Now, after the marriage ceremony Slue-foot Sue got a really bad idea. She decided that she wanted to ride Widow Maker. Bill begged her not to try. But she had her mind made up.
lines.zh: 婚礼一结束，滑脚苏就冒出一个很糟糕的主意：她想骑“寡妇制造者”。比尔求她别试，可她已经下定了决心。

lines.en: Well, the second she jumped on the horse's back he began to kick and buck like nothing anyone had ever seen. He sent Sue flying so high that she sailed clear over the new moon.
lines.zh: 她一跳上马背，马就开始又踢又跳，那架势谁都没见过。它把苏甩得高高飞起，一直飞过了新月。

lines.en: She fell back to Earth, but the steel-spring bustle just bounced her back up as high as before.
lines.zh: 她落回地面，可钢弹簧裙撑又把她弹回到和刚才一样高。

lines.en: Now, there are many different stories about what happened next. One story says Bill saw that Sue was in trouble. She would keep bouncing forever if nothing was done. So he took his rope out -- though some say it was a huge rattlesnake -- and lassoed Sue to catch her and bring her down to Earth. Only, she just bounced him back up with her.
lines.zh: 接下来发生了什么，说法有很多。有一种说法是，比尔看出苏有麻烦了：如果不想办法，她会永远弹下去。于是他拿出绳子——也有人说是一条巨大的响尾蛇——套住苏，想把她拉回地面。可她却把他也一起弹了上去。

lines.en: Somehow the two came to rest on the moon. And that's where they stayed. Some people say they raised a family up there. Their children were as loud and wild as Bill and Sue were in their younger days. People say the sound of thunder that sometimes carries over the dry land around the Pecos River is nothing more than Pecos Bill's family laughing up a storm.
lines.zh: 不知怎么的，两人最后停在了月亮上，就在那儿住下了。有人说他们在上面养了一家人，孩子们和比尔、苏年轻时一样又吵又野。人们说，佩科斯河一带干旱的土地上空有时传来的雷声，不过是佩科斯·比尔一家在开怀大笑罢了。

qs.q: Who raised Pecos Bill?
qs.a: coyotes
qs.why: "a group of animals called coyotes found Bill and raised him."

qs.q: What did Bill ride to the Hell's Gate Gang camp?
qs.a: a mountain lion
qs.why: "He rode that mountain lion all the way to the camp."

qs.q: Where did Bill and Sue end up?
qs.a: on the moon
qs.why: "Somehow the two came to rest on the moon."

gloss: （美国旧式幽默说法）害兽，讨厌的野物

lessons.title: The Gift of the Magi
lessons.sum: 圣诞节前夜，穷困的年轻妻子德拉只有一美元八十七美分。为了给丈夫吉姆买一条配他金表的表链，她卖掉了自己最珍贵的长发；而吉姆为了给她买一套梳子，卖掉了祖传的金表。

lines.en: One dollar and eighty-seven cents. That was all. And sixty cents of it in the smallest pieces of money - pennies. Pennies saved one and two at a time by negotiating with the men at the market who sold vegetables and meat. Negotiating until one's face burned with the silent knowledge of being poor. Three times Della counted it. One dollar and eighty-seven cents. And the next day would be Christmas.
lines.zh: 一美元八十七美分。就这么多。其中六十美分还是最小的硬币——一美分的。这些硬币是一个两个攒下来的，靠的是跟卖菜卖肉的人讨价还价，讨到脸上发烫，心里默默明白自己有多穷。德拉数了三遍。一美元八十七美分。而第二天就是圣诞节了。

lines.en: There was clearly nothing to do but sit down and cry. So Della cried. Which led to the thought that life is made up of little cries and smiles, with more little cries than smiles.
lines.zh: 显然，除了坐下来哭一场，什么办法也没有。于是德拉哭了。这让人想到，生活就是由小小的哭泣和微笑组成的，而哭泣比微笑多。

lines.en: Della finished her crying and dried her face. She stood by the window and looked out unhappily at a gray cat walking along a gray fence in a gray back yard. Tomorrow would be Christmas Day, and she had only one dollar and eighty-seven cents to buy her husband Jim a gift. She had been saving every penny she could for months, with this result.
lines.zh: 德拉哭完，擦干了脸。她站在窗前，闷闷不乐地望着一只灰猫在灰色后院的灰色篱笆上走。明天就是圣诞节了，她只有一美元八十七美分给丈夫吉姆买礼物。她几个月来一分一分地攒，结果就攒了这么点。

lines.en: Jim earned twenty dollars a week, which does not go far. Expenses had been greater than she had expected. They always are. Many a happy hour she had spent planning to buy something nice for him. Something fine and rare -- something close to being worthy of the honor of belonging to Jim.
lines.zh: 吉姆一星期挣二十美元，花不了多久就没了。开销比她预想的大，开销总是这样。她曾花了许多快乐的时光，盘算着给他买件好东西——精致而难得的东西，配得上属于吉姆的那份荣耀的东西。

lines.en: There was a tall glass mirror between the windows of the room. Suddenly Della turned from the window and stood before the glass mirror and looked at herself. Her eyes were shining, but her face had lost its color within twenty seconds. Quickly she pulled down her hair and let it fall to its full length.
lines.zh: 屋子两扇窗户之间有一面高高的穿衣镜。德拉突然从窗前转过身，站到镜子前打量自己。她的眼睛闪闪发亮，可二十秒之内脸色就变得苍白。她迅速把头发放下来，让它完全披散开。

lines.en: Now, Mr. and Mrs. James Dillingham Young had two possessions which they valued. One was Jim's gold time piece, the watch that had been his father's and his grandfather's. The other was Della's hair.
lines.zh: 詹姆斯·迪林厄姆·杨夫妇有两样十分珍爱的东西。一样是吉姆的金表，那是他父亲和祖父传下来的。另一样就是德拉的头发。

lines.en: Had the Queen of Sheba lived in their building, Della would have let her hair hang out the window to dry just to reduce the value of the queen's jewels.
lines.zh: 假如示巴女王住在他们这栋楼里，德拉也会把头发垂到窗外去晾干，好让女王的珠宝黯然失色。

lines.en: So now Della's beautiful hair fell about her, shining like a brown waterfall. It reached below her knees and made itself almost like a covering for her. And then quickly she put it up again. She stood still while a few tears fell on the floor.
lines.zh: 此刻，德拉美丽的头发披散在身上，像一道棕色的瀑布闪闪发光。头发长过膝盖，几乎像一件衣服把她裹住。接着她又迅速把头发盘了起来。她静静地站着，几滴眼泪落在地板上。

lines.en: She put on her coat and her old brown hat. With a quick motion and brightness still in her eyes, she danced out the door and down the street.
lines.zh: 她穿上外套，戴上旧的棕色帽子。她动作飞快，眼里还闪着光，轻快地出了门，走到街上。

lines.en: Where she stopped the sign read: "Madame Sofronie. Hair Goods of All Kinds." Della ran up the steps to the shop, out of breath.
lines.zh: 她停下的地方挂着一块招牌：“索弗罗尼夫人。各类发制品。”德拉跑上台阶进了店，上气不接下气。

lines.en: "Will you buy my hair?" asked Della.
lines.zh: “您买我的头发吗？”德拉问。

lines.en: "I buy hair," said Madame. "Take your hat off and let us have a look at it."
lines.zh: “我收头发，”夫人说，“把帽子摘了，让我们看看。”

lines.en: Down came the beautiful brown waterfall of hair.
lines.zh: 那美丽的棕色瀑布倾泻而下。

lines.en: "Twenty dollars," said Madame, lifting the hair with an experienced hand.
lines.zh: “二十美元。”夫人用老练的手托起头发说。

lines.en: "Give it to me quick," said Della.
lines.zh: “快给我吧。”德拉说。

lines.en: The next two hours went by as if they had wings. Della looked in all the stores to choose a gift for Jim.
lines.zh: 接下来的两个小时像长了翅膀一样飞过。德拉逛遍了所有商店，给吉姆挑礼物。

lines.en: She found it at last. It surely had been made for Jim and no one else. It was a chain -- simple round rings of silver. It was perfect for Jim's gold watch. As soon as she saw it she knew that it must be for him. It was like him. Quiet and with great value. She gave the shopkeeper twenty-one dollars and she hurried home with the eighty-seven cents that was left.
lines.zh: 她终于找到了。它一定是专为吉姆做的，不是为别人。那是一条表链——简单的银色圆环串成的。配吉姆的金表再合适不过了。她一看到就知道它非吉姆莫属。它就像吉姆一样：朴素而珍贵。她付给店主二十一美元，揣着剩下的八十七美分赶回了家。

lines.en: When Della arrived home she began to repair what was left of her hair. The hair had been ruined by her love and her desire to give a special gift. Repairing the damage was a very big job.
lines.zh: 德拉到家后，开始收拾剩下的头发。这头发是被她的爱和想送一份特别礼物的心意毁掉的。修补这场“灾难”可是个大工程。

lines.en: Within forty minutes her head was covered with tiny round curls of hair that made her look wonderfully like a schoolboy. She looked at herself in the glass mirror long and carefully.
lines.zh: 四十分钟后，她满头都是细小的圆卷，看起来活像个小男生。她对着镜子仔仔细细地看了很久。

lines.en: "If Jim does not kill me before he takes a second look at me," she said to herself, "he'll say I look like a song girl. But what could I do--oh! what could I do with a dollar and eighty-seven cents?"
lines.zh: “要是吉姆看我第二眼之前没杀了我，”她自言自语道，“他会说我像个卖唱的姑娘。可我能怎么办——哦！一美元八十七美分，我能怎么办呢？”

lines.en: At seven o'clock that night the coffee was made and the pan on the back of the stove was hot and ready to cook the meat.
lines.zh: 那天晚上七点，咖啡煮好了，炉子后面的煎锅也热好了，准备煎肉。

lines.en: Jim was never late coming home from work. Della held the silver chain in her hand and sat near the door. Then she heard his step and she turned white for just a minute. She had a way of saying a little silent prayer about the simplest everyday things, and now she whispered: "Please God, make him think I am still pretty."
lines.zh: 吉姆下班从不晚回家。德拉手里握着银表链，坐在门边。接着她听见了他的脚步声，脸刷地白了一下。她习惯为最平常的小事默默祈祷几句，这时她低声说：“上帝啊，求你让他觉得我还是漂亮的。”

lines.en: The door opened and Jim stepped in. He looked thin and very serious. Poor man, he was only twenty-two and he had to care for a wife. He needed a new coat and gloves to keep his hands warm.
lines.zh: 门开了，吉姆走了进来。他看起来很瘦，神情严肃。可怜的人，他才二十二岁，就得养活一个妻子。他需要一件新大衣，还需要一副手套暖手。

lines.en: Jim stopped inside the door, as immovable as a dog smelling a bird. His eyes were fixed upon Della. There was an expression in them that she could not read, and it frightened her. It was not anger, nor surprise, nor fear, nor any of the feelings that she had been prepared for. He simply looked at her with a strange expression on his face. Della went to him.
lines.zh: 吉姆在门里站住了，像猎狗嗅到鸟一样一动不动。他的眼睛盯着德拉，那里面有一种她读不懂的表情，这让她害怕。那不是愤怒，不是惊讶，不是恐惧，也不是她事先准备好面对的任何一种情绪。他只是带着一种奇怪的表情看着她。德拉走到他身边。

lines.en: "Jim, my love," she cried, "do not look at me that way. I had my hair cut and sold because I could not have lived through Christmas without giving you a gift. My hair will grow out again. I just had to do it. My hair grows very fast. Say 'Merry Christmas!' Jim, and let us be happy. You do not know what a nice-- what a beautiful, nice gift I have for you."
lines.zh: “吉姆，亲爱的，”她喊道，“别那样看着我。我把头发剪下来卖了，因为不送你一件礼物，我过不了这个圣诞节。头发会再长出来的。我非这么做不可。我的头发长得很快。说声‘圣诞快乐’吧，吉姆，让我们开开心心的。你不知道我给你准备了一件多好——多美、多好的礼物。”

lines.en: "You have cut off your hair?" asked Jim, slowly, as if he had not accepted the information even after his mind worked very hard.
lines.zh: “你把头发剪掉了？”吉姆慢慢地问，好像费了好大劲动脑子，还是没能接受这个消息。

lines.en: "Cut it off and sold it," said Della. "Do you not like me just as well? I am the same person without my hair, right?
lines.zh: “剪下来卖了，”德拉说，“你不像以前那样喜欢我了吗？没有头发，我还是我呀，对吧？”

lines.en: Jim looked about the room as if he were looking for something.
lines.zh: 吉姆在屋里四处张望，好像在找什么东西。

lines.en: "You say your hair is gone?" he asked.
lines.zh: “你说你的头发没了？”他问。

lines.en: "You need not look for it," said Della. "It is sold, I tell you--sold and gone, too. It is Christmas Eve, boy. Be good to me, for it was cut for you. Maybe the hairs of my head were numbered," she went on with sudden serious sweetness, "but nobody could ever count my love for you. Shall I put the meat on, Jim?"
lines.zh: “你不用找了，”德拉说，“卖了，我告诉你——卖了，没了。今天是圣诞夜，亲爱的。对我好一点，头发是为你剪的。也许我头上的头发数得清，”她突然又温柔又认真地说下去，“可我对你的爱谁也数不清。我去煎肉好吗，吉姆？”

lines.en: Jim seemed to awaken quickly and put his arms around Della. Then he took a package from his coat and threw it on the table.
lines.zh: 吉姆好像一下子醒了过来，伸出双臂抱住德拉。然后他从大衣里掏出一个小包，扔在桌上。

lines.en: "Do not make any mistake about me, Dell," he said. "I do not think there is any haircut that could make me like my girl any less. But if you will open that package you may see why you had me frightened at first."
lines.zh: “别误会我，德尔，”他说，“我觉得不管什么发型，都不会让我少爱我的姑娘一点。不过你要是打开那个包，就会明白我刚才为什么愣住了。”

lines.en: White fingers quickly tore at the string and paper. There was a scream of joy; and then, alas! a change to tears and cries, requiring the man of the house to use all his skill to calm his wife.
lines.zh: 白皙的手指飞快地扯开绳子和包装纸。先是一声欢喜的尖叫；接着，唉！马上变成了眼泪和哭声，这家的男主人只好使出浑身解数来安慰妻子。

lines.en: For there were the combs -- the special set of objects to hold her hair that Della had wanted ever since she saw them in a shop window. Beautiful combs, made of shells, with jewels at the edge --just the color to wear in the beautiful hair that was no longer hers. They cost a lot of money, she knew, and her heart had wanted them without ever hoping to have them. And now, the beautiful combs were hers, but the hair that should have touched them was gone.
lines.zh: 因为包里是那套梳子——一套别头发用的梳子，德拉自从在一家商店橱窗里看见，就一直想要。漂亮的梳子，玳瑁做的，边上镶着宝石——颜色正好配她那头已经不再属于她的美丽长发。她知道它们很贵，她心里一直渴望，却从没指望能得到。如今，这套漂亮的梳子是她的了，可本该配上它们的头发却没了。

lines.en: But she held the combs to herself, and soon she was able to look up with a smile and say, "My hair grows so fast, Jim!"
lines.zh: 可她还是把梳子紧紧抱在怀里，过了一会儿，她抬起头，笑着说：“我的头发长得可快了，吉姆！”

lines.en: Then Della jumped up like a little burned cat and cried, "Oh, oh!"
lines.zh: 接着德拉像一只被烫着的小猫一样跳起来，叫道：“哦，哦！”

lines.en: Jim had not yet seen his beautiful gift. She happily held it out to him in her open hands. The silver chain seemed so bright.
lines.zh: 吉姆还没看到他那件漂亮的礼物呢。她开心地把它捧在摊开的手心里递给他。银表链显得那么亮。

lines.en: "Isn't it wonderful, Jim? I looked all over town to find it. You will have to look at the time a hundred times a day now. Give me your watch. I want to see how it looks on it."
lines.zh: “是不是很漂亮，吉姆？我找遍了全城才找到的。现在你一天得看一百次时间了。把你的表给我，我想看看配上是什么样子。”

lines.en: Instead of obeying, Jim fell on the couch and put his hands under the back of his head and smiled.
lines.zh: 吉姆没有照做，而是倒在沙发上，双手枕在脑后，笑了。

lines.en: "Dell," said he, "let us put our Christmas gifts away and keep them a while. They are too nice to use just right now. I sold my gold watch to get the money to buy the set of combs for your hair. And now, why not put the meat on."
lines.zh: “德尔，”他说，“我们把圣诞礼物收起来，先放一阵子吧。它们太好了，现在还用不上。我把金表卖了，换钱给你买了那套梳子。好了，去煎肉吧。”

lines.en: The magi were wise men--wonderfully wise men--who brought gifts to the Baby Jesus. They invented the art of giving Christmas gifts. Being wise, their gifts were wise ones. And here I have told you the story of two young people who most unwisely gave for each other the greatest treasures of their house. But in a last word to the wise of these days, let it be said that of all who give gifts, these two were the wisest. Everywhere they are wisest. They are the magi.
lines.zh: 麦琪是智者——非常聪明的智者——他们给婴儿耶稣带来了礼物，发明了赠送圣诞礼物的艺术。他们是智者，送的礼物也是聪明的礼物。而我在这里讲的，是两个年轻人的故事：他们极不聪明地为对方牺牲了家中最宝贵的东西。但最后，我要对今天的聪明人说一句：在所有送礼物的人当中，这两个人是最聪明的。无论在哪里，他们都是最聪明的。他们就是麦琪。

qs.q: What did Della sell?
qs.a: her hair
qs.why: "Twenty dollars," said Madame.

qs.q: What did Della buy for Jim?
opts: a silver chain for his watch
qs.a: a silver chain for his watch
qs.why: "It was a chain -- simple round rings of silver."

qs.q: Why can't Jim use his gift?
opts: He sold his watch to buy her combs.
qs.a: He sold his watch to buy her combs.
qs.why: "I sold my gold watch to get the money to buy the set of combs."

gloss: （《圣经》中）东方三贤士，给婴儿耶稣送礼的智者

lessons.title: The Last Leaf
lessons.sum: 纽约格林尼治村，年轻画家琼西得了肺炎，认定窗外常春藤的最后一片叶子落下时自己也会死去。一夜狂风暴雨后，那片叶子却依然挂在墙上……她重新燃起了活下去的希望，而叶子背后藏着老画家贝尔曼的秘密。

lines.en: Our story today is called "The Last Leaf." It was written by O. Henry. Here is Barbara Klein with the story.
lines.zh: 我们今天的故事叫《最后一片叶子》，作者是欧·亨利。下面请芭芭拉·克莱因为大家讲述。

lines.en: Many artists lived in the Greenwich Village area of New York. Two young women named Sue and Johnsy shared a studio apartment at the top of a three-story building. Johnsy's real name was Joanna.
lines.zh: 很多艺术家住在纽约的格林尼治村。两个年轻姑娘苏和琼西合住在一栋三层楼顶层的一间画室公寓里。琼西的本名叫乔安娜。

lines.en: In November, a cold, unseen stranger came to visit the city. This disease, pneumonia, killed many people. Johnsy lay on her bed, hardly moving. She looked through the small window. She could see the side of the brick house next to her building.
lines.zh: 十一月，一个冰冷的、看不见的陌生人来到了这座城市。这种疾病——肺炎——夺走了很多人的生命。琼西躺在床上，几乎一动不动。她透过小窗往外看，能看到隔壁那栋砖房的侧墙。

lines.en: One morning, a doctor examined Johnsy and took her temperature. Then he spoke with Sue in another room.
lines.zh: 一天早上，医生给琼西做了检查，量了体温。然后他在另一个房间跟苏谈话。

lines.en: "She has one chance in -- let us say ten," he said. "And that chance is for her to want to live. Your friend has made up her mind that she is not going to get well. Has she anything on her mind?"
lines.zh: “她只有——这么说吧，十分之一的希望，”他说，“而这点希望取决于她自己想不想活。你的朋友已经认定自己好不了了。她有什么心事吗？”

lines.en: "She -- she wanted to paint the Bay of Naples in Italy some day," said Sue.
lines.zh: “她——她想有一天去画意大利的那不勒斯湾。”苏说。

lines.en: "Paint?" said the doctor. "Bosh! Has she anything on her mind worth thinking twice -- a man for example?"
lines.zh: “画画？”医生说，“胡扯！她有没有什么值得多想一想的心事——比如说，一个男人？”

lines.en: "A man?" said Sue. "Is a man worth -- but, no, doctor; there is nothing of the kind."
lines.zh: “男人？”苏说，“男人值得——不，医生，没有这回事。”

lines.en: "I will do all that science can do," said the doctor. "But whenever my patient begins to count the carriages at her funeral, I take away fifty percent from the curative power of medicines."
lines.zh: “科学能做的我都会做，”医生说，“可是一旦我的病人开始数她葬礼上会有几辆马车，药效就得打对折。”

lines.en: After the doctor had gone, Sue went into the workroom and cried. Then she went to Johnsy's room with her drawing board, whistling ragtime.
lines.zh: 医生走后，苏走进工作室哭了一场。然后她拿着画板走进琼西的房间，吹着拉格泰姆小调。

lines.en: Johnsy lay with her face toward the window. Sue stopped whistling, thinking she was asleep. She began making a pen and ink drawing for a story in a magazine. Young artists must work their way to "Art" by making pictures for magazine stories. Sue heard a low sound, several times repeated. She went quickly to the bedside.
lines.zh: 琼西脸朝着窗户躺着。苏以为她睡着了，就不吹口哨了。她开始给一本杂志上的故事画钢笔素描。年轻画家要走向“艺术”，就得先给杂志故事画插图。苏听到一个低低的声音，重复了好几次。她赶紧走到床边。

lines.en: Johnsy's eyes were open wide. She was looking out the window and counting -- counting backward. "Twelve," she said, and a little later "eleven"; and then "ten" and "nine;" and then "eight" and "seven," almost together.
lines.zh: 琼西的眼睛睁得大大的。她望着窗外，在数数——倒着数。“十二。”她说，过了一会儿又说“十一”；接着是“十”和“九”；然后“八”和“七”几乎是一起说出来的。

lines.en: Sue looked out the window. What was there to count? There was only an empty yard and the blank side of the house seven meters away. An old ivy vine, going bad at the roots, climbed half way up the wall. The cold breath of autumn had stricken leaves from the plant until its branches, almost bare, hung on the bricks.
lines.zh: 苏朝窗外看去。有什么可数的？只有一个空荡荡的院子和七米外那栋房子光秃秃的侧墙。一株老常春藤，根已经开始烂了，爬到了墙的半腰。秋天的寒气吹落了它的叶子，枝条几乎光秃秃地挂在砖墙上。

lines.en: "What is it, dear?" asked Sue.
lines.zh: “怎么了，亲爱的？”苏问。

lines.en: "Six," said Johnsy, quietly. "They're falling faster now. Three days ago there were almost a hundred. It made my head hurt to count them. But now it's easy. There goes another one. There are only five left now."
lines.zh: “六，”琼西轻声说，“现在落得更快了。三天前还差不多有一百片，数得我头疼。可现在容易了。又落了一片。现在只剩五片了。”

lines.en: "Five what, dear?" asked Sue.
lines.zh: “五片什么，亲爱的？”苏问。

lines.en: "Leaves. On the plant. When the last one falls I must go, too. I've known that for three days. Didn't the doctor tell you?"
lines.zh: “叶子。藤上的叶子。最后一片落下的时候，我也该走了。这三天我一直知道。医生没告诉你吗？”

lines.en: "Oh, I never heard of such a thing," said Sue. "What have old ivy leaves to do with your getting well? And you used to love that vine. Don't be silly. Why, the doctor told me this morning that your chances for getting well real soon were -- let's see exactly what he said – he said the chances were ten to one! Try to eat some soup now. And, let me go back to my drawing, so I can sell it to the magazine and buy food and wine for us."
lines.zh: “哦，我从没听过这种怪事，”苏说，“老常春藤叶子跟你的病好不好有什么关系？你以前还很喜欢那株藤呢。别傻了。嘿，医生今天早上还跟我说，你很快好起来的机会是——我想想他到底怎么说的——他说机会是十比一！现在喝点汤吧。让我回去画画，好卖给杂志，给我们买吃的和酒。”

lines.en: "You needn't get any more wine," said Johnsy, keeping her eyes fixed out the window. "There goes another one. No, I don't want any soup. That leaves just four. I want to see the last one fall before it gets dark. Then I'll go, too."
lines.zh: “你不用再买酒了，”琼西说，眼睛一直盯着窗外，“又落了一片。不，我不想喝汤。只剩四片了。我想在天黑前看着最后一片落下。然后我也就走了。”

lines.en: "Johnsy, dear," said Sue, "will you promise me to keep your eyes closed, and not look out the window until I am done working? I must hand those drawings in by tomorrow."
lines.zh: “琼西，亲爱的，”苏说，“你能答应我闭上眼睛，在我画完之前别看窗外吗？那些画我明天必须交。”

lines.en: "Tell me as soon as you have finished," said Johnsy, closing her eyes and lying white and still as a fallen statue. "I want to see the last one fall. I'm tired of waiting. I'm tired of thinking. I want to turn loose my hold on everything, and go sailing down, down, just like one of those poor, tired leaves."
lines.zh: “你一画完就告诉我，”琼西说着闭上眼睛，躺在那儿，苍白而静止，像一尊倒下的雕像，“我想看最后一片落下。我等累了，想累了。我想放下一切，飘下去，飘下去，就像那些可怜的、疲倦的叶子一样。”

lines.en: "Try to sleep," said Sue. "I must call Mister Behrman up to be my model for my drawing of an old miner. Don't try to move until I come back."
lines.zh: “试着睡一会儿，”苏说，“我得叫贝尔曼先生上来，给我画老矿工当模特。我回来之前别乱动。”

lines.en: Old Behrman was a painter who lived on the ground floor of the apartment building. Behrman was a failure in art. For years, he had always been planning to paint a work of art, but had never yet begun it. He earned a little money by serving as a model to artists who could not pay for a professional model. He was a fierce, little, old man who protected the two young women in the studio apartment above him.
lines.zh: 老贝尔曼是个画家，住在这栋公寓楼的一楼。贝尔曼在艺术上是个失败者。多年来，他一直打算画一幅杰作，却从没动笔。他给请不起专业模特的画家当模特，挣一点钱。他是个脾气暴躁的小老头，一直护着楼上画室里的这两个年轻姑娘。

lines.en: Sue found Behrman in his room. In one area was a blank canvas that had been waiting twenty-five years for the first line of paint. Sue told him about Johnsy and how she feared that her friend would float away like a leaf.
lines.zh: 苏在贝尔曼的房间找到了他。屋子一角放着一块空白画布，二十五年来一直在等着落下第一笔。苏跟他讲了琼西的事，说她怕自己的朋友会像一片叶子一样飘走。

lines.en: Old Behrman was angered at such an idea. "Are there people in the world with the foolishness to die because leaves drop off a vine? Why do you let that silly business come in her brain?"
lines.zh: 老贝尔曼听到这种想法很生气。“世上竟有这么傻的人，因为藤上的叶子掉了就要死？你怎么能让这种蠢念头钻进她脑子里？”

lines.en: "She is very sick and weak," said Sue, "and the disease has left her mind full of strange ideas."
lines.zh: “她病得很重，很虚弱，”苏说，“这病让她脑子里满是奇怪的念头。”

lines.en: "This is not any place in which one so good as Miss Johnsy shall lie sick," yelled Behrman. "Some day I will paint a masterpiece, and we shall all go away."
lines.zh: “像琼西小姐这么好的人，不该躺在这种地方生病！”贝尔曼嚷道，“总有一天我要画一幅杰作，然后我们全都搬走。”

lines.en: Johnsy was sleeping when they went upstairs. Sue pulled the shade down to cover the window. She and Behrman went into the other room. They looked out a window fearfully at the ivy vine. Then they looked at each other without speaking. A cold rain was falling, mixed with snow. Behrman sat and posed as the miner.
lines.zh: 他们上楼时，琼西睡着了。苏拉下窗帘遮住窗户。她和贝尔曼走进另一个房间，提心吊胆地从窗口望着那株常春藤，然后默默地对视了一眼。冰冷的雨夹着雪落下来。贝尔曼坐下来，摆出矿工的姿势。

lines.en: The next morning, Sue awoke after an hour's sleep. She found Johnsy with wide-open eyes staring at the covered window.
lines.zh: 第二天早上，苏只睡了一个小时就醒了。她发现琼西睁大眼睛，盯着拉下的窗帘。

lines.en: "Pull up the shade; I want to see," she ordered, quietly.
lines.zh: “把窗帘拉起来，我要看。”她轻声命令道。

lines.en: Sue obeyed.
lines.zh: 苏照做了。

lines.en: After the beating rain and fierce wind that blew through the night, there yet stood against the wall one ivy leaf. It was the last one on the vine. It was still dark green at the center. But its edges were colored with the yellow. It hung bravely from the branch about seven meters above the ground.
lines.zh: 经过一整夜的暴雨和狂风，墙上竟然还挂着一片常春藤叶子。那是藤上的最后一片。叶子中间还是深绿色的，边缘已经泛黄。它勇敢地挂在离地大约七米的枝条上。

lines.en: "It is the last one," said Johnsy. "I thought it would surely fall during the night. I heard the wind. It will fall today and I shall die at the same time."
lines.zh: “这是最后一片了，”琼西说，“我以为它夜里肯定会掉的。我听到了风声。它今天会掉的，我也会同时死去。”

lines.en: "Dear, dear!" said Sue, leaning her worn face down toward the bed. "Think of me, if you won't think of yourself. What would I do?"
lines.zh: “亲爱的，亲爱的！”苏把疲惫的脸俯向床边说，“你不为自己想，也为我想想吧。我该怎么办？”

lines.en: But Johnsy did not answer.
lines.zh: 可琼西没有回答。

lines.en: The next morning, when it was light, Johnsy demanded that the window shade be raised. The ivy leaf was still there. Johnsy lay for a long time, looking at it. And then she called to Sue, who was preparing chicken soup.
lines.zh: 第二天早上，天一亮，琼西就要求把窗帘拉起来。那片常春藤叶子还在。琼西躺了很久，一直看着它。然后她叫正在熬鸡汤的苏。

lines.en: "I've been a bad girl," said Johnsy. "Something has made that last leaf stay there to show me how bad I was. It is wrong to want to die. You may bring me a little soup now."
lines.zh: “我真是个坏姑娘，”琼西说，“是有什么东西让那最后一片叶子留在那儿，让我看到自己有多坏。想死是不对的。你现在可以给我拿点汤来了。”

lines.en: An hour later she said: "Someday I hope to paint the Bay of Naples."
lines.zh: 一个小时后，她说：“我希望有一天能去画那不勒斯湾。”

lines.en: Later in the day, the doctor came, and Sue talked to him in the hallway.
lines.zh: 那天晚些时候，医生来了，苏在走廊里跟他说话。

lines.en: "Even chances," said the doctor. "With good care, you'll win. And now I must see another case I have in your building. Behrman, his name is -- some kind of an artist, I believe. Pneumonia, too. He is an old, weak man and his case is severe. There is no hope for him; but he goes to the hospital today to ease his pain."
lines.zh: “一半一半的机会了，”医生说，“好好照顾，你会赢的。现在我得去看楼里的另一个病人。他叫贝尔曼——大概是个什么画家吧。也是肺炎。他是个虚弱的老头，病得很重。他没希望了，不过今天会送他去医院，减轻点痛苦。”

lines.en: The next day, the doctor said to Sue: "She's out of danger. You won. Nutrition and care now -- that's all."
lines.zh: 第二天，医生对苏说：“她脱离危险了。你赢了。现在只需要营养和照顾——就这些。”

lines.en: Later that day, Sue came to the bed where Johnsy lay, and put one arm around her.
lines.zh: 那天晚些时候，苏来到琼西躺着的床边，伸出一只胳膊搂住她。

lines.en: "I have something to tell you, white mouse," she said. "Mister Behrman died of pneumonia today in the hospital. He was sick only two days. They found him the morning of the first day in his room downstairs helpless with pain. His shoes and clothing were completely wet and icy cold. They could not imagine where he had been on such a terrible night.
lines.zh: “我有件事要告诉你，小白鼠，”她说，“贝尔曼先生今天在医院里死于肺炎。他只病了两天。第一天早上，人们发现他在楼下的房间里，疼得动弹不得。他的鞋和衣服全都湿透了，冰冷冰冷的。他们想不出在那样可怕的夜晚，他去过哪儿。

lines.en: And then they found a lantern, still lighted. And they found a ladder that had been moved from its place. And art supplies and a painting board with green and yellow colors mixed on it.
lines.zh: 后来他们找到了一盏还亮着的灯笼，还找到一架被挪了位置的梯子，还有一些画具和一块调色板，上面调着绿色和黄色。

lines.en: And look out the window, dear, at the last ivy leaf on the wall. Didn't you wonder why it never moved when the wind blew? Ah, darling, it is Behrman's masterpiece – he painted it there the night that the last leaf fell."
lines.zh: 亲爱的，你看看窗外墙上那最后一片常春藤叶子。你没奇怪过，为什么风吹的时候它从来不动吗？啊，亲爱的，那是贝尔曼的杰作——是他在最后一片叶子落下的那个晚上画上去的。”

qs.q: What disease does Johnsy have?
qs.a: pneumonia
qs.why: "This disease, pneumonia, killed many people."

qs.q: What does Johnsy think will happen when the last leaf falls?
qs.a: She will die.
qs.why: "When the last one falls I must go, too."

qs.q: Who made the last leaf?
opts: Behrman painted it on the wall.
qs.a: Behrman painted it on the wall.
qs.why: "it is Behrman's masterpiece – he painted it there."

lessons.title: After Twenty Years
lessons.sum: 一个雨夜，纽约街头，一个从西部回来的男人在等二十年前约好的老朋友吉米。巡警和他聊了几句就走了。后来来了一个高个子男人……结局出人意料：他等的朋友早就来过了。

lines.en: The cop moved along the street, looking strong and important. This was the way he always moved. He was not thinking of how he looked. There were few people on the street to see him. It was only about ten at night, but it was cold. And there was a wind with a little rain in it.
lines.zh: 巡警沿着街道走着，看上去强壮而威严。他一向这样走路，并没在想自己看起来怎么样。街上没几个人看他。才晚上十点左右，可天很冷，还刮着夹着小雨的风。

lines.en: He stopped at doors as he walked along, trying each door to be sure that it was closed for the night. Now and then he turned and looked up and down the street. He was a fine-looking cop, watchful, guarding the peace.
lines.zh: 他一边走，一边在各家门口停下，试试每扇门，确保晚上都锁好了。他不时转身朝街道两头张望。他是个相貌堂堂的警察，警觉地守护着一方平安。

lines.en: People in this part of the city went home early. Now and then you might see the lights of a shop or of a small restaurant. But most of the doors belonged to business places that had been closed hours ago.
lines.zh: 城里这一带的人回家早。偶尔你能看到一家商店或小饭馆的灯光，不过大多数门都属于几个小时前就关门的店铺。

lines.en: Then the cop suddenly slowed his walk. Near the door of a darkened shop a man was standing. As the cop walked toward him, the man spoke quickly.
lines.zh: 这时，巡警突然放慢了脚步。一家熄了灯的商店门口站着一个男人。巡警朝他走过去时，那人赶紧开口了。

lines.en: "It's all right, officer," he said. "I'm waiting for a friend. Twenty years ago we agreed to meet here tonight. It sounds strange to you, doesn't it? I'll explain if you want to be sure that everything's all right. About twenty years ago there was a restaurant where this shop stands. 'Big Joe' Brady's restaurant."
lines.zh: “没事，警官，”他说，“我在等一个朋友。二十年前我们约好今晚在这儿见面。你听着觉得奇怪，是吧？如果你想确认没什么问题，我可以解释。大约二十年前，这家店的位置是一家饭馆——“大个子乔”布雷迪的饭馆。”

lines.en: "It was here until five years ago," said the cop.
lines.zh: “那家饭馆五年前还在这儿。”巡警说。

lines.en: The man near the door had a colorless square face with bright eyes, and a little white mark near his right eye. He had a large jewel in his necktie.
lines.zh: 门口那人有一张没有血色的方脸，眼睛很亮，右眼旁有一道小小的白疤。他的领带上别着一颗大宝石。

lines.en: "Twenty years ago tonight," said the man, "I had dinner here with Jimmy Wells. He was my best friend and the best fellow in the world. He and I grew up together here in New York, like two brothers. I was eighteen and Jimmy was twenty. The next morning I was to start for the West. I was going to find a job and make a great success. You couldn't have pulled Jimmy out of New York. He thought it was the only place on earth.
lines.zh: “二十年前的今晚，”那人说，“我和吉米·韦尔斯在这儿吃了晚饭。他是我最好的朋友，也是世上最好的家伙。我们俩在纽约一起长大，就像亲兄弟一样。那时我十八岁，吉米二十。第二天早上我就要动身去西部，去找份工作，干一番大事业。可你没法把吉米拽出纽约，他觉得这是世上唯一的好地方。

lines.en: "We agreed that night that we would meet here again in twenty years. We thought that in twenty years we would know what kind of men we were, and what future waited for us."
lines.zh: “那天晚上我们约定，二十年后再在这儿见面。我们以为二十年后，就会知道自己成了什么样的人，有什么样的前途在等着我们。”

lines.en: "It sounds interesting," said the cop. "A long time between meetings, it seems to me. Have you heard from your friend since you went West?"
lines.zh: “听起来挺有意思，”巡警说，“不过我觉得两次见面隔得也太久了。你去西部以后，有你朋友的消息吗？”

lines.en: "Yes, for a time we did write to each other," said the man. "But after a year or two, we stopped. The West is big. I moved around everywhere, and I moved quickly. But I know that Jimmy will meet me here if he can. He was as true as any man in the world. He'll never forget. I came a thousand miles to stand here tonight. But I'll be glad about that, if my old friend comes too."
lines.zh: “有，我们通过一阵子信，”那人说，“可一两年后就断了。西部太大了，我到处跑，换地方换得很快。不过我知道，只要吉米能来，他一定会来这儿见我。他是世上最讲信用的人，他绝不会忘的。我跑了一千英里来到这儿站着，只要我的老朋友也来，就值了。”

lines.en: The man waiting took out a fine watch, covered with small jewels.
lines.zh: 等人的那个男人掏出一块精致的怀表，上面镶满了小宝石。

lines.en: "Three minutes before ten," he said. "It was ten that night when we said goodbye here at the restaurant door."
lines.zh: “差三分十点，”他说，“那天晚上我们就是十点在这家饭馆门口告别的。”

lines.en: "You were successful in the West, weren't you?" asked the cop.
lines.zh: “你在西部混得不错吧？”巡警问。

lines.en: "I surely was! I hope Jimmy has done half as well. He was a slow mover. I've had to fight for my success. In New York a man doesn't change much. In the West you learn how to fight for what you get."
lines.zh: “那当然！希望吉米能有我一半好。他做事慢吞吞的。我的成功可是拼出来的。在纽约，人变化不大；在西部，你会学会怎么为自己想要的东西去拼。”

lines.en: The cop took a step or two. "I'll go on my way," he said. "I hope your friend comes all right. If he isn't here at ten, are you going to leave?"
lines.zh: 巡警走了一两步。“我得走了，”他说，“希望你的朋友会来。要是他十点没到，你就走吗？”

lines.en: "I am not!" said the other. "I'll wait half an hour, at least. If Jimmy is alive on earth, he'll be here by that time. Good night, officer."
lines.zh: “不走！”那人说，“我至少再等半个小时。只要吉米还活在世上，到那时他一定会来。晚安，警官。”

lines.en: "Good night," said the cop, and walked away, trying doors as he went.
lines.zh: “晚安。”巡警说着走开了，边走边试着推一扇扇门。

lines.en: There was now a cold rain falling and the wind was stronger. The few people walking along that street were hurrying, trying to keep warm. At the door of the shop stood the man who had come a thousand miles to meet a friend. Such a meeting could not be certain. But he waited.
lines.zh: 这时下起了冷雨，风也更大了。街上寥寥几个行人都匆匆赶路，想暖和一点。那个跑了一千英里来见朋友的男人仍站在商店门口。这样的约会并没有把握，可他还是等着。

lines.en: About twenty minutes he waited, and then a tall man in a long coat came hurrying across the street. He went directly to the waiting man.
lines.zh: 他等了大约二十分钟，一个穿长大衣的高个子男人匆匆穿过马路，径直朝等候的人走来。

lines.en: "Is that you, Bob?" he asked, doubtfully.
lines.zh: “是你吗，鲍勃？”他半信半疑地问。

lines.en: "Is that you, Jimmy Wells?" cried the man at the door.
lines.zh: “是你吗，吉米·韦尔斯？”门口的人叫道。

lines.en: The new man took the other man's hands in his. "It's Bob! It surely is. I was certain I would find you here if you were still alive. Twenty years is a long time. The old restaurant is gone, Bob. I wish it were here, so that we could have another dinner in it. Has the West been good to you?"
lines.zh: 新来的人握住对方的双手。“是鲍勃！真的是你。我就知道，只要你还活着，我一定能在这儿找到你。二十年可真久啊。老饭馆没了，鲍勃。真希望它还在，我们好再在里面吃顿晚饭。西部待你不错吧？”

lines.en: "It gave me everything I asked for. You've changed, Jimmy. I never thought you were so tall."
lines.zh: “我想要的它都给了我。你变了，吉米。我从没想过你这么高。”

lines.en: "Oh, I grew a little after I was twenty."
lines.zh: “哦，我二十岁以后又长高了一点。”

lines.en: "Are you doing well in New York, Jimmy?"
lines.zh: “你在纽约过得好吗，吉米？”

lines.en: "Well enough. I work for the city. Come on, Bob, We'll go to a place I know, and have a good long talk about old times."
lines.zh: “还过得去。我在市政府工作。走吧，鲍勃，我们去一个我知道的地方，好好聊聊过去的事。”

lines.en: The two men started along the street, arm in arm. The man from the West was beginning to tell the story of his life. The other, with his coat up to his ears, listened with interest.
lines.zh: 两人挽着胳膊沿街走去。从西部来的人开始讲他的人生故事，另一个人大衣领子竖到耳朵，饶有兴趣地听着。

lines.en: At the corner stood a shop bright with electric lights. When they came near, each turned to look at the other's face.
lines.zh: 街角有一家亮着电灯的商店。走近时，两人都转过头看对方的脸。

lines.en: The man from the West stopped suddenly and pulled his arm away. "You're not Jimmy Wells," he said. "Twenty years is a long time, but not long enough to change the shape of a man's nose."
lines.zh: 从西部来的人突然停下，把胳膊抽了回来。“你不是吉米·韦尔斯，”他说，“二十年是很久，可也没久到能改变一个人鼻子的形状。”

lines.en: "It sometimes changes a good man into a bad one," said the tall man. "You've been under arrest for ten minutes, Bob. Chicago cops thought you might be coming to New York. They told us to watch for you. Are you coming with me quietly? That's wise. But first here is something I was asked to give you. You may read it here at the window. It's from a cop named Wells."
lines.zh: “可有时候它能把一个好人变成坏人，”高个子说，“你已经被捕十分钟了，鲍勃。芝加哥警方认为你可能会来纽约，让我们留意你。你要安安静静跟我走吗？这才明智。不过先给你一样东西，是别人托我交给你的。你可以在这扇窗户边看。是一个叫韦尔斯的警察写的。”

lines.en: The man from the West opened the little piece of paper. His hand began to shake a little as he read.
lines.zh: 从西部来的人打开那张小纸条。他读着读着，手开始微微发抖。

lines.en: "Bob: I was at the place on time. I saw the face of the man wanted by Chicago cops. I didn't want to arrest you myself. So I went and got another cop and sent him to do the job.
lines.zh: “鲍勃：我准时到了约定的地方。我看到了芝加哥警方通缉的那个人的脸。我不想亲手逮捕你，所以我去找了另一个警察，派他来办这件事。

lines.en: JIMMY."
lines.zh: 吉米。”

qs.q: Why is the man waiting at the shop door?
opts: to meet a friend after twenty years
qs.a: to meet a friend after twenty years
qs.why: "Twenty years ago we agreed to meet here tonight."

qs.q: How did Bob know the tall man was not Jimmy?
qs.a: His nose was different.
qs.why: "not long enough to change the shape of a man's nose."

qs.q: Who was the first cop?
qs.a: Jimmy Wells
qs.why: "It's from a cop named Wells."

lessons.title: The Cop and the Anthem
lessons.sum: 冬天要来了，流浪汉索皮想进监狱过冬——那里有吃有住。他吃霸王餐、砸橱窗、调戏女士、偷雨伞，警察就是不抓他。最后他在教堂外听到赞美诗，决心重新做人，偏偏就在这时被警察抓走了。

lines.en: Soapy moved restlessly on his seat in Madison Square. There are certain signs to show that winter is coming. Birds begin to fly south. Women who want nice new warm coats become very kind to their husbands. And Soapy moves restlessly on his seat in the park. When you see these signs, you know that winter is near.
lines.zh: 索皮在麦迪逊广场的长椅上坐立不安。冬天快到时总有一些迹象：鸟儿开始往南飞；想要漂亮暖和新大衣的女人对丈夫变得格外温柔；而索皮在公园的长椅上坐立不安。看到这些迹象，你就知道冬天近了。

lines.en: A dead leaf fell at Soapy's feet. That was a special sign for him that winter was coming. It was time for all who lived in Madison Square to prepare.
lines.zh: 一片枯叶落在索皮脚边。对他来说，这是冬天要来的特殊信号。住在麦迪逊广场的人都该做准备了。

lines.en: Soapy's mind now realized the fact. The time had come. He had to find some way to take care of himself during the cold weather. And therefore he moved restlessly on his seat.
lines.zh: 索皮心里终于意识到了这一点：时候到了。他得想办法熬过寒冷的季节。所以他在长椅上坐立不安。

lines.en: Soapy's hopes for the winter were not very high. He was not thinking of sailing away on a ship. He was not thinking of southern skies, or of the Bay of Naples. Three months in the prison on Blackwell's Island was what he wanted. Three months of food every day and a bed every night. Three months safe from the cold north wind and safe from cops. This seemed to Soapy the most desirable thing in the world.
lines.zh: 索皮对过冬的期望并不高。他没想坐船远航，没想南方的天空，也没想那不勒斯湾。他想要的是在布莱克威尔岛的监狱里待三个月。三个月每天有饭吃、每晚有床睡；三个月躲开寒冷的北风，也躲开警察。在索皮看来，这是世上最值得向往的事。

lines.en: For years Blackwell's Island had been his winter home. Richer New Yorkers made their large plans to go to Florida or to the shore of the Mediterranean Sea each winter. Soapy made his small plans for going to the Island.
lines.zh: 多年来，布莱克威尔岛一直是他的冬季之家。有钱的纽约人每年冬天都要隆重计划去佛罗里达或地中海海边，索皮则小小地计划一下去那个岛。

lines.en: And now the time had come. Three big newspapers, some under his coat and some over his legs, had not kept him warm during the night in the park. So Soapy was thinking of the Island.
lines.zh: 现在时候到了。昨晚在公园里，三张大报纸——一些塞在外套里，一些盖在腿上——没能让他暖和起来。所以索皮想到了那个岛。

lines.en: There were places in the city where he could go and ask for food and a bed. These would be given to him. He could move from one building to another, and he would be taken care of through the winter. But he liked Blackwell's Island better.
lines.zh: 城里有一些地方，他可以去讨吃的和床位，人家也会给他。他可以从一处换到另一处，整个冬天都有人照顾。可他还是更喜欢布莱克威尔岛。

lines.en: Soapy's spirit was proud. If he went to any of these places, there were certain things he had to do. In one way or another, he would have to pay for what they gave him. They would not ask him for money. But they would make him wash his whole body. They would make him answer questions; they would want to know everything about his life. No. Prison was better than that. The prison had rules that he would have to follow. But in prison a gentleman's own life was still his own life.
lines.zh: 索皮心气很高。如果他去那些地方，就得做某些事，总要以某种方式为人家给的东西付出代价。他们不会向他要钱，但会让他把全身洗干净，会让他回答问题，什么都要打听他的生活。不，监狱比那强。监狱有规矩得遵守，可在监狱里，一位绅士自己的生活还是他自己的。

lines.en: Soapy, having decided to go to the Island, at once began to move toward his desire.
lines.zh: 索皮决定去岛上，马上就开始朝他的愿望行动。

lines.en: There were many easy ways of doing this. The most pleasant way was to go and have a good dinner at some fine restaurant. Then he would say that he had no money to pay. And then a cop would be called. It would all be done very quietly. The cop would arrest him. He would be taken to a judge. The judge would do the rest.
lines.zh: 有很多简单的办法。最愉快的一种是去一家高级餐馆好好吃一顿，然后说没钱付账。接着会有人叫警察来。一切都会安安静静地进行：警察逮捕他，把他带到法官那里，剩下的事法官会办。

lines.en: Soapy left his seat and walked out of Madison Square to the place where the great street called Broadway and Fifth Avenue meet. He went across this wide space and started north on Broadway. He stopped at a large and brightly lighted restaurant. This was where the best food and the best people in the best clothes appeared every evening.
lines.zh: 索皮离开长椅，走出麦迪逊广场，来到百老汇大街和第五大道交汇的地方。他穿过这片宽阔的地方，沿着百老汇往北走，在一家灯火辉煌的大餐馆前停下。每天晚上，最好的食物和衣着最讲究的上等人都出现在这里。

lines.en: Soapy believed that above his legs he looked all right. His face was clean. His coat was good enough. If he could get to a table, he believed that success would be his. The part of him that would be seen above the table would look all right. The waiter would bring him what he asked for.
lines.zh: 索皮觉得自己腿以上的部分还算体面。脸是干净的，外套也还过得去。只要能坐到桌边，他相信就能成功。露在桌面上的部分看起来没问题，服务员会把他点的东西端上来。

lines.en: He began thinking of what he would like to eat. In his mind he could see the whole dinner. The cost would not be too high. He did not want the restaurant people to feel any real anger. But the dinner would leave him filled and happy for the journey to his winter home.
lines.zh: 他开始想吃什么。脑子里已经能看到整顿晚餐了。价钱不会太高——他不想让餐馆的人真的大动肝火。但这顿饭能让他吃饱喝足、高高兴兴地踏上去冬季之家的旅程。

lines.en: But as Soapy put his foot inside the restaurant door, the head waiter saw his broken old shoes and torn clothes that covered his legs. Strong and ready hands turned Soapy around and moved him quietly and quickly outside again.
lines.zh: 可索皮的脚刚踏进餐馆门，领班就看到了他那双破旧的鞋和腿上破烂的裤子。几双有力而利落的手把索皮转了个身，悄无声息又飞快地把他送回了门外。

lines.en: Soapy turned off Broadway. It seemed that this easy, this most desirable way to the Island was not to be his. He must think of some other way of getting there.
lines.zh: 索皮拐离了百老汇。看来这条去岛上的轻松、最理想的路是走不通了。他得想别的办法。

lines.en: At a corner of Sixth Avenue was a shop with a wide glass window, bright with electric lights. Soapy picked up a big stone and threw it through the glass. People came running around the corner. A cop was the first among them. Soapy stood still and smiled when he saw the cop.
lines.zh: 第六大道的一个街角有家商店，宽大的玻璃橱窗亮着电灯。索皮捡起一块大石头，砸穿了玻璃。人们从街角跑过来，跑在最前面的是一个警察。索皮站着没动，看见警察就笑了。

lines.en: "Where's the man that did that?" asked the cop.
lines.zh: “干这事的人呢？”警察问。

lines.en: "Don't you think that I might have done it?" said Soapy. He was friendly and happy. What he wanted was coming toward him.
lines.zh: “你不觉得可能是我干的吗？”索皮说。他友好又开心，他想要的东西正朝他走来。

lines.en: But the cop's mind would not consider Soapy. Men who break windows do not stop there to talk to cops. They run away as fast as they can. The cop saw a man further along the street, running. He ran after him. And Soapy, sick at heart, walked slowly away. He had failed two times.
lines.zh: 可警察压根没往索皮身上想。砸窗户的人不会留下来跟警察聊天，他们会拼命逃跑。警察看到街那头有个人在跑，就追了过去。索皮心里很难受，慢慢走开了。他已经失败两次了。

lines.en: Across the street was another restaurant. It was not so fine as the one on Broadway. The people who went there were not so rich. Its food was not so good. Into this, Soapy took his old shoes and his torn clothes, and no one stopped him. He sat down at a table and was soon eating a big dinner. When he had finished, he said that he and money were strangers.
lines.zh: 街对面是另一家餐馆，没有百老汇那家高级，去的人没那么有钱，菜也没那么好。索皮穿着破鞋和破衣服走了进去，没人拦他。他在桌边坐下，很快就吃了一顿大餐。吃完后，他说自己和钱素不相识。

lines.en: "Get busy and call a cop," said Soapy. "And don't keep a gentleman waiting."
lines.zh: “快去叫警察，”索皮说，“别让一位绅士久等。”

lines.en: "No cop for you," said the waiter. He called another waiter.
lines.zh: “没警察给你叫。”服务员说。他叫来了另一个服务员。

lines.en: The two waiters threw Soapy upon his left ear on the hard street outside. He stood up slowly, one part at a time, and beat the dust from his clothes. Prison seemed only a happy dream. The Island seemed very far away. A cop who was standing near laughed and walked away.
lines.zh: 两个服务员把索皮扔到外面坚硬的街上，左耳着地。他慢慢地、一节一节地爬起来，拍掉衣服上的灰。监狱仿佛只是一个美梦，那个岛显得遥不可及。站在附近的一个警察笑了笑，走开了。

lines.en: Soapy traveled almost half a mile before he tried again. This time he felt very certain that he would be successful. A nice-looking young woman was standing before a shop window, looking at the objects inside. Very near stood a large cop.
lines.zh: 索皮走了差不多半英里才再试一次。这次他非常确定自己会成功。一位漂亮的年轻女子站在商店橱窗前看里面的东西，离她很近的地方站着一个高大的警察。

lines.en: Soapy's plan was to speak to the young woman. She seemed to be a very nice young lady, who would not want a strange man to speak to her. She would ask the cop for help. And then Soapy would be happy to feel the cop's hand on his arm. He would be on his way to the Island. He went near her. He could see that the cop was already watching him. The young woman moved away a few steps. Soapy followed. Standing beside her he said:
lines.zh: 索皮的计划是去跟这位年轻女子搭话。她看起来是位很规矩的小姐，不会愿意让陌生男人跟她说话。她会向警察求助，然后索皮就能高兴地感觉到警察的手抓住他的胳膊，他就在去岛上的路上了。他走近她，看得出警察已经在注意他了。年轻女子挪开了几步，索皮跟了过去。站在她身边，他说：

lines.en: "Good evening, Bedelia! Don't you want to come and play with me?"
lines.zh: “晚上好，贝蒂丽娅！不想跟我一起去玩玩吗？”

lines.en: The cop was still looking. The young woman had only to move her hand, and Soapy would be on his way to the place where he wanted to go. He was already thinking how warm he would be.
lines.zh: 警察还在看着。年轻女子只要动一下手，索皮就能去他想去的地方了。他已经在想自己会有多暖和了。

lines.en: The young woman turned to him. Putting out her hand, she took his arm.
lines.zh: 年轻女子转向他，伸出手挽住了他的胳膊。

lines.en: "Sure, Mike," she said joyfully, "if you'll buy me something to drink. I would have spoken to you sooner, but the cop was watching."
lines.zh: “当然好啊，迈克，”她高兴地说，“只要你请我喝一杯。我早就想跟你搭话了，可警察一直在看着。”

lines.en: With the young woman holding his arm, Soapy walked past the cop. He was filled with sadness. He was still free. Was he going to remain free forever?
lines.zh: 年轻女子挽着他的胳膊，索皮从警察身边走过，心里满是悲哀。他还是自由的。难道他要永远自由下去吗？

lines.en: At the next corner he pulled his arm away, and ran.
lines.zh: 到了下一个街角，他抽出胳膊，跑了。

lines.en: When he stopped, he was near several theaters. In this part of the city, streets are brighter and hearts are more joyful than in other parts. Women and men in rich, warm coats moved happily in the winter air.
lines.zh: 他停下来时，已经到了几家剧院附近。城里这一带的街道比别处更亮，人们的心情也比别处更快活。穿着华贵暖和大衣的男男女女在冬夜里开心地走着。

lines.en: A sudden fear caught Soapy. No cop was going to arrest him. Then he came to another cop standing in front of a big theater.
lines.zh: 索皮突然害怕起来：没有一个警察会逮捕他。这时他又走到一个站在大剧院门前的警察面前。

lines.en: He thought of something else to try.
lines.zh: 他想到了另一个办法。

lines.en: He began to shout as if he'd had too much to drink. His voice was as loud as he could make it. He danced, he cried out.
lines.zh: 他开始大喊大叫，好像喝多了一样。他扯着嗓子喊，又跳又叫。

lines.en: And the cop turned his back to Soapy, and said to a man standing near him, "It's one of those college boys. He won't hurt anything. We had orders to let them shout."
lines.zh: 可警察背对着索皮，对身边一个人说：“是那种大学生。他不会闹出什么事的。我们接到命令，让他们喊。”

lines.en: Soapy was quiet. Was no cop going to touch him? He began to think of the Island as if it were as far away as heaven. He pulled his thin coat around him. The wind was very cold.
lines.zh: 索皮安静下来了。难道没有一个警察会碰他吗？他开始觉得那个岛像天堂一样遥远。他把薄薄的外套裹紧。风很冷。

lines.en: Then he saw a man in the shop buying a newspaper. The man's umbrella stood beside the door. Soapy stepped inside the shop, took the umbrella, and walked slowly away. The man followed him quickly.
lines.zh: 这时他看见一个男人在店里买报纸，那人的雨伞靠在门边。索皮走进店里，拿起雨伞，慢慢地走开了。那人很快追了上来。

lines.en: "My umbrella," he said.
lines.zh: “我的雨伞。”他说。

lines.en: "Oh, is it?" said Soapy. "Why don't you call a cop? I took it. Your umbrella! Why don't you call a cop? There's one standing at the corner."The man walked more slowly. Soapy did the same. But he had a feeling that he was going to fail again. The cop looked at the two men.
lines.zh: “哦，是吗？”索皮说，“那你怎么不叫警察？是我拿的。你的雨伞！你怎么不叫警察？街角就站着一个。”那人放慢了脚步，索皮也一样。可他有种感觉，自己又要失败了。警察看着这两个人。

lines.en: "I — " said the umbrella man — "that is — you know how these things happen — I — if that's your umbrella I'm very sorry — I — I found it this morning in a restaurant — if you say it's yours — I hope you'll — "
lines.zh: “我——”雨伞的主人说，“就是——你知道这种事是怎么回事——我——如果那是你的雨伞，我很抱歉——我——我是今天早上在一家餐馆捡的——如果你说是你的——希望你——”

lines.en: "It's mine!" cried Soapy with anger in his voice.
lines.zh: “是我的！”索皮生气地叫道。

lines.en: The umbrella man hurried away. The cop helped a lady across the street. Soapy walked east. He threw the umbrella as far as he could throw it. He talked to himself about cops and what he thought of them. Because he wished to be arrested, they seemed to believe he was like a king, who could do no wrong. At last Soapy came to one of the quiet streets on the east side of the city. He turned here and began to walk south toward Madison Square. He was going home, although home was only a seat in the park.
lines.zh: 拿雨伞的人匆匆走了。警察扶着一位女士过马路。索皮往东走去，把雨伞扔得远远的。他嘴里念叨着警察，念叨着自己对他们的看法。正因为他想被捕，他们似乎就把他当成了一个不会犯错的国王。最后，索皮来到城东一条安静的街上。他在这里转弯，往南朝麦迪逊广场走去。他要回家了，虽然他的家只是公园里的一张长椅。

lines.en: But on a very quiet corner Soapy stopped. There was an old, old church. Through one of the colored-glass window came a soft light. Sweet music came to Soapy's ears and seemed to hold him there.
lines.zh: 可在一个非常安静的街角，索皮停住了。那里有一座古老古老的教堂。柔和的灯光从一扇彩色玻璃窗里透出来，美妙的音乐传进索皮的耳朵，仿佛把他留在了那里。

lines.en: The moon was above, peaceful and bright. There were few people passing. He could hear birds high above him.
lines.zh: 月亮高挂，宁静而明亮。行人寥寥。他能听到高处的鸟叫。

lines.en: And the anthem that came from the church held Soapy there, for he had known it well long ago. In those days his life contained such things as mothers and flowers and high hopes and friends and clean thoughts and clean clothes.
lines.zh: 教堂里传出的赞美诗把索皮定在了那里，因为很久以前他非常熟悉这首歌。那时他的生活里有母亲、鲜花、远大的希望、朋友、纯洁的思想和干净的衣服。

lines.en: Soapy's mind was ready for something like this. He had come to the old church at the right time. There was a sudden and wonderful change in his soul. He saw with sick fear how he had fallen. He saw his worthless days, his wrong desires, his dead hopes, the lost power of his mind.
lines.zh: 索皮的心正需要这样的东西。他在恰当的时候来到了这座古老的教堂。他的灵魂突然发生了奇妙的变化。他惊恐地看到自己堕落到了什么地步：他看到了自己虚度的日子、错误的欲望、死去的希望和丧失的心智。

lines.en: And also in a moment his heart answered this change in his soul. He would fight to change his life. He would pull himself up, out of the mud. He would make a man of himself again.
lines.zh: 就在这一刻，他的心也回应了灵魂的这一变化。他要奋斗，改变自己的生活。他要把自己从泥潭里拉出来，重新做一个像样的人。

lines.en: There was time. He was young enough. He would find his old purpose in life, and follow it. That sweet music had changed him. Tomorrow he would find work. A man had once offered him a job. He would find that man tomorrow. He would be somebody in the world. He would—
lines.zh: 还来得及。他还年轻。他要找回过去的人生目标，并为之努力。那美妙的音乐改变了他。明天他就去找工作。曾经有个人愿意给他一份工作，明天他就去找那个人。他要在这世上做个有出息的人。他要——

lines.en: Soapy felt a hand on his arm. He looked quickly around into the broad face of a cop.
lines.zh: 索皮感到有一只手搭在他的胳膊上。他赶紧回头，看到一张警察的宽脸。

lines.en: "What are you doing hanging around here?" asked the cop. "Nothing," said Soapy.
lines.zh: “你在这儿晃悠什么？”警察问。“没什么。”索皮说。

lines.en: "You think I believe that?" said the cop.
lines.zh: “你以为我会信？”警察说。

lines.en: Full of his new strength, Soapy began to argue. And it is not wise to argue with a New York cop.
lines.zh: 索皮满怀新生的力量，开始争辩。而跟纽约警察争辩可不是明智之举。

lines.en: "Come along," said the cop.
lines.zh: “跟我走。”警察说。

lines.en: "Three months on the Island," said the Judge to Soapy the next morning.
lines.zh: 第二天早上，法官对索皮说：“岛上三个月。”

qs.q: Why does Soapy want to go to prison?
opts: to have food and a bed for the winter
qs.a: to have food and a bed for the winter
qs.why: "Three months of food every day and a bed every night."

qs.q: What changed Soapy's mind about his life?
qs.a: music from an old church
qs.why: "That sweet music had changed him."

qs.q: What happened in the end?
opts: He was sent to the Island for three months.
qs.a: He was sent to the Island for three months.
qs.why: "Three months on the Island," said the Judge.

lessons.title: A Retrieved Reformation
lessons.sum: 开保险箱的高手吉米·瓦伦丁出狱后又干起老本行，警探本·普莱斯紧追不舍。吉米在小镇爱上了银行家的女儿，改名换姓开起鞋店，决心金盆洗手。就在婚礼前，一个小女孩被锁进了银行的保险库……

lines.en: In the prison shoe-shop, Jimmy Valentine was busily at work making shoes. A prison officer came into the shop, and led Jimmy to the prison office. There Jimmy was given an important paper. It said that he was free.
lines.zh: 在监狱的制鞋作坊里，吉米·瓦伦丁正忙着做鞋。一名狱警走进作坊，把吉米带到监狱办公室。在那里，吉米拿到了一份重要文件，上面写着他自由了。

lines.en: Jimmy took the paper without showing much pleasure or interest. He had been sent to prison to stay for four years. He had been there for ten months. But he had expected to stay only three months. Jimmy Valentine had many friends outside the prison. A man with so many friends does not expect to stay in prison long.
lines.zh: 吉米接过文件，没露出多少高兴或兴趣。他被判了四年，已经关了十个月。不过他原本以为只会待三个月。吉米·瓦伦丁在狱外有很多朋友，朋友这么多的人，不会指望在牢里待太久。

lines.en: "Valentine," said the chief prison officer, "you'll go out tomorrow morning. This is your chance. Make a man of yourself. You're not a bad fellow at heart. Stop breaking safes open, and live a better life."
lines.zh: “瓦伦丁，”监狱长说，“你明天早上就出去了。这是你的机会。做个像样的人吧。你本性不坏。别再撬保险箱了，好好过日子。”

lines.en: "Me?" said Jimmy in surprise. "I never broke open a safe in my life."
lines.zh: “我？”吉米吃惊地说，“我这辈子从没撬过保险箱。”

lines.en: "Oh, no," the chief prison officer laughed. "Never. Let's see. How did you happen to get sent to prison for opening that safe in Springfield? Was it because you didn't want to tell where you really were? Perhaps because you were with some lady, and you didn't want to tell her name? Or was it because the judge didn't like you? You men always have a reason like that. You never go to prison because you broke open a safe."
lines.zh: “哦，没有，”监狱长笑了，“从来没有。我想想，你怎么会因为撬了斯普林菲尔德那个保险箱进了监狱呢？是因为你不想说出你当时真正在哪儿？也许你跟哪位女士在一起，不想说出她的名字？还是因为法官看你不顺眼？你们这些人总有这样的理由，从来不是因为撬了保险箱才进监狱的。”

lines.en: "Me?" Jimmy said. His face still showed surprise. "I was never in Springfield in my life."
lines.zh: “我？”吉米说，脸上还是一副吃惊的样子，“我这辈子从没去过斯普林菲尔德。”

lines.en: "Take him away," said the chief prison officer. "Get him the clothes he needs for going outside. Bring him here again at seven in the morning. And think about what I said, Valentine."
lines.zh: “带他下去，”监狱长说，“给他准备出狱穿的衣服。明早七点再带他来。好好想想我说的话，瓦伦丁。”

lines.en: At a quarter past seven on the next morning, Jimmy stood again in the office. He had on some new clothes that did not fit him, and a pair of new shoes that hurt his feet. These are the usual clothes given to a prisoner when he leaves the prison.
lines.zh: 第二天早上七点一刻，吉米又站在了办公室里。他穿着一身不合身的新衣服和一双夹脚的新鞋。犯人出狱时通常就发这样的衣服。

lines.en: Next they gave him money to pay for his trip on a train to the city near the prison. They gave him five dollars more. The five dollars were supposed to help him become a better man.
lines.zh: 接着他们给了他坐火车去监狱附近那座城市的路费，又多给了五美元。这五美元据说是用来帮他重新做人的。

lines.en: Then the chief prison officer put out his hand for a handshake. That was the end of Valentine, Prisoner 9762. Mr. James Valentine walked out into the sunshine.
lines.zh: 然后监狱长伸出手跟他握了握。犯人瓦伦丁，编号 9762，就此结束了。詹姆斯·瓦伦丁先生走进了阳光里。

lines.en: He did not listen to the song of the birds or look at the green trees or smell the flowers. He went straight to a restaurant. There he tasted the first sweet joys of being free. He had a good dinner. After that he went to the train station. He gave some money to a blind man who sat there, asking for money, and then he got on the train.
lines.zh: 他没听鸟叫，没看绿树，也没闻花香。他直奔一家餐馆，在那里尝到了自由的第一份甜蜜。他美美地吃了一顿，然后去了火车站。他给坐在那儿乞讨的一个盲人一些钱，就上了火车。

lines.en: Three hours later he got off the train in a small town. Here he went to the restaurant of Mike Dolan.
lines.zh: 三个小时后，他在一个小镇下了车，来到迈克·多兰的饭馆。

lines.en: Mike Dolan was alone there. After shaking hands he said, "I'm sorry we couldn't do it sooner, Jimmy my boy. But there was that safe in Springfield, too. It wasn't easy. Feeling all right?"
lines.zh: 迈克·多兰一个人在店里。握完手，他说：“抱歉没能早点把你弄出来，吉米老弟。可还有斯普林菲尔德那个保险箱的事，不容易啊。感觉还好吧？”

lines.en: "Fine," said Jimmy. "Is my room waiting for me?"
lines.zh: “很好，”吉米说，“我的房间还给我留着吗？”

lines.en: He went up and opened the door of a room at the back of the house. Everything was as he had left it. It was here they had found Jimmy, when they took him to prison. There on the floor was a small piece of cloth. It had been torn from the coat of the cop, as Jimmy was fighting to escape.
lines.zh: 他上楼打开屋子后面一个房间的门。一切都和他离开时一样。当初人们就是在这儿抓到吉米、把他送进监狱的。地上还有一小块布，是吉米拼命逃跑时从警察外套上扯下来的。

lines.en: There was a bed against the wall. Jimmy pulled the bed toward the middle of the room. The wall behind it looked like any wall, but now Jimmy found and opened a small door in it. From this opening he pulled out a dust-covered bag.
lines.zh: 墙边有一张床。吉米把床拉到屋子中间。床后的墙看上去和普通的墙一样，但吉米找到墙上一扇小门，把它打开，从洞里拉出一个满是灰尘的包。

lines.en: He opened this and looked lovingly at the tools for breaking open a safe. No finer tools could be found any place. They were complete; everything needed was here. They had been made of a special material, in the necessary sizes and shapes. Jimmy had planned them himself, and he was very proud of them.
lines.zh: 他打开包，深情地看着里面撬保险箱的工具。哪儿也找不到比这更好的工具了。工具很齐全，需要的东西都在这儿。它们是用特殊材料做的，尺寸和形状都恰到好处。这些都是吉米自己设计的，他很为它们自豪。

lines.en: It had cost him over nine hundred dollars to have these tools made at a place where they make such things for men who work at the job of safe-breaking.
lines.zh: 他花了九百多美元，在一个专为干撬保险箱这一行的人做这种东西的地方把它们做了出来。

lines.en: In half an hour Jimmy went downstairs and through the restaurant. He was now dressed in good clothes that fitted him well. He carried his dusted and cleaned bag.
lines.zh: 半小时后，吉米下楼穿过饭馆。他现在穿着一身合身的好衣服，提着那个掸干净的包。

lines.en: "Do you have everything planned?" asked Mike Dolan.
lines.zh: “都计划好了？”迈克·多兰问。

lines.en: "Me?" asked Jimmy as if surprised. "I don't understand. I work for the New York Famous Bread and Cake Makers Company. And I sell the best bread and cake in the country."
lines.zh: “我？”吉米好像很惊讶地问，“我不明白。我在纽约著名面包蛋糕公司工作，卖的是全国最好的面包和蛋糕。”

lines.en: Mike enjoyed these words so much that Jimmy had to take a drink with him. Jimmy had some milk. He never drank anything stronger.
lines.zh: 迈克太喜欢这番话了，吉米只好陪他喝一杯。吉米喝了点牛奶，他从不喝比这更烈的东西。

lines.en: A week after Valentine, 9762, left the prison, a safe was broken open in Richmond, Indiana. No one knew who did it. Eight hundred dollars were taken.
lines.zh: 瓦伦丁，9762 号，出狱一星期后，印第安纳州里士满的一个保险箱被撬开了。没人知道是谁干的。八百美元被偷走了。

lines.en: Two weeks after that, a safe in Logansport was opened. It was a new kind of safe; it had been made, they said, so strong that no one could break it open. But someone did, and took fifteen hundred dollars.
lines.zh: 两星期后，洛根斯波特的一个保险箱被打开了。那是一种新型保险箱，据说坚固得谁也撬不开。可还是有人撬开了，拿走了一千五百美元。

lines.en: Then a safe in Jefferson City was opened. Five thousand dollars were taken. This loss was a big one. Ben Price was a cop who worked on such important matters, and now he began to work on this.
lines.zh: 接着，杰斐逊城的一个保险箱被打开了，五千美元被盗。这次损失很大。本·普莱斯是专办这类大案的警探，现在他开始查这个案子了。

lines.en: He went to Richmond, Indiana, and to Logansport, to see how the safe-breaking had been done in those places. He was heard to say: "I can see that Jim Valentine has been here. He is in business again. Look at the way he opened this one. Everything easy, everything clean. He is the only man who has the tools to do it. And he is the only man who knows how to use tools like this. Yes, I want Mr. Valentine. Next time he goes to prison, he's going to stay there until his time is finished."
lines.zh: 他去了印第安纳州里士满和洛根斯波特，查看那里的保险箱是怎么被撬的。有人听到他说：“我看得出吉姆·瓦伦丁来过这儿。他又重操旧业了。瞧他开这个保险箱的手法，一切都那么轻松、那么干净。只有他有这样的工具，也只有他知道怎么用这样的工具。没错，我要抓瓦伦丁先生。下次他进监狱，就得把刑期坐满。”

lines.en: Ben Price knew how Jimmy worked. Jimmy would go from one city to another far away. He always worked alone. He always left quickly when he was finished. He enjoyed being with nice people. For all these reasons, it was not easy to catch Mr. Valentine.
lines.zh: 本·普莱斯了解吉米的作案方式。吉米会从一座城市跑到很远的另一座城市。他总是单干，干完总是马上离开。他喜欢和体面人来往。因为这些原因，要抓到瓦伦丁先生可不容易。

lines.en: People with safes full of money were glad to hear that Ben Price was at work trying to catch Mr. Valentine.
lines.zh: 保险箱里装满钱的人听说本·普莱斯正在设法抓瓦伦丁先生，都很高兴。

lines.en: One afternoon Jimmy Valentine and his bag arrived in a small town named Elmore. Jimmy, looking as young as a college boy, walked down the street toward the hotel.
lines.zh: 一天下午，吉米·瓦伦丁带着他的包来到一个叫埃尔莫尔的小镇。吉米看上去像个大学生一样年轻，他沿街朝旅馆走去。

lines.en: A young lady walked across the street, passed him at the corner, and entered a door. Over the door was the sign, "The Elmore Bank." Jimmy Valentine looked into her eyes, forgetting at once what he was. He became another man. She looked away, and brighter color came into her face. Young men like Jimmy did not appear often in Elmore.
lines.zh: 一位年轻小姐穿过马路，在街角和他擦肩而过，走进一扇门。门上的招牌写着“埃尔莫尔银行”。吉米·瓦伦丁望着她的眼睛，一下子忘了自己是谁，变成了另一个人。她移开目光，脸上泛起红晕。像吉米这样的年轻人在埃尔莫尔可不常见。

lines.en: Jimmy saw a boy near the bank door, and began to ask questions about the town. After a time the young lady came out and went on her way. She seemed not to see Jimmy as she passed him
lines.zh: 吉米看到银行门口有个男孩，就向他打听镇上的事。过了一会儿，那位年轻小姐出来走了。她从吉米身边经过时，好像没看见他。

lines.en: "Isn't that young lady Polly Simpson?" asked Jimmy.
lines.zh: “那位小姐是波莉·辛普森吗？”吉米问。

lines.en: "No," said the boy. "She's Annabel Adams. Her father owns this bank."
lines.zh: “不是，”男孩说，“她是安娜贝尔·亚当斯。她爸爸是这家银行的老板。”
