lines.en: Jimmy went to the hotel, where he said his name was Ralph D. Spencer. He got a room there. He told the hotel man he had come to Elmore to go into business. How was the shoe business? Was there already a good shoe-shop?
lines.zh: 吉米去了旅馆，说他叫拉尔夫·D·斯宾塞，在那儿开了个房间。他告诉旅馆老板，他来埃尔莫尔是想做生意。鞋生意怎么样？镇上已经有好的鞋店了吗？

lines.en: The man thought that Jimmy's clothes and manners were fine. He was happy to talk to him.
lines.zh: 老板觉得吉米衣着体面、举止得体，很乐意跟他聊。

lines.en: Yes, Elmore needed a good shoe-shop. There was no shop that sold just shoes. Shoes were sold in the big shops that sold everything. All business in Elmore was good. He hoped Mr. Spencer would decide to stay in Elmore. It was a pleasant town to live in and the people were friendly.
lines.zh: 是的，埃尔莫尔需要一家好鞋店。镇上没有专门卖鞋的店，鞋都在什么都卖的大商店里卖。埃尔莫尔的生意都很好做。他希望斯宾塞先生决定留在埃尔莫尔。这是个住着很舒服的小镇，人们也很友好。

lines.en: Mr. Spencer said he would stay in the town a few days and learn something about it. No, he said, he himself would carry his bag up to his room. He didn't want a boy to take it. It was very heavy.
lines.zh: 斯宾塞先生说他会在镇上住几天，了解了解情况。不，他说，他要自己把包提上楼，不用伙计帮忙。包很重。

lines.en: Mr. Ralph Spencer remained in Elmore. He started a shoe-shop. Business was good.
lines.zh: 拉尔夫·斯宾塞先生留在了埃尔莫尔。他开了一家鞋店，生意很好。

lines.en: Also he made many friends. And he was successful with the wish of his heart. He met Annabel Adams. He liked her better every day.
lines.zh: 他还交了很多朋友，心里的愿望也实现了：他认识了安娜贝尔·亚当斯，一天比一天更喜欢她。

lines.en: At the end of a year everyone in Elmore liked Mr. Ralph Spencer. His shoe-shop was doing very good business. And he and Annabel were going to be married in two weeks. Mr. Adams, the small-town banker, liked Spencer. Annabel was very proud of him. He seemed already to belong to the Adams family.
lines.zh: 一年后，埃尔莫尔人人都喜欢拉尔夫·斯宾塞先生。他的鞋店生意兴隆，他和安娜贝尔再过两星期就要结婚了。小镇银行家亚当斯先生很喜欢斯宾塞，安娜贝尔也为他自豪。他好像已经是亚当斯家的一员了。

lines.en: One day Jimmy sat down in his room to write this letter, which he sent to one of his old friends:
lines.zh: 一天，吉米坐在房间里写了这封信，寄给他的一个老朋友：

lines.en: Dear Old Friend: I want you to meet me at Sullivan's place next week, on the evening of the 10th. I want to give you my tools. I know you'll be glad to have them. You couldn't buy them for a thousand dollars. I finished with the old business—a year ago. I have a nice shop. I'm living a better life, and I'm going to marry the best girl on earth two weeks from now. It's the only life—I wouldn't ever again touch another man's money. After I marry, I'm going to go further west, where I'll never see anyone who knew me in my old life. I tell you, she's a wonderful girl. She trusts me.
lines.zh: 亲爱的老朋友：下星期 10 号晚上，请到沙利文那儿跟我见面。我想把我的工具送给你。我知道你会很高兴得到它们，一千美元都买不到。我已经洗手不干那一行了——一年前就不干了。我有一家不错的店，过着更好的生活，两星期后我就要娶世上最好的姑娘了。这才是唯一的活法——我再也不会碰别人的一分钱了。结婚以后，我要搬到更西边去，在那里我再也不会碰到认识我过去的人。告诉你，她是个了不起的姑娘。她信任我。

lines.en: Your old friend, Jimmy.
lines.zh: 你的老朋友，吉米。

lines.en: On the Monday night after Jimmy sent this letter, Ben Price arrived quietly in Elmore. He moved slowly about the town in his quiet way, and he learned all that he wanted to know. Standing inside a shop, he watched Ralph D. Spencer walk by.
lines.zh: 吉米寄出这封信后的那个星期一晚上，本·普莱斯悄悄来到了埃尔莫尔。他用他那种不声不响的方式在镇上慢慢转，打听到了他想知道的一切。他站在一家店里，看着拉尔夫·D·斯宾塞从门前走过。

lines.en: "You're going to marry the banker's daughter, are you, Jimmy?" said Ben to himself. "I don't feel sure about that!"
lines.zh: “你要娶银行家的女儿了，是吗，吉米？”本自言自语道，“那可说不准！”

lines.en: The next morning Jimmy was at the Adams home. He was going to a nearby city that day to buy new clothes for the wedding. He was also going to buy a gift for Annabel. It would be his first trip out of Elmore. It was more than a year now since he had done any safe-breaking.
lines.zh: 第二天早上，吉米在亚当斯家。那天他要去附近一座城市买结婚穿的新衣服，还要给安娜贝尔买件礼物。这将是他第一次离开埃尔莫尔。他已经一年多没撬过保险箱了。

lines.en: Most of the Adams family went to the bank together that morning. There were Mr. Adams, Annabel, Jimmy, and Annabel's married sister with her two little girls, aged five and nine. They passed Jimmy's hotel, and Jimmy ran up to his room and brought along his bag. Then they went to the bank.
lines.zh: 那天早上，亚当斯家的大部分人一起去了银行：亚当斯先生、安娜贝尔、吉米，还有安娜贝尔已婚的姐姐和她的两个小女儿，一个五岁，一个九岁。他们经过吉米住的旅馆时，吉米跑上楼把他的包拿了下来。然后他们去了银行。

lines.en: All went inside—Jimmy, too, for he was one of the family. Everyone in the bank was glad to see the good-looking, nice young man who was going to marry Annabel. Jimmy put down his bag.
lines.zh: 大家都进去了——吉米也进去了，因为他已经是一家人了。银行里每个人都很高兴见到这位要娶安娜贝尔的英俊和善的年轻人。吉米把包放下。

lines.en: Annabel, laughing, put Jimmy's hat on her head and picked up the bag.
lines.zh: 安娜贝尔笑着把吉米的帽子戴到自己头上，拎起了那个包。

lines.en: "How do I look?" she asked. "Ralph, how heavy this bag is! It feels full of gold."
lines.zh: “我看起来怎么样？”她问，“拉尔夫，这包好重啊！感觉里面装满了金子。”

lines.en: "It's full of some things I don't need in my shop," Jimmy said. "I'm taking them to the city, to the place where they came from. That saves me the cost of sending them. I'm going to be a married man. I must learn to save money."
lines.zh: “里面装的是我店里用不着的一些东西，”吉米说，“我要把它们带到城里，送回原来的地方。这样能省下运费。我要成家了，得学会省钱。”

lines.en: The Elmore bank had a new safe. Mr. Adams was very proud of it, and he wanted everyone to see it. It was as large as a small room, and it had a very special door. The door was controlled by a clock. Using the clock, the banker planned the time when the door should open. At other times no one, not even the banker himself, could open it. He explained about it to Mr. Spencer. Mr. Spencer seemed interested but he did not seem to understand very easily. The two children, May and Agatha, enjoyed seeing the shining heavy door, with all its special parts.
lines.zh: 埃尔莫尔银行有一个新保险库。亚当斯先生很为它自豪，想让每个人都看看。它有一间小屋那么大，还有一扇很特别的门。门由一个时钟控制：银行家用时钟设定开门的时间，其他时候谁也打不开，连银行家本人也不行。他向斯宾塞先生解释这一切。斯宾塞先生好像很感兴趣，但似乎不太容易听懂。两个孩子梅和阿加莎很喜欢看那扇闪闪发亮、装满特殊零件的厚重大门。

lines.en: While they were busy like this, Ben Price entered the bank and looked around. He told a young man who worked there that he had not come on business; he was waiting for a man.
lines.zh: 他们正忙着看的时候，本·普莱斯走进银行四处张望。他对银行里一个年轻职员说，他不是来办业务的，他在等一个人。

lines.en: Suddenly there was a cry from the women. They had not been watching the children. May, the nine-year-old girl, had playfully but firmly closed the door of the safe. And Agatha was inside.
lines.zh: 突然，女人们发出一声尖叫。她们刚才没看着孩子。九岁的梅闹着玩，却牢牢地关上了保险库的门，而阿加莎在里面。

lines.en: The old banker tried to open the door. He pulled at it for a moment. "The door can't be opened," he cried. "And the clock—I hadn't started it yet."
lines.zh: 老银行家想打开门，拉了一会儿。“门打不开了，”他叫道，“而且时钟——我还没设定呢。”

lines.en: Agatha's mother cried out again.
lines.zh: 阿加莎的妈妈又尖叫起来。

lines.en: "Quiet!" said Mr. Adams, raising a shaking hand. "All be quiet for a moment. Agatha!" he called as loudly as he could. "Listen to me." They could hear, but not clearly, the sound of the child's voice. In the darkness inside the safe, she was wild with fear.
lines.zh: “安静！”亚当斯先生举起一只颤抖的手说，“大家安静一下。阿加莎！”他用最大的声音喊道，“听我说。”他们能听到孩子的声音，但听不清楚。在保险库里的黑暗中，她吓坏了。

lines.en: "My baby!" her mother cried. "She will die of fear! Open the door! Break it open! Can't you men do something?"
lines.zh: “我的孩子！”她妈妈哭喊道，“她会吓死的！把门打开！把它砸开！你们男人就不能想想办法吗？”

lines.en: "There isn't a man nearer than the city who can open that door," said Mr. Adams, in a shaking voice. "My God! Spencer, what shall we do? That child—she can't live long in there. There isn't enough air. And the fear will kill her."
lines.zh: “离这儿最近能打开那扇门的人在城里，”亚当斯先生声音发抖地说，“我的上帝！斯宾塞，我们怎么办？那孩子——她在里面活不了多久。里面空气不够。恐惧也会要了她的命。”

lines.en: Agatha's mother, wild too now, beat on the door with her hands. Annabel turned to Jimmy, her large eyes full of pain, but with some hope, too. A woman thinks that the man she loves can somehow do anything.
lines.zh: 阿加莎的妈妈也发了狂，用手拍打着门。安娜贝尔转向吉米，大眼睛里满是痛苦，但也带着一丝希望。女人总觉得自己爱的男人无所不能。

lines.en: "Can't you do something, Ralph? Try, won't you?"
lines.zh: “你就不能想想办法吗，拉尔夫？试试，好吗？”

lines.en: He looked at her with a strange soft smile on his lips and in his eyes.
lines.zh: 他看着她，嘴角和眼里带着一种奇怪而温柔的笑。

lines.en: "Annabel," he said, "give me that flower you are wearing, will you?"
lines.zh: “安娜贝尔，”他说，“把你戴的那朵花给我，好吗？”

lines.en: She could not believe that she had really heard him. But she put the flower in his hand. Jimmy took it and put it where he could not lose it. Then he pulled off his coat. With that act, Ralph D. Spencer passed away and Jimmy Valentine took his place.
lines.zh: 她不敢相信自己真的听到了这句话。可她还是把花放到了他手里。吉米接过花，放在丢不了的地方。然后他脱下外套。这个动作一做，拉尔夫·D·斯宾塞就消失了，取而代之的是吉米·瓦伦丁。

lines.en: "Stand away from the door, all of you," he commanded.
lines.zh: “都离门远点。”他命令道。

lines.en: He put his bag on the table, and opened it flat. From that time on, he seemed not to know that anyone else was near. Quickly he laid the shining strange tools on the table. The others watched as if they had lost the power to move.
lines.zh: 他把包放在桌上，摊开。从这时起，他好像不知道身边还有别人。他飞快地把那些闪亮的奇怪工具摆在桌上。其他人看着，好像失去了动弹的能力。

lines.en: In a minute Jimmy was at work on the door. In ten minutes— faster than he had ever done it before—he had the door open.
lines.zh: 一分钟后，吉米已经在开门了。十分钟后——比他以往任何一次都快——他把门打开了。

lines.en: Agatha was taken into her mother's arms.
lines.zh: 阿加莎被抱进了妈妈的怀里。

lines.en: Jimmy Valentine put on his coat, picked up the flower and walked toward the front door. As he went he thought he heard a voice call, "Ralph!" He did not stop.
lines.zh: 吉米·瓦伦丁穿上外套，拿起那朵花，朝前门走去。走的时候，他好像听到有个声音在喊“拉尔夫！”他没有停下。

lines.en: At the door a big man stood in his way.
lines.zh: 门口，一个大个子挡住了他的路。

lines.en: "Hello, Ben!" said Jimmy, still with his strange smile. "You're here at last, are you? Let's go. I don't care, now."
lines.zh: “你好，本！”吉米说，脸上仍带着那种奇怪的笑，“你终于来了，是吧？走吧。现在我无所谓了。”

lines.en: And then Ben Price acted rather strangely.
lines.zh: 接着，本·普莱斯的举动相当奇怪。

lines.en: "I guess you're wrong about this, Mr. Spencer," he said. "I don't believe I know you, do I?"
lines.zh: “我想你弄错了，斯宾塞先生，”他说，“我不认识你，对吧？”

lines.en: And Ben Price turned and walked slowly down the street.
lines.zh: 本·普莱斯转过身，沿着街慢慢走了。

qs.q: What did Jimmy do before prison?
qs.a: He broke open safes.
qs.why: "Stop breaking safes open."

qs.q: Why did Jimmy stay in Elmore?
opts: He fell in love with Annabel.
He wanted to rob the bank.
qs.a: He fell in love with Annabel.
qs.why: "He met Annabel Adams. He liked her better every day."

qs.q: Why didn't Ben Price arrest Jimmy?
opts: Jimmy had saved the child and changed his life.
qs.a: Jimmy had saved the child and changed his life.
qs.why: "I don't believe I know you, do I?"

lessons.title: Two Thanksgiving Day Gentlemen
lessons.sum: 连续九年的感恩节，一位老绅士都在纽约联合广场找到流浪汉“胖子皮特”，请他吃一顿大餐，想把这变成一个美国传统。今年皮特刚被别人请吃得撑不动了，却仍不忍心拒绝……而老绅士自己也有一个秘密。

lines.en: There is one day that is ours. There is one day when all Americans go back to the old home and eat a big dinner. Bless the day. The President gives it to us every year.
lines.zh: 有一天是属于我们的。在这一天，所有美国人都回到老家，吃一顿丰盛的晚餐。为这一天祝福吧。总统每年都把这一天给我们。

lines.en: Sometimes he talks about the people who had the first Thanksgiving. They were the Puritans. They were some people who landed on our Atlantic shore. We don't really remember much about them.
lines.zh: 有时总统会讲起过第一个感恩节的人们——清教徒。他们是在我们大西洋海岸登陆的一群人。其实我们对他们记得不多。

lines.en: But those people ate a large bird called turkey on the first Thanksgiving Day. So we have turkey for Thanksgiving dinner, if we have enough money to buy turkey. That is a tradition.
lines.zh: 不过那些人在第一个感恩节吃了一种叫火鸡的大鸟。所以感恩节晚餐我们吃火鸡——如果我们有钱买火鸡的话。这是一个传统。

lines.en: Yes. Thanksgiving Day is the one day of the year that is purely American. And now here is the story to prove to you that we have old traditions in this new country. They are growing older more quickly than traditions in old countries. That is because we are so young and full of life. We do everything quickly.
lines.zh: 是的，感恩节是一年中唯一纯粹属于美国的节日。现在就来讲个故事，向你证明在这个新国家里我们也有古老的传统。它们比老国家的传统老得更快，因为我们是这样年轻、充满活力，做什么都快。

lines.en: Stuffy Pete sat down on a seat in the New York City park named Union Square. It was the third seat to the right as you enter Union Square from the east.
lines.zh: 胖子皮特在纽约一个叫联合广场的公园里坐了下来。从东边进联合广场，右手第三张长椅就是。

lines.en: Every Thanksgiving for nine years he had sat down there at one in the afternoon. Every time, things had happened to him. They were wonderful things. They made his heart feel full of joy—and they filled another part of him, too. They filled the part below his heart.
lines.zh: 九年来的每个感恩节，他都在下午一点坐在那里。每一次，他都会遇到一些事——美妙的事。它们让他心里充满喜悦——也填满了他身上的另一个部位，就在心脏下面。

lines.en: On those other Thanksgiving Days he had been hungry. (It is a strange thing. There are rich people who wish to help the poor. But many of them seem to think that the poor are hungry only on Thanksgiving Day.)
lines.zh: 以前那些感恩节，他都是饿着的。（这事很奇怪。有些富人想帮助穷人，可他们中很多人似乎以为穷人只在感恩节才挨饿。）

lines.en: But today Pete was not hungry. He had come from a dinner so big that he had almost no power to move. His light green eyes looked out from a gray face on which there was still a little food. His breath was short. His body had suddenly become too big for his clothes; it seemed ready to break out of them. They were torn. You could see his skin through a hole in the front of his shirt. But the cold wind, with snow in it, felt pleasantly cool to him.
lines.zh: 可今天皮特不饿。他刚吃完一顿大餐，撑得几乎动不了。他那双浅绿色的眼睛从一张灰扑扑的脸上往外看，脸上还沾着一点食物。他喘不过气来。他的身体突然变得比衣服还大，好像随时要把衣服撑破。衣服已经破了，从衬衫前面的一个洞里能看到他的皮肤。可夹着雪的寒风吹在他身上，倒觉得凉爽舒服。

lines.en: For Stuffy Pete was overheated with the warmth of all he had had to eat. The dinner had been much too big. It seemed to him that his dinner had included all the turkey and all the other food in the whole world.
lines.zh: 因为胖子皮特吃下去的东西让他浑身燥热。那顿饭实在太大了。他觉得自己好像把全世界的火鸡和别的食物都吃下去了。

lines.en: So he sat, very, very full. He looked out at the world without interest, as if it could never offer him anything more.
lines.zh: 于是他坐在那儿，撑得不得了。他毫无兴趣地望着这个世界，好像世界再也给不了他任何东西了。

lines.en: The dinner had not been expected.
lines.zh: 这顿饭是意外得来的。

lines.en: He had been passing a large house near the beginning of that great broad street called Fifth Avenue. It was the home of two old ladies of an old family. These two old ladies had a deep love of traditions. There were certain things they always did. On Thanksgiving Day at noon they always sent a servant to stand at the door. There he waited for the first hungry person who walked by. The servant had orders to bring that person into the house and feed him until he could eat no more. Stuffy Pete happened to pass by on his way to the park. The servant had gathered him in. Tradition had been followed.
lines.zh: 他刚才路过那条宽阔的第五大道开头附近的一栋大房子。那是一个老家族的两位老太太的家。这两位老太太非常热爱传统，有些事情她们每年都做：感恩节中午，她们总是派一个仆人站在门口，等第一个路过的饥饿的人。仆人奉命把那人请进屋，让他吃到吃不下为止。胖子皮特去公园时正好路过，就被仆人请了进去。传统得到了遵守。

lines.en: Stuffy Pete sat in the park looking straight before him for ten minutes. Then he felt a desire to look in another direction. With a very great effort, he moved his head slowly to the left.
lines.zh: 胖子皮特坐在公园里，直直地盯着前方看了十分钟。然后他想往另一个方向看看。他费了好大的劲，才把头慢慢转向左边。

lines.en: Then his eyes grew wider and his breath stopped. His feet in their torn shoes at the ends of his short legs moved about on the ground.
lines.zh: 接着他的眼睛瞪大了，呼吸也停住了。他那两条短腿末端穿着破鞋的脚在地上挪来挪去。

lines.en: For the Old Gentleman was coming across Fourth Avenue toward Stuffy's seat.
lines.zh: 因为老绅士正穿过第四大道，朝胖子的长椅走来。

lines.en: Every Thanksgiving Day for nine years the Old Gentleman had come there to find Stuffy Pete on his seat. That was a thing that the Old Gentleman was trying to make into a tradition. Every Thanksgiving Day for nine years he had found Stuffy there. Then he had led Stuffy to a restaurant and watched him eat a big dinner.
lines.zh: 九年来的每个感恩节，老绅士都会来这儿找坐在长椅上的胖子皮特。这是老绅士想要把它变成传统的一件事。九年来的每个感恩节，他都在这儿找到胖子，然后带他去一家餐馆，看着他吃一顿大餐。

lines.en: They do these things more easily in old countries like England. They do them without thinking about them.
lines.zh: 在英国这样的老国家，做这种事容易多了，人们做起来想都不用想。

lines.en: But in this young country, we must think about them. In order to build a tradition, we must do the same thing again and again for a long time. The Old Gentleman loved his country. He believed he was helping to build a great American tradition. And he had been doing very well. Nine years is a long time here.
lines.zh: 可在这个年轻的国家，我们得想着去做。要建立一个传统，就得长期一遍又一遍地做同一件事。老绅士热爱他的国家，他相信自己正在帮助建立一个伟大的美国传统。而且他一直做得很好。在这里，九年已经很长了。

lines.en: The Old Gentleman moved, straight and proud, toward the tradition that he was building. Truly feeding Stuffy Pete once a year was not a very important tradition. There are greater and more important traditions in England. But it was a beginning. It proved that a tradition was at least possible in America.
lines.zh: 老绅士挺直身子，自豪地朝他正在建立的传统走去。说实话，一年请胖子皮特吃一顿饭，并不是什么很重要的传统。英国有更伟大、更重要的传统。但这是一个开始。它证明了在美国至少有可能建立传统。

lines.en: The Old Gentleman was thin and tall and sixty. He was dressed all in black. He wore eyeglasses. His hair was whiter and thinner than it had been last year. His legs did not seem as strong as they had seemed the year before.
lines.zh: 老绅士又瘦又高，六十岁，一身黑衣，戴着眼镜。他的头发比去年更白更稀了，两条腿好像也不如前一年有力了。

lines.en: As this kind Old Gentleman came toward him, Stuffy began to shake and his breath was shorter. He wished he could fly away. But he could not move from his seat.
lines.zh: 这位和善的老绅士向他走来时，胖子开始发抖，呼吸更急促了。他真希望能飞走，可他从长椅上动弹不得。

lines.en: "Good morning," said the Old Gentleman. "I am glad to see that the troubles of another year have not hurt you. You continue to move in health about the beautiful world. For that blessing you and I can give thanks on this day of thanksgiving. If you will come with me, my man, I will give you a dinner that will surely make your body feel as thankful as your mind."
lines.zh: “早上好，”老绅士说，“很高兴看到又一年的磨难没有伤到你。你依然健健康康地在这美丽的世界上走动。为了这份福气，你我可以在这感恩的日子里表示感谢。如果你愿意跟我来，我的朋友，我请你吃一顿饭，保证让你的身体和你的心一样感恩。”

lines.en: That is what the Old Gentleman said every time. Every Thanksgiving Day for nine years. The words themselves were almost a tradition. Always before, they had been music in Stuffy's ear. But now he looked up at the Old Gentleman's face with tears of suffering in his eyes. The snow turned quickly to water when it fell upon his hot face. But the Old Gentleman was shaking with the cold. He turned away, with his back to the wind, and he did not see Stuffy's eyes.
lines.zh: 老绅士每次都是这么说的。九年来的每个感恩节都是这样。这些话本身几乎已经成了一个传统。以前，这些话在胖子耳朵里一向像音乐一样动听。可现在，他抬头望着老绅士的脸，眼里含着痛苦的泪水。雪花落在他发烫的脸上，很快就化成了水。可老绅士冻得发抖，他转过身背对着风，没看到胖子的眼睛。

lines.en: Stuffy had always wondered why the Old Gentleman seemed sad as he spoke. He did not know that it was because the Old Gentleman was wishing that he had a son. A son would come there after he himself was gone. A son would stand proud and strong before Stuffy, and say: "In remembrance of my father." Then it would really be a tradition.
lines.zh: 胖子一直纳闷，为什么老绅士说话时显得很伤感。他不知道，那是因为老绅士希望自己有个儿子。等他自己不在了，儿子会来这里，自豪而有力地站在胖子面前说：“为了纪念我的父亲。”那样，这才真正成了一个传统。

lines.en: But the Old Gentleman had no family. He lived in a room in one of the old houses near the park. In the winter he grew a few flowers there. In the spring he walked on Fifth Avenue. In the summer he lived in a farmhouse in the hills outside New York, and he talked of a strange bug he hoped some day to find. In the fall season he gave Stuffy a dinner. These were the things that filled the Old Gentleman's life.
lines.zh: 可老绅士没有家人。他住在公园附近一栋老房子里的一个房间。冬天他在屋里种几盆花；春天他在第五大道散步；夏天他住在纽约城外山里的一座农舍，念叨着他希望有一天能找到的一种奇怪的虫子；秋天他请胖子吃一顿饭。这些就是充实老绅士生活的事。

lines.en: Stuffy Pete looked up at him for a half minute, helpless and very sorry for himself. The Old Gentleman's eyes were bright with the giving pleasure. His face was getting older every year, but his clothes were very clean and fresh.
lines.zh: 胖子皮特抬头看了他半分钟，无可奈何，非常可怜自己。老绅士的眼里闪烁着施予的快乐。他的脸一年比一年老，可他的衣服非常干净整洁。

lines.en: And then Stuffy made a strange noise. He was trying to speak. As the Old Gentleman had heard the noise nine times before, he understood it. He knew that Stuffy was accepting.
lines.zh: 然后胖子发出一个奇怪的声音，他在努力说话。老绅士以前已经听过九次这种声音，所以明白了。他知道胖子接受了。

lines.en: "Thank you. I'm very hungry."
lines.zh: “谢谢您。我很饿。”

lines.en: Stuffy was very full, but he understood that he was part of a tradition. His desire for food on Thanksgiving Day was not his own. It belonged to this kind Old Gentleman. True, America is free. But there are some things that must be done.
lines.zh: 胖子已经很饱了，可他明白自己是一个传统的一部分。他在感恩节想吃东西的愿望并不属于他自己，而是属于这位和善的老绅士。没错，美国是自由的，可有些事情是必须做的。

lines.en: The Old Gentleman led Stuffy to the restaurant and to the same table where they had always gone. They were known here.
lines.zh: 老绅士把胖子带到那家餐馆，坐到他们一向坐的那张桌子。这里的人都认识他们。

lines.en: "Here comes that old man," said a waiter, "that buys that old no-good fellow a dinner every Thanksgiving."
lines.zh: “那个老头又来了，”一个服务员说，“就是每年感恩节都给那个没出息的老家伙买顿饭的那位。”

lines.en: The Old Gentleman sat at the table, watching. The waiters brought food, and more food. And Stuffy began to eat.
lines.zh: 老绅士坐在桌边看着。服务员端来了食物，一道又一道。胖子开始吃了。

lines.en: No great and famous soldier ever battled more strongly against an enemy. The turkey and all the other food were gone almost as quickly as they appeared. Stuffy saw the look of happiness on the Old Gentleman's face. He continued to eat in order to keep it there.
lines.zh: 没有哪位伟大著名的战士和敌人作战时比他更拼命。火鸡和其他食物几乎是一端上来就没了。胖子看到老绅士脸上幸福的神情，为了让这神情一直留在那里，他继续吃。

lines.en: In an hour the battle was finished.
lines.zh: 一个小时后，战斗结束了。

lines.en: "Thank you," Stuffy said. "Thank you for my Thanksgiving dinner." Then he stood up heavily and started to go to the wrong door. A waiter turned him in the right direction.
lines.zh: “谢谢您，”胖子说，“谢谢您请我吃感恩节晚餐。”然后他沉重地站起来，朝错的门走去。一个服务员把他转向了正确的方向。

lines.en: The Old Gentleman carefully counted out $1.30, and left fifteen cents more for the waiter.
lines.zh: 老绅士仔细地数出一美元三十美分，又给服务员留了十五美分小费。

lines.en: They said goodbye, as they did each year, at the door. The Old Gentleman went south, and Stuffy went north.
lines.zh: 他们像每年一样，在门口道别。老绅士往南走，胖子往北走。

lines.en: Stuffy went around the first corner, and stood for one minute. Then he fell.
lines.zh: 胖子拐过第一个街角，站了一分钟，然后倒了下去。

lines.en: There he was found. He was picked up and taken to a hospital. They put him on a bed, and began to try to discover what strange sickness had made him fall.
lines.zh: 人们在那里发现了他，把他抬起来送到医院。他们让他躺到床上，开始设法查出是什么怪病让他倒下的。

lines.en: And an hour later the Old Gentleman was brought to the same hospital. And they put him on another bed, and began to try to discover what his sickness could be.
lines.zh: 一个小时后，老绅士也被送到了同一家医院。他们让他躺到另一张床上，开始设法查出他得的是什么病。

lines.en: After a little time one of the doctors met another doctor, and they talked.
lines.zh: 过了一会儿，一位医生碰到另一位医生，两人聊了起来。

lines.en: "That nice old gentleman over there," he said. "Do you know what's wrong with him? He's almost dead for the need of food. A very proud old man, I think. He told me he has had nothing to eat for three days."
lines.zh: “那边那位和善的老先生，”他说，“你知道他怎么了吗？他快饿死了。我想他是个非常要强的老人。他告诉我，他已经三天没吃东西了。”

qs.q: Why was Stuffy Pete not hungry this time?
opts: Two old ladies had already fed him a big dinner.
He had bought his own dinner.
qs.a: Two old ladies had already fed him a big dinner.
qs.why: "The servant had gathered him in."

qs.q: What did the Old Gentleman want to build?
qs.a: an American tradition
qs.why: "He believed he was helping to build a great American tradition."

qs.q: Why did the Old Gentleman fall ill?
opts: He had not eaten for three days.
qs.a: He had not eaten for three days.
qs.why: "He has had nothing to eat for three days."

lessons.title: One Thousand Dollars
lessons.sum: 花花公子吉利安从去世的叔叔那里只继承了一千美元，遗嘱要求他交一份花钱的报告。他四处问人这钱该怎么花，最后悄悄把钱送给了他暗恋的海登小姐。没想到遗嘱还有一份附加条款……

lines.en: "One thousand dollars," said the lawyer Tolman, in a severe and serious voice. "And here is the money."
lines.zh: “一千美元，”律师托尔曼用严厉认真的语气说，“钱在这儿。”

lines.en: Young Gillian touched the thin package of $50 bills and laughed.
lines.zh: 年轻的吉利安摸了摸那薄薄一叠五十美元的钞票，笑了。

lines.en: "It's such an unusual amount," he explained kindly to the lawyer. "If it had been $10,000, a man might celebrate with a lot of fireworks. Even $50 would have been less trouble."
lines.zh: “这个数目真不寻常，”他和气地向律师解释，“要是一万美元，还可以放一大堆烟花庆祝一下。就算是五十美元，也没这么麻烦。”

lines.en: "You heard the reading of your uncle's will after he died," continued the lawyer Tolman. "I do not know if you paid much attention to its details. I must remind you of one. You are required to provide us with a report of how you used this $1,000 as soon as you have spent it. I trust that you will obey the wishes of your late uncle."
lines.zh: “你叔叔去世后，你听过他遗嘱的宣读，”律师托尔曼接着说，“我不知道你有没有留意其中的细节。有一条我得提醒你：这一千美元一花完，你就必须向我们交一份报告，说明你是怎么用的。我相信你会遵从你已故叔叔的意愿。”

lines.en: "You may depend on it," said the young man respectfully.
lines.zh: “您放心。”年轻人恭恭敬敬地说。

lines.en: Gillian went to his club. He searched for a man he called Old Bryson.
lines.zh: 吉利安去了他的俱乐部，找一个他称为“老布赖森”的人。

lines.en: Old Bryson was a calm, anti-social man, about 40 years old. He was in a corner reading a book. When he saw Gillian coming near he took a noisy, deep breath, laid down his book and took off his glasses.
lines.zh: 老布赖森是个冷静、不爱交际的人，四十岁左右，正坐在角落里看书。他看到吉利安走近，就大声深吸一口气，放下书，摘下了眼镜。

lines.en: "I have a funny story to tell you," said Gillian.
lines.zh: “我有个好笑的故事要讲给你听。”吉利安说。

lines.en: "I wish you would tell it to someone in the billiard room," said Old Bryson. "You know how I hate your stories."
lines.zh: “我希望你去台球室讲给别人听，”老布赖森说，“你知道我多讨厌你的故事。”

lines.en: "This is a better one than usual," said Gillian, rolling a cigarette, and I'm glad to tell it to you. It's too sad and funny to go with the rattling of billiard balls.
lines.zh: “这个比平常那些好，”吉利安边卷烟边说，“我很乐意讲给你听。这故事又悲惨又好笑，配不上台球的咔嗒声。

lines.en: I've just come from a meeting with my late uncle's lawyers. He leaves me an even $1,000. Now, what can a man possibly do with $1,000?"
lines.zh: 我刚跟我已故叔叔的律师们见完面。他留给我整整一千美元。你说，一个人拿一千美元能干什么？”

lines.en: Old Bryson showed very little interest. "I thought the late Septimus Gillian was worth something like half a million."
lines.zh: 老布赖森没表现出多少兴趣。“我还以为已故的塞普蒂默斯·吉利安有五十万左右的身家。”

lines.en: "He was," agreed Gillian, happily. "And that's where the joke comes in. He has left a lot of his money to an organism. That is, part of it goes to the man who invents a new bacillus and the rest to establish a hospital for doing away with it again. There are one or two small, unimportant gifts on the side. The butler and the housekeeper get a seal ring and $10 dollars each. His nephew gets $1,000 thousand dollars."
lines.zh: “是有，”吉利安高兴地附和道，“笑话就在这儿。他把一大笔钱留给了一种微生物。也就是说，一部分给发现一种新杆菌的人，剩下的用来建一所医院，再把这种杆菌消灭掉。另外还有一两笔不值一提的小遗赠：管家和女管家各得一枚图章戒指和十美元。他的侄子得一千美元。”

lines.en: "Were there any others mentioned in your uncle's will?" asked Old Bryson.
lines.zh: “你叔叔的遗嘱里还提到别人吗？”老布赖森问。

lines.en: "None." said Gillian. "There is a Miss Hayden. My uncle was responsible for her. She lived in his house. She's a quiet thing … musical … the daughter of somebody who was unlucky enough to be his friend.
lines.zh: “没有了，”吉利安说，“有一位海登小姐，我叔叔是她的监护人，她住在他家里。她是个文静的姑娘……懂音乐……她父亲倒霉，跟我叔叔是朋友。

lines.en: "I forgot to say that she was in on the ring and $10 joke, too. I wish I had been. Then I could have had two bottles of wine, given the ring to the waiter and had the whole business off my hands. Now tell me what a man can do with $1,000."
lines.zh: “我忘了说，戒指加十美元的笑话也有她一份。我倒希望有我一份。那样我就能买两瓶酒，把戒指给服务员，整件事就了结了。现在告诉我，一个人拿一千美元能干什么。”

lines.en: Old Bryson rubbed his glasses and smiled. And when Old Bryson smiled, Gillian knew that he intended to be more offensive than ever.
lines.zh: 老布赖森擦了擦眼镜，笑了。老布赖森一笑，吉利安就知道他要说比平时更难听的话了。

lines.en: There are many good things a man could do with $1,000," said Bryson. "You?" he said with a gentle laugh. "Why, Bobby Gillian, there's only one reasonable thing you could do. You can go and buy Miss Lotta Lauriere a diamond necklace with the money and then take yourself off to Idaho and inflict your presence upon a ranch. I advise a sheep ranch, as I have a particular dislike for sheep."
lines.zh: “一个人拿一千美元能做很多好事，”布赖森说，“你嘛？”他轻声笑道，“哎，鲍比·吉利安，你只能做一件合情合理的事：用这钱去给洛塔·劳里埃小姐买条钻石项链，然后自己滚到爱达荷州，去祸害一个牧场。我建议去养羊的牧场，因为我特别讨厌羊。”

lines.en: "Thanks," said Gillian as he rose from his chair. "I knew I could depend on you, Old Bryson. You've hit on the very idea. I wanted to spend the money on one thing, because I have to turn in a report for it, and I hate itemizing."
lines.zh: “谢谢，”吉利安从椅子上站起来说，“我就知道能指望你，老布赖森。你正好说中了我的想法。我想把钱花在一样东西上，因为我得交报告，而我最讨厌一项一项列清单。”

lines.en: Gillian phoned for a cab and said to the driver: "The stage entrance of the Columbine Theatre."
lines.zh: 吉利安打电话叫了辆出租马车，对车夫说：“去哥伦拜恩剧院的后台入口。”

lines.en: The theater was crowded. Miss Lotta Lauriere was preparing for her performance when her assistant spoke the name of Mr. Gillian.
lines.zh: 剧院里人很多。洛塔·劳里埃小姐正在准备演出，她的助手报上了吉利安先生的名字。

lines.en: "Let it in," said Miss Lauriere. "Now, what is it, Bobby? I'm going on stage in two minutes."
lines.zh: “让他进来，”劳里埃小姐说，“怎么了，鲍比？我两分钟后就要上台了。”

lines.en: "It won't take two minutes for me. What do you say to a little thing in the jewelry line? I can spend $1,000."
lines.zh: “用不了两分钟。来点珠宝首饰怎么样？我能花一千美元。”

lines.en: "Say, Bobby," said Miss Lauriere, "Did you see that necklace Della Stacey had on the other night? It cost $2,200 at Tiffany's."
lines.zh: “我说，鲍比，”劳里埃小姐说，“你看到那天晚上黛拉·斯泰西戴的那条项链了吗？在蒂芙尼买的，两千两百美元。”

lines.en: Miss Lauriere was called to the stage for her performance.
lines.zh: 劳里埃小姐被叫上台演出去了。

lines.en: Gillian slowly walked out to where his cab was waiting. "What would you do with $1,000 if you had it?" he asked the driver.
lines.zh: 吉利安慢慢走到等着他的马车旁。“如果你有一千美元，你会拿它干什么？”他问车夫。

lines.en: "Open a drinking place," said the driver, quickly. "I know a place I could take money in with both hands. I've got it worked out -- if you were thinking of putting up the money."
lines.zh: “开个酒馆，”车夫马上说，“我知道一个地方，开了钱能两只手往里收。我都盘算好了——要是您想出这笔钱的话。”

lines.en: "Oh, no," said Gillian. "I was just wondering."
lines.zh: “哦，不，”吉利安说，“我只是好奇。”

lines.en: Eight blocks down Broadway, Gillian got out of the cab. A blind man sat on the sidewalk selling pencils. Gillian went out and stood in front of him.
lines.zh: 沿百老汇往下走了八个街区，吉利安下了车。一个盲人坐在人行道上卖铅笔。吉利安走过去站在他面前。

lines.en: "Excuse me, but would you mind telling me what you would do if you had $1,000?" asked Gillian.
lines.zh: “打扰一下，您介不介意告诉我，如果您有一千美元，您会做什么？”吉利安问。

lines.en: The blind man took a small book from his coat pocket and held it out. Gillian opened it and saw that it was a bank deposit book.
lines.zh: 盲人从外套口袋里掏出一个小本子递给他。吉利安打开一看，是一本银行存折。

lines.en: It showed that the blind man had a balance of $1,785 in his bank account. Gillian returned the bank book and got back into the cab.
lines.zh: 存折上显示，盲人的银行账户里有一千七百八十五美元。吉利安把存折还给他，又上了马车。

lines.en: "I forgot something," he said. "You may drive to the law offices of Tolman and Sharp."
lines.zh: “我忘了点事，”他说，“去托尔曼和夏普律师事务所。”

lines.en: Lawyer Tolman looked at Gillian in a hostile and questioning way.
lines.zh: 律师托尔曼带着敌意和疑问看着吉利安。

lines.en: "I beg your pardon," said Gillian, cheerfully. "But was Miss Hayden left anything by my uncle's will in addition to the ring and the $10 dollars?"
lines.zh: “打扰了，”吉利安高高兴兴地说，“请问我叔叔的遗嘱里，除了戒指和十美元，还留给海登小姐别的东西了吗？”

lines.en: "Nothing," said Mr. Tolman.
lines.zh: “没有。”托尔曼先生说。

lines.en: "I thank you very much, sir," said Gillian, and went to his cab. He gave the driver the address of his late uncle's home.
lines.zh: “非常感谢您，先生。”吉利安说着回到马车上，把他已故叔叔家的地址告诉了车夫。

lines.en: Miss Hayden was writing letters in the library. The small, thin woman wore black clothes. But you would have noticed her eyes. Gillian entered the room as if the world were unimportant.
lines.zh: 海登小姐正在书房里写信。这个瘦小的女人穿着一身黑衣，可你一定会注意到她的眼睛。吉利安走进房间，一副天下事都无所谓的样子。

lines.en: "I have just come from old Tolman's," he explained. "They have been going over the papers down there. They found a …"
lines.zh: “我刚从老托尔曼那儿来，”他解释道，“他们在那儿翻文件，发现了一个……”

lines.en: Gillian searched his memory for a legal term. "They found an amendment or a post-script or something to the will. It seemed that my uncle had second thoughts and willed you $1,000. Tolman asked me to bring you the money. Here it is."
lines.zh: 吉利安在记忆里搜寻一个法律术语。“他们发现了遗嘱的一条修正案还是附言之类的东西。好像我叔叔后来改了主意，留给你一千美元。托尔曼让我把钱给你带来。在这儿。”

lines.en: Gillian laid the money beside her hand on the desk. Miss Hayden turned white. "Oh!" she said. And again, "Oh!"
lines.zh: 吉利安把钱放在书桌上她的手边。海登小姐脸色发白。“哦！”她说，又说了一声：“哦！”

lines.en: Gillian half turned and looked out the window. In a low voice he said, "I suppose, of course, that you know I love you."
lines.zh: 吉利安半转过身，望着窗外，低声说：“我想，你当然知道我爱你。”

lines.en: "I am sorry," said Miss Hayden, as she picked up her money.
lines.zh: “对不起。”海登小姐说着拿起了她的钱。

lines.en: "There is no use?" asked Gillian, almost light-heartedly.
lines.zh: “没希望了？”吉利安问，口气几乎很轻松。

lines.en: "I am sorry," she said again.
lines.zh: “对不起。”她又说了一遍。

lines.en: "May I write a note?" asked Gillian, with a smile. Miss Hayden supplied him with paper and pen, and then went back to her writing table.
lines.zh: “我可以写张便条吗？”吉利安笑着问。海登小姐给了他纸和笔，然后回到她的写字台前。

lines.en: Gillian wrote a report of how he spent the $1,000: "Paid by Robert Gillian, $1,000 on account of the eternal happiness, owed by Heaven to the best and dearest woman on Earth."
lines.zh: 吉利安写了一份他如何花掉一千美元的报告：“罗伯特·吉利安支付一千美元，用于天堂欠世上最好、最可爱的女人的永恒幸福。”

lines.en: Gillian put the note into an envelope. He bowed to Miss Hayden and left.
lines.zh: 吉利安把便条装进信封，向海登小姐鞠了一躬，走了。

lines.en: His cab stopped again at the offices of Tolman and Sharp.
lines.zh: 他的马车又停在托尔曼和夏普律师事务所门口。

lines.en: "I have spent the $1,000," he said cheerfully, to Tolman. "And I have come to present a report of it, as I agreed." He threw a white envelope on the lawyer's table.
lines.zh: “我已经花掉了一千美元，”他高兴地对托尔曼说，“按照约定，我来交报告。”他把一个白信封扔在律师桌上。

lines.en: Without touching the envelope, Mr. Tolman went to a door and called his partner, Sharp. Together they searched for something in a large safe. They brought out a big envelope sealed with wax. As they opened the envelope, they shook their heads together over its contents. Then Tolman became the spokesman.
lines.zh: 托尔曼先生没碰信封，而是走到一扇门前，叫来了他的合伙人夏普。两人一起在一个大保险箱里找东西，拿出一个用蜡封着的大信封。打开信封后，两人看着里面的东西，一起摇了摇头。然后托尔曼开口了。

lines.en: "Mr. Gillian," he said, "there was an addition to your uncle's will. It was given to us privately, with instructions that it not be opened until you had provided us with a full report of your handling of the $1,000 received in the will.
lines.zh: “吉利安先生，”他说，“你叔叔的遗嘱还有一份附加条款。是私下交给我们的，并指示在你向我们提交如何使用遗嘱中那一千美元的完整报告之前，不得打开。

lines.en: "As you have satisfied the conditions, my partner and I have read the addition. I will explain to you the spirit of its contents.
lines.zh: “既然你已满足了条件，我和我的合伙人已经读了这份附加条款。我来向你说明它的大意。

lines.en: "In the event that your use of the $1,000 shows that you possess any of the qualifications that deserve reward, you stand to gain much more. If your disposal of the money in question has been sensible, wise, or unselfish, it is in our power to give you bonds to the value of $50,000. But if you have used this money in a wasteful, foolish way as you have in the past, the $50,000 is to be paid to Miriam Hayden, ward of the late Mr. Gillian, without delay.
lines.zh: “如果你对这一千美元的使用表明你具备任何值得奖励的品质，你就将得到多得多的钱。如果你对这笔钱的处置是明智、聪明或无私的，我们有权交给你价值五万美元的债券。但如果你像过去那样把钱用得浪费、愚蠢，这五万美元就要立即支付给已故吉利安先生的受监护人米里亚姆·海登。

lines.en: "Now, Mr. Gillian, Mr. Sharp and I will examine your report of the $1,000."
lines.zh: “现在，吉利安先生，夏普先生和我要审阅你那一千美元的报告了。”

lines.en: Mr. Tolman reached for the envelope. Gillian was a little quicker in taking it up. He calmly tore the report and its cover into pieces and dropped them into his pocket.
lines.zh: 托尔曼先生伸手去拿信封，吉利安比他快了一点把它拿了起来。他不慌不忙地把报告连同信封撕成碎片，塞进了口袋。

lines.en: "It's all right," he said, smilingly. "There isn't a bit of need to bother you with this. I don't suppose you would understand these itemized bets, anyway. I lost the $1,000 on the races. Good-day to you, gentlemen."
lines.zh: “没事，”他笑着说，“完全不必麻烦你们看这个。反正我想你们也看不懂这些一笔一笔的赌注。我把一千美元全输在赛马上了。祝你们日安，先生们。”

lines.en: Tolman and Sharp shook their heads mournfully at each other when Gillian left. They heard him whistling happily in the hallway as he waited for the elevator.
lines.zh: 吉利安走后，托尔曼和夏普对视着，难过地摇了摇头。他们听到他在走廊里等电梯时快活地吹着口哨。

qs.q: What did Gillian's uncle leave him?
qs.why: "He leaves me an even $1,000."

qs.q: What did Gillian really do with the money?
opts: He gave it to Miss Hayden.
He lost it on the races.
qs.a: He gave it to Miss Hayden.
qs.why: 他假称是遗嘱附言，把钱给了海登小姐。

qs.q: Why did Gillian tear up his report?
opts: So Miss Hayden would get the $50,000.
He made a mistake in it.
qs.a: So Miss Hayden would get the $50,000.
qs.why: 浪费钱，五万美元就归海登小姐。

lessons.title: The Ransom of Red Chief
lessons.sum: 两个骗子绑架了小镇富人的十岁儿子，想要两千美元赎金。没想到这孩子自称“红酋长”，把他们折腾得苦不堪言。孩子的父亲回信开出的条件，让绑匪哭笑不得。

lines.en: We present the short story "The Ransom of Red Chief" by O. Henry. This story was adapted for VOA Learning English by Shelley Gollust. It was produced by Lawan Davis. Here is Shep O'Neal with the story.
lines.zh: 我们为大家带来欧·亨利的短篇小说《红酋长的赎金》。本故事由谢莉·戈勒斯特为 VOA 慢速英语改编，拉万·戴维斯制作。下面请谢普·奥尼尔讲述。

lines.en: It looked like a good thing. But wait till I tell you. We were down south, in Alabama – Bill Driscoll and myself – when this kidnapping idea struck us. There was a town down there, as flat as a pancake, and called Summit. Bill and I had about $600. We needed just $2,000 more for an illegal land deal in Illinois.
lines.zh: 这事看起来是笔好买卖。不过，等我讲给你听。我们当时在南方的阿拉巴马州——比尔·德里斯科尔和我——突然冒出了绑架的念头。那儿有个小镇，平得像张煎饼，叫萨米特。比尔和我大约有六百美元，要在伊利诺伊做一桩非法的土地买卖，还差两千美元。

lines.en: We chose for our victim -- the only child of an influential citizen named Ebenezer Dorset. He was a boy of 10, with red hair. Bill and I thought that Ebenezer would pay a ransom of $2,000 to get his boy back. But wait till I tell you.
lines.zh: 我们选中的受害者是一位有头有脸的居民埃比尼泽·多塞特的独生子。那是个十岁的男孩，一头红发。比尔和我以为，埃比尼泽会付两千美元赎金把儿子赎回去。不过，等我讲给你听。

lines.en: About 2 miles from Summit was a little mountain, covered with cedar trees. There was an opening on the back of the mountain. We stored our supplies in that cave.
lines.zh: 离萨米特大约两英里有座小山，山上长满了雪松。山背面有个洞口，我们把补给都存在那个山洞里。

lines.en: One night, we drove a horse and carriage past old Dorset's house. The boy was in the street, throwing rocks at a cat on the opposite fence.
lines.zh: 一天晚上，我们赶着一辆马车经过老多塞特的家。那男孩在街上，正朝对面篱笆上的一只猫扔石头。

lines.en: "Hey little boy!" says Bill. "Would you like to have a bag of candy and a nice ride?"
lines.zh: “嘿，小朋友！”比尔说，“想要一袋糖果，再坐一趟好玩的车吗？”

lines.en: The boy hits Bill directly in the eye with a piece of rock.
lines.zh: 男孩一块石头正好砸中比尔的眼睛。

lines.en: That boy put up a fight like a wild animal. But, at last, we got him down in the bottom of the carriage and drove away.
lines.zh: 那孩子像头野兽一样反抗。不过最后，我们还是把他按在马车底板上，把车赶走了。

lines.en: We took him up to the cave. The boy had two large bird feathers stuck in his hair. He points a stick at me and says:
lines.zh: 我们把他带到山洞。男孩头发上插着两根大鸟羽毛。他用一根棍子指着我说：

lines.en: "Ha! Paleface, do you dare to enter the camp of Red Chief, the terror of the plains?"
lines.zh: “哈！白脸人，你竟敢闯进平原恐怖之王——红酋长的营地？”

lines.en: "He's all right now," says Bill, rolling up his pants and examining wounds on his legs. "We're playing Indian. I'm Old Hank, the trapper, Red Chief's captive. I'm going to be scalped at daybreak. By Geronimo! That kid can kick hard."
lines.zh: “他现在没事了，”比尔说着卷起裤腿，查看腿上的伤，“我们在玩印第安人的游戏。我是老汉克，捕兽人，红酋长的俘虏。天一亮我就要被剥头皮了。天哪！这小子踢得真狠。”

lines.en: "Red Chief," says I to the boy, "would you like to go home?"
lines.zh: “红酋长，”我对男孩说，“你想回家吗？”

lines.en: "Aw, what for?" says he. "I don't have any fun at home. I hate to go to school. I like to camp out. You won't take me back home again, will you?"
lines.zh: “哎，回家干吗？”他说，“在家一点也不好玩。我讨厌上学。我喜欢露营。你们不会再把我送回家吧？”

lines.en: "Not right away," says I. "We'll stay here in the cave a while."
lines.zh: “暂时不会，”我说，“我们在山洞里待一阵子。”

lines.en: "All right!" says he. "That'll be fine. I never had such fun in all my life."
lines.zh: “好啊！”他说，“那太好了。我这辈子从没这么开心过。”

lines.en: We went to bed about 11 o'clock. Just at daybreak, I was awakened by a series of terrible screams from Bill. Red Chief was sitting on Bill's chest, with one hand holding his hair. In the other, he had a sharp knife. He was attempting to cut off the top of Bill's head, based on what he had declared the night before.
lines.zh: 我们大约十一点睡觉。天刚亮，我就被比尔一连串可怕的尖叫声吵醒了。红酋长正坐在比尔胸口上，一只手揪着他的头发，另一只手拿着一把锋利的刀，照他前一晚宣布的那样，想把比尔的头皮割下来。

lines.en: I got the knife away from the boy. But, after that event, Bill's spirit was broken. He lay down, but he never closed an eye again in sleep as long as that boy was with us.
lines.zh: 我把刀从男孩手里夺了下来。可经过这件事，比尔的精神就垮了。他躺下了，可只要那孩子还跟我们在一起，他就再没合过眼。

lines.en: "Do you think anybody will pay out money to get a little imp like that back home?" Bill asked.
lines.zh: “你觉得会有人花钱把这么个小魔鬼赎回家吗？”比尔问。

lines.en: "Sure," I said. "A boy like that is just the kind that parents love. Now, you and the Chief get up and make something to eat, while I go up on the top of this mountain and look around."
lines.zh: “当然，”我说，“这样的孩子正是父母最疼的那种。好了，你和酋长起来做点吃的，我到山顶去看看。”

lines.en: I climbed to the top of the mountain. Over toward Summit, I expected to see the men of the village searching the countryside. But all was peaceful.
lines.zh: 我爬到山顶，朝萨米特那边望去，以为会看到村里的男人们在乡间到处搜寻。可一切都很平静。

lines.en: "Perhaps," says I to myself, "it has not yet been discovered that the wolves have taken the lamb from the fold." I went back down the mountain.
lines.zh: “也许，”我自言自语，“人们还没发现狼已经从羊圈里叼走了小羊。”我下了山。

lines.en: When I got to the cave, I found Bill backed up against the side of it. He was breathing hard, with the boy threatening to strike him with a rock.
lines.zh: 我回到山洞时，看见比尔背靠着洞壁，喘着粗气，那男孩正拿着一块石头要砸他。

lines.en: "He put a red-hot potato down my back," explained Bill, "and then crushed it with his foot. I hit his ears. Have you got a gun with you, Sam?"
lines.zh: “他把一个烫得发红的土豆塞进我后背，”比尔解释说，“然后用脚踩烂了。我扇了他耳光。你带枪了吗，山姆？”

lines.en: I took the rock away from the boy and ended the argument.
lines.zh: 我从男孩手里拿走石头，结束了这场争吵。

lines.en: "I'll fix you," says the boy to Bill. "No man ever yet struck the Red Chief but what he got paid for it. You better be careful!"
lines.zh: “我会收拾你的，”男孩对比尔说，“打过红酋长的人，没有一个不付出代价的。你最好小心点！”

lines.en: After eating, the boy takes a leather object with strings tied around it from his clothes and goes outside the cave unwinding it. Then we heard a kind of shout. It was Red Chief holding a sling in one hand. He moved it faster and faster around his head.
lines.zh: 吃完饭，男孩从衣服里掏出一个缠着绳子的皮东西，一边解开一边走出山洞。接着我们听到一声叫喊。原来是红酋长一只手拿着弹弓，在头顶上越甩越快。

lines.en: Just then I heard a heavy sound and a deep breath from Bill. A rock the size of an egg had hit him just behind his left ear. Bill fell in the fire across the frying pan of hot water for washing the dishes. I pulled him out and poured cold water on his head for half an hour.
lines.zh: 就在这时，我听到一声闷响和比尔的一声深喘。一块鸡蛋大的石头打中了他左耳后面。比尔倒进了火堆，压在装着洗碗热水的煎锅上。我把他拖出来，往他头上浇了半个小时的冷水。

lines.en: Then I went out and caught that boy and shook him.
lines.zh: 然后我出去抓住那孩子，摇了他一顿。

lines.en: "If your behavior doesn't improve," says I, "I'll take you straight home. Now, are you going to be good, or not?"
lines.zh: “你要是再不规矩，”我说，“我马上送你回家。现在，你到底乖不乖？”

lines.en: "I was only funning," says he. "I didn't mean to hurt Old Hank. But what did he hit me for? I'll behave if you don't send me home."
lines.zh: “我只是闹着玩，”他说，“我不是故意伤老汉克的。可他干吗打我？只要你们不送我回家，我就乖。”

lines.en: I thought it best to send a letter to old man Dorset that day, demanding the ransom and telling how it should be paid. The letter said:
lines.zh: 我想最好当天就给老多塞特送封信，要赎金，并说明怎么付。信上写道：

lines.en: "We have your boy hidden in a place far from Summit. We demand $1,500 for his return; the money to be left at midnight tonight at the same place and in the same box as your answer.
lines.zh: “我们把你儿子藏在离萨米特很远的地方。要赎回他，我们要一千五百美元；钱须于今晚午夜放在与你的回信相同的地点、相同的盒子里。

lines.en: "If you agree to these terms, send the answer in writing by a messenger tonight at half past 8 o'clock. After crossing Owl Creek, on the road to Poplar Cove, there are three large trees. At the bottom of the fence, opposite the third tree, will be a small box. The messenger will place the answer in this box and return immediately to Summit. If you fail to agree to our demand, you will never see your boy again. If you pay the money as demanded, he will be returned to you safe and well within three hours."
lines.zh: “如果你同意这些条件，今晚八点半派一名送信人送来书面答复。沿通往白杨湾的路过了猫头鹰溪，有三棵大树。在第三棵树对面的篱笆脚下，会有一个小盒子。送信人把回信放进盒子，立即返回萨米特。如果你不答应我们的要求，就再也见不到你儿子了。如果你按要求付钱，三小时内他就会平平安安地回到你身边。”

lines.en: I took the letter and walked over to Poplar Cove. I then sat around the post office and store. An old man there says he hears Summit is all worried because of Ebenezer Dorset's boy having been lost or stolen. That was all I wanted to know. I mailed my letter and left. The postmaster said the mail carrier would come by in an hour to take the mail on to Summit.
lines.zh: 我带着信走到白杨湾，在邮局兼杂货店附近转悠。那里有个老头说，他听说萨米特全镇都在着急，因为埃比尼泽·多塞特的儿子走丢了或被人拐了。我想知道的就这些。我寄了信就走了。邮局局长说，邮差一小时后会来把信送到萨米特。

lines.en: At half past eight, I was up in the third tree, waiting for the messenger to arrive. Exactly on time, a half-grown boy rides up the road on a bicycle. He finds the box at the foot of the fence. He puts a folded piece of paper into it and leaves, turning back toward Summit.
lines.zh: 八点半，我爬到第三棵树上，等送信人来。他准时到了：一个半大的男孩骑着自行车上了路，在篱笆脚下找到盒子，把一张折好的纸放进去，然后掉头回萨米特去了。

lines.en: I slid down the tree, got the note and was back at the cave in a half hour. I opened the note and read it to Bill. This is what it said:
lines.zh: 我从树上滑下来，拿到纸条，半小时后回到山洞。我打开纸条念给比尔听，上面写着：

lines.en: "Gentlemen: I received your letter about the ransom you ask for the return of my son. I think you are a little high in your demands. I hereby make you a counter-proposal, which I believe you will accept. You bring Johnny home and pay me $250, and I agree to take him off your hands. You had better come at night because the neighbors believe he is lost. And, I could not be responsible for what they would do to anybody they saw bringing him back. Very respectfully, Ebenezer Dorset."
lines.zh: “先生们：我收到了你们要求赎金归还我儿子的信。我觉得你们要价有点高。我在此向你们提出一个反建议，相信你们会接受：你们把约翰尼送回家，再付给我两百五十美元，我就同意把他从你们手里接过来。你们最好晚上来，因为邻居们以为他走丢了，我可不能保证他们会对送他回来的人做出什么事。此致敬礼，埃比尼泽·多塞特。”

lines.en: "Great pirates of Penzance!" says I, "of all the nerve…" But I looked at Bill and stopped. He had the most appealing look in his eyes I ever saw on the face of a dumb or talking animal.
lines.zh: “我的天哪！”我说，“真是好大的胆子……”可我看了看比尔，就住了口。他眼里那种哀求的神情，是我在任何哑巴动物或会说话的动物脸上都没见过的。

lines.en: "Sam," says he, "what's $250, after all? We've got the money. One more night of this boy will drive me crazy. I think Mister Dorset is making us a good offer. You aren't going to let the chance go, are you?"
lines.zh: “山姆，”他说，“说到底，两百五十美元算什么？我们有这笔钱。再跟这孩子待一个晚上，我就要疯了。我觉得多塞特先生开的条件挺好。你不会放过这个机会吧？”

lines.en: "Tell you the truth, Bill," says I, "this little lamb has got on my nerves, too. We'll take him home, pay the ransom and make our get-away."
lines.zh: “说实话，比尔，”我说，“这只小羊羔也快把我逼疯了。我们把他送回家，付了赎金，赶紧逃。”

lines.en: We took him home that night. We got him to go by telling him that his father had bought him a gun and we were going to hunt bears the next day.
lines.zh: 当天晚上我们就把他送回了家。我们骗他说，他爸爸给他买了一支枪，第二天我们要去猎熊，他才肯走。

lines.en: It was 12 o'clock when we knocked on Ebenezer's front door. Bill counted out $250 into Dorset's hand.
lines.zh: 我们敲埃比尼泽家的前门时已经十二点了。比尔把两百五十美元一张张数到多塞特手里。

lines.en: When the boy learned we were planning to leave him at home, he started to cry loudly and held himself as tight as he could to Bill's leg. His father pulled him away slowly.
lines.zh: 男孩一知道我们打算把他留在家里，就大哭起来，死死抱住比尔的腿。他爸爸慢慢把他拉开。

lines.en: "How long can you hold him?" asks Bill.
lines.zh: “你能抓住他多久？”比尔问。

lines.en: "I'm not as strong as I used to be," says old Dorset, "but I think I can promise you 10 minutes."
lines.zh: “我没以前那么有力气了，”老多塞特说，“不过我想我能保证十分钟。”

lines.en: "Enough," says Bill. "In 10 minutes, I shall cross the Central, Southern and Middle Western states, and be running for the Canadian border."
lines.zh: “够了，”比尔说，“十分钟里，我就能穿过中部、南部和中西部各州，一路奔向加拿大边境。”

lines.en: And, as dark as it was, and as fat as Bill was, and as good a runner as I am, he was a good mile and a half out of Summit before I could catch up with him.
lines.zh: 尽管天那么黑，比尔那么胖，而我又那么能跑，可直到他跑出萨米特足足一英里半，我才追上他。

qs.q: Why did Sam and Bill kidnap the boy?
qs.a: to get ransom money
qs.why: "Ebenezer would pay a ransom of $2,000."

qs.q: What did the boy call himself?
qs.a: Red Chief
qs.why: "the camp of Red Chief, the terror of the plains"

qs.q: What did the father ask for?
qs.a: that the kidnappers pay him $250
qs.why: "You bring Johnny home and pay me $250."

gloss: 白脸人（旧时故事里印第安人对白人的称呼）

lessons.title: Luck
lessons.sum: 一位家喻户晓的英国将军，在他的老师眼里却是个“彻头彻尾的傻瓜”。从考试到战场，他每犯一个错，都靠惊人的好运变成了胜利，最后满胸勋章——马克·吐温辛辣地讽刺了“名声”与“运气”。

lines.en: Our story today is called "Luck." It was written by Mark Twain. Here is Shep O'Neal with the story.
lines.zh: 我们今天的故事叫《运气》，作者是马克·吐温。下面请谢普·奥尼尔讲述。

lines.en: I was at a dinner in London given in honor of one of the most celebrated English military men of his time. I do not want to tell you his real name and titles. I will just call him Lieutenant General Lord Arthur Scoresby.
lines.zh: 我在伦敦参加过一次晚宴，那是为当时英国最著名的军人之一举办的。我不想说出他的真名和头衔，就叫他陆军中将阿瑟·斯科斯比勋爵吧。

lines.en: I cannot describe my excitement when I saw this great and famous man. There he sat, the man himself, in person, all covered with medals. I could not take my eyes off him. He seemed to show the true mark of greatness. His fame had no effect on him. The hundreds of eyes watching him, the worship of so many people, did not seem to make any difference to him.
lines.zh: 看到这位伟大而著名的人物时，我激动得无法形容。他就坐在那里，本人亲临，满身勋章。我的眼睛离不开他。他似乎显示出真正伟人的风范：名声对他毫无影响，几百双注视他的眼睛、那么多人的崇拜，对他好像都无所谓。

lines.en: Next to me sat a clergyman, who was an old friend of mine. He was not always a clergyman. During the first half of his life he was a teacher in the military school at Woolwich. There was a strange look in his eye as he leaned toward me and whispered – "Privately – he is a complete fool." He meant, of course, the hero of our dinner.
lines.zh: 坐在我旁边的是一位牧师，我的老朋友。他并不是一直当牧师的。前半生，他在伍利奇的军校当教官。他凑过来对我耳语时，眼里有一种奇怪的神情：“私下说一句——他是个彻头彻尾的傻瓜。”他指的当然是我们这场晚宴的主角。

lines.en: This came as a shock to me. I looked hard at my friend. I could not have been more surprised if he had said the same thing about Napoleon, or Socrates, or Solomon. But I was sure of two things about the clergyman. He always spoke the truth. And, his judgment of men was good. Therefore, I wanted to find out more about our hero as soon as I could.
lines.zh: 这让我大吃一惊。我紧紧盯着我的朋友。就算他说的是拿破仑、苏格拉底或所罗门，我也不会更惊讶了。可我对这位牧师有两点很确定：他总是说真话，而且他看人很准。所以，我想尽快多了解一些我们这位英雄的事。

lines.en: Some days later I got a chance to talk with the clergyman, and he told me more. These are his exact words:
lines.zh: 几天后，我有机会和牧师聊天，他又告诉了我更多。下面是他的原话：

lines.en: About forty years ago, I was an instructor in the military academy at Woolwich, when young Scoresby was given his first examination. I felt extremely sorry for him. Everybody answered the questions well, intelligently, while he – why, dear me – he did not know anything, so to speak. He was a nice, pleasant young man. It was painful to see him stand there and give answers that were miracles of stupidity.
lines.zh: 大约四十年前，我在伍利奇军校当教官，那时年轻的斯科斯比参加他的第一次考试。我非常同情他。别人都答得很好、很聪明，而他——哎呀，可以说他什么都不知道。他是个和善讨喜的年轻人。看他站在那里，给出一个个蠢得像奇迹一样的答案，真让人难受。

lines.en: I knew of course that when examined again he would fail and be thrown out. So, I said to myself, it would be a simple, harmless act to help him as much as I could.
lines.zh: 我当然知道他下次考试一定会不及格，被赶出学校。所以我对自己说，尽力帮帮他，是件简单又无害的事。

lines.en: I took him aside and found he knew a little about Julius Caesar's history. But, he did not know anything else. So, I went to work and tested him and worked him like a slave. I made him work, over and over again, on a few questions about Caesar, which I knew he would be asked.
lines.zh: 我把他叫到一边，发现他对尤利乌斯·恺撒的历史略知一二，别的就一窍不通了。于是我就开始考他，像对奴隶一样逼他用功。我让他翻来覆去地练几道关于恺撒的题，我知道考试一定会问到。

lines.en: If you will believe me, he came through very well on the day of the examination. He got high praise too, while others who knew a thousand times more than he were sharply criticized. By some strange, lucky accident, he was asked no questions but those I made him study. Such an accident does not happen more than once in a hundred years.
lines.zh: 信不信由你，考试那天他表现得非常好，还得到了高度赞扬，而那些比他多懂一千倍的人却挨了严厉批评。真是奇怪的幸运巧合，考官问他的全是我让他准备的题。这种巧合一百年也碰不上一次。

lines.en: Well, all through his studies, I stood by him, with the feeling a mother has for a disabled child. And he always saved himself by some miracle.
lines.zh: 就这样，他整个求学期间，我都守着他，就像母亲对待残疾的孩子那样。而他每次都靠某种奇迹化险为夷。

lines.en: I thought that what in the end would destroy him would be the mathematics examination. I decided to make his end as painless as possible. So, I pushed facts into his stupid head for hours. Finally, I let him go to the examination to experience what I was sure would be his dismissal from school. Well, sir, try to imagine the result. I was shocked out of my mind. He took first prize! And he got the highest praise.
lines.zh: 我想，最后毁掉他的会是数学考试。我决定让他的结局尽量不那么痛苦。于是我花了好几个小时，把知识硬塞进他那笨脑袋里。最后我让他去参加考试，去经历我确信必然到来的开除。好了，先生，你猜结果怎么样？我惊得魂都没了：他得了第一名！还得到了最高的赞扬。

lines.en: I felt guilty day and night – what I was doing was not right. But I only wanted to make his dismissal a little less painful for him. I never dreamed it would lead to such strange, laughable results.
lines.zh: 我日夜内疚——我做的事是不对的。可我只是想让他被开除时少受点罪。我做梦也没想到会导致这么奇怪又可笑的结果。

lines.en: I thought that sooner or later one thing was sure to happen: The first real test once he was through school would ruin him.
lines.zh: 我想，迟早有一件事肯定会发生：他一毕业，第一次真正的考验就会把他毁掉。

lines.en: Then, the Crimean War broke out. I felt that sad for him that there had to be a war. Peace would have given this donkey a chance to escape from ever being found out as being so stupid. Nervously, I waited for the worst to happen. It did. He was appointed an officer. A captain, of all things! Who could have dreamed that they would place such a responsibility on such weak shoulders as his.
lines.zh: 后来，克里米亚战争爆发了。我为他难过，偏偏要打仗。要是和平，这头蠢驴说不定一辈子都不会被人发现有多蠢。我紧张地等着最坏的事情发生。果然发生了：他被任命为军官。偏偏还是个上尉！谁能想到他们会把这么重的担子放在他这么弱的肩膀上。

lines.en: I said to myself that I was responsible to the country for this. I must go with him and protect the nation against him as far as I could. So, I joined up with him. And away we went to the field.
lines.zh: 我对自己说，这件事我得对国家负责。我必须跟着他，尽我所能保护国家不受他的害。于是我跟他一起参了军，一起上了战场。

lines.en: And there – oh dear, it was terrible. Mistakes, fearful mistakes – why, he never did anything that was right – nothing but mistakes. But, you see, nobody knew the secret of how stupid he really was. Everybody misunderstood his actions. They saw his stupid mistakes as works of great intelligence. They did, honestly!
lines.zh: 到了那里——哦，天哪，太可怕了。错误，可怕的错误——哎，他就没做对过一件事——全是错误。可你知道，没人知道他到底有多蠢这个秘密。大家都误解了他的行为，把他的愚蠢错误看成了大智慧的杰作。真的是这样！

lines.en: His smallest mistakes made a man in his right mind cry, and shout and scream too – to himself, of course. And what kept me in a continual fear was the fact that every mistake he made increased his glory and fame. I kept saying to myself that when at last they find out about him, it will be like the sun falling out of the sky.
lines.zh: 他最小的错误都能让一个头脑正常的人哭、喊、尖叫——当然是在心里。而让我一直提心吊胆的是：他每犯一个错，他的荣耀和名声就增加一分。我不停地对自己说，等他们终于发现真相的时候，那就像太阳从天上掉下来一样。

lines.en: He continued to climb up, over the dead bodies of his superiors. Then, in the hottest moment of one battle down went our colonel. My heart jumped into my mouth, for Scoresby was the next in line to take his place. Now, we are in for it, I said…
lines.zh: 他踩着阵亡的上级一路往上爬。后来，在一场战斗最激烈的时候，我们的上校倒下了。我的心都提到了嗓子眼，因为斯科斯比是接替他的下一个人。我说，这下我们完了……

lines.en: The battle grew hotter. The English and their allies were steadily retreating all over the field. Our regiment occupied a position that was extremely important. One mistake now would bring total disaster. And what did Scoresby do this time – he just mistook his left hand for his right hand…that was all. An order came for him to fall back and support our right. Instead, he moved forward and went over the hill to the left. We were over the hill before this insane movement could be discovered and stopped. And what did we find? A large and unsuspected Russian army waiting! And what happened – were we all killed? That is exactly what would have happened in ninety-nine cases out of a hundred. But no – those surprised Russians thought that no one regiment by itself would come around there at such a time.
lines.zh: 战斗越来越激烈。英军和盟军在整个战场上节节败退。我们团守着一个极其重要的阵地，此刻一个错误就会带来彻底的灾难。这次斯科斯比做了什么？他只是把左手当成了右手……就这么回事。命令要他后撤去支援我们的右翼，他却向前推进，翻过左边的山头。等这个疯狂的行动被发现、被制止时，我们已经翻过了山。结果我们发现了什么？一支没人料到的庞大俄军正在那里等着！结果怎么样——我们全被消灭了吗？一百次里有九十九次会是这样。可是没有——那些吃惊的俄国人以为，不可能有哪个团会在这种时候单独绕到那里。

lines.en: It must be the whole British army, they thought. They turned tail, away they went over the hill and down into the field in wild disorder, and we after them. In no time, there was the greatest turn around you ever saw. The allies turned defeat into a sweeping and shining victory.
lines.zh: 他们以为一定是整个英国军队来了。他们掉头就跑，乱哄哄地翻过山头冲下田野，我们紧追在后。转眼间，出现了你见过的最大逆转。盟军反败为胜，取得了一场彻底而辉煌的胜利。

lines.en: The allied commander looked on, his head spinning with wonder, surprise and joy. He sent right off for Scoresby, and put his arms around him and hugged him on the field in front of all the armies. Scoresby became famous that day as a great military leader – honored throughout the world. That honor will never disappear while history books last.
lines.zh: 盟军司令看着这一切，惊奇、意外、欢喜得头都晕了。他马上派人叫来斯科斯比，当着全军的面在战场上拥抱了他。那天，斯科斯比成了著名的伟大将领，誉满全球。只要历史书还在，这份荣誉就永远不会消失。

lines.en: He is just as nice and pleasant as ever, but he still does not know enough to come in out of the rain. He is the stupidest man in the universe.
lines.zh: 他还是像以前一样和善讨喜，可他至今仍蠢得连下雨了都不知道进屋躲雨。他是全宇宙最蠢的人。

lines.en: Until now, nobody knew it but Scoresby and myself. He has been followed, day by day, year by year, by a strange luck. He has been a shining soldier in all our wars for years. He has filled his whole military life with mistakes. Every one of them brought him another honorary title. Look at his chest, flooded with British and foreign medals. Well, sir, every one of them is the record of some great stupidity or other. They are proof that the best thing that can happen to a man is to be born lucky. I say again, as I did at the dinner, Scoresby's a complete fool.
lines.zh: 直到现在，除了斯科斯比和我，没人知道这一点。一天又一天，一年又一年，一种奇怪的好运一直跟着他。多年来，他在我们的每一场战争中都是一颗耀眼的将星。他的整个军旅生涯全是错误，而每一个错误都给他带来又一个荣誉头衔。看看他的胸前，挂满了英国和外国的勋章。先生，每一枚都记录着某一次大蠢事。它们证明了一个人能碰到的最好的事，就是生来好运。我再说一遍，就像我在晚宴上说的：斯科斯比是个彻头彻尾的傻瓜。

qs.q: What does the clergyman say about Scoresby?
qs.a: He is a complete fool.
qs.why: "Privately – he is a complete fool."

qs.q: How did Scoresby pass his first examination?
opts: He was asked only the questions he had practiced.
qs.a: He was asked only the questions he had practiced.
qs.why: "he was asked no questions but those I made him study."

qs.q: What mistake won the battle?
opts: He went left instead of right.
qs.a: He went left instead of right.
qs.why: "he just mistook his left hand for his right hand."

lessons.title: The Celebrated Jumping Frog of Calaveras County
lessons.zh: 卡拉维拉斯县著名的跳蛙
lessons.sum: 在加州一个荒废的淘金营地，老西蒙·惠勒絮絮叨叨讲起赌徒吉姆·斯迈利的故事：他什么都赌，还花三个月训练出一只会跳的青蛙“丹尼尔·韦伯斯特”。一个陌生人跟他打赌，却偷偷往青蛙嘴里灌了铅弹……马克·吐温的成名作。

lines.en: Our story is called "The Celebrated Jumping Frog of Calaveras County." It was written by Mark Twain. Here is Shep O'Neal with the story.
lines.zh: 我们的故事叫《卡拉维拉斯县著名的跳蛙》，作者是马克·吐温。下面请谢普·奥尼尔讲述。

lines.en: A friend of mine in the East asked me to visit old Simon Wheeler, to ask about my friends friend, Leonidas W. Smiley. I did as my friend asked me to do and this story is the result.
lines.zh: 我在东部的一位朋友让我去拜访老西蒙·惠勒，打听一下他朋友的朋友——列奥尼达斯·W·斯迈利。我照朋友说的做了，于是就有了这个故事。

lines.en: I found Simon Wheeler sleeping by the stove in the ruined mining camp of Angels.
lines.zh: 我在荒废了的天使营淘金营地找到了西蒙·惠勒，他正在炉子边睡觉。

lines.en: I saw that he was fat and had no hair, and had a gentle and simple look upon his peaceful face. He woke up, and gave me "good-day."
lines.zh: 我看到他胖胖的，头上没有头发，平静的脸上带着温和、朴实的神情。他醒了，跟我道了声“你好”。

lines.en: I told him a friend had asked me to find out about a friend named Leonidas W. Smiley, who he heard was at one time living in Angels Camp. I added that if Mr. Wheeler could tell me anything about this Leonidas W. Smiley, I would feel a great responsibility to him.
lines.zh: 我告诉他，有位朋友托我打听一个叫列奥尼达斯·W·斯迈利的朋友，听说他曾经在天使营住过。我还说，如果惠勒先生能告诉我任何关于这位列奥尼达斯·W·斯迈利的事，我会非常感激他。

lines.en: Simon Wheeler forced me into a corner with his chair and began telling me this long story. He never smiled, he never frowned. But all through the endless story there was a feeling of great seriousness and honesty. This showed me plainly that he thought the heroes of the story were men of great intelligence.
lines.zh: 西蒙·惠勒用椅子把我逼到一个角落，开始给我讲这个长长的故事。他从不笑，也从不皱眉。可在这个没完没了的故事里，自始至终都有一种非常严肃认真的感觉。这让我清楚地看出，他认为故事里的英雄都是非常聪明的人。

lines.en: I let him go on in his own way, and never stopped him once. This is the story Simon Wheeler told.
lines.zh: 我任由他按自己的方式讲下去，一次也没打断他。下面就是西蒙·惠勒讲的故事。

lines.en: Leonidas W. …. hm… Le… well, there was a man here once by the name of Jim Smiley, in the winter of 1849 -- or may be it was the spring of 1850. Anyway, he was the strangest man. He was always making money on anything that turned up if he could get anybody to try to make money on the other side. And if he could not do that, he would change sides.
lines.zh: 列奥尼达斯·W……嗯……列……嗯，这儿从前有个人叫吉姆·斯迈利，是 1849 年冬天——也可能是 1850 年春天。总之，他是个最古怪的人。只要能找到人跟他对赌，什么事他都要拿来赌钱。要是找不到，他就换到另一边去赌。

lines.en: And he was lucky, uncommon lucky. He most always was a winner. If there was a dog-fight, he would try to win money on it. If there was a cat-fight, he would take the risk. If there was a chicken-fight, he would try to win money on it. Why, if there was two birds setting on a fence, he would want you to decide which one would fly first so he could win money.
lines.zh: 而且他运气好，好得出奇。他几乎总是赢家。要是有斗狗，他就想赌一把；要是有猫打架，他也要冒这个险；要是有斗鸡，他也想赢钱。哎呀，要是有两只鸟停在篱笆上，他都想让你猜哪只先飞，好赢你的钱。

lines.en: Lots of the boys here have seen that Smiley and can tell you about him. Why, it did not matter to him. He would try to make money on anything. He was the most unusual man. Parson Walker's wife was very sick once, for a long time, and it seemed as if they were not going to save her.
lines.zh: 这儿有好多小伙子都见过那个斯迈利，能给你讲他的事。哎，对他来说什么都无所谓，他什么都要赌。他是最不寻常的人。有一次，沃克牧师的妻子病得很重，病了很久，看样子是救不活了。

lines.en: But one morning he come in, and Smiley asked him how was his wife, and he said she was better, thank God. And Smiley, before he thought, says, "Well, I'll risk my money she will not get well."
lines.zh: 可有一天早上牧师进来，斯迈利问他妻子怎么样了，他说好些了，感谢上帝。斯迈利想都没想就说：“那好，我赌她好不了。”

lines.en: And Smiley had a little small dog. To look at the dog, you would think he was not worth anything but to sit around and look mean and look for a chance to steal something. But as soon as there was money, he was a different dog. Another dog might attack and throw him around two or three times. Then all of a sudden Smiley's dog would grab that other dog by his back leg and hang on till the men said it was over.
lines.zh: 斯迈利有一条小狗。光看那条狗，你会觉得它一无是处，只会到处坐着，一副凶相，找机会偷东西。可一旦有钱下注，它就变成了另一条狗。别的狗可能扑上来把它甩来甩去两三回，然后斯迈利的狗会突然咬住对方的后腿，死死不放，直到人们宣布比赛结束。

lines.en: Smiley always come out the winner on that dog, at least until he found a dog once that did not have any back legs. The dog's legs had been cut off in a machine. Well, the fighting continued long enough, and the money was gone. Then when Smiley's dog come to make a grab (at) the other dog's back legs, he saw in a minute how there was a problem.
lines.zh: 斯迈利靠那条狗一直赢，直到有一次他碰到一条没有后腿的狗。那条狗的腿被机器轧断了。斗了很久，钱都押上了。斯迈利的狗去咬对方的后腿时，一下子就看出了问题。

lines.en: The other dog was going to win and Smiley's dog looked surprised and did not try to win the fight anymore. He gave Smiley a look that said he was sorry for fighting a dog that did not have any back legs for him to hold, which he needed to win a fight. Then Smiley's dog walked away, laid down and died. He was a good dog, and would have made a name for himself if he had lived, for he had intelligence. It always makes me feel sorry when I think of that last fight of his and the way it turned out.
lines.zh: 对方要赢了，斯迈利的狗一脸惊讶，再也不想赢了。它给了斯迈利一个眼神，像是在说，对不起，跟一条没有后腿可咬的狗打——而咬后腿是它赢的法宝。然后斯迈利的狗走开，躺下，死了。它是条好狗，要是活着一定能出名，因为它很聪明。每次想起它最后那场斗和那样的结局，我就难过。

lines.en: Well, this Smiley had rats, and chickens, and cats and all of them kind of things. You could not get anything for him to risk money on but he would match you. He caught a frog one day, and took him home, and said he was going to educate the frog. And so he never done nothing for three months but sit in his back yard and teach that frog to jump. And you bet you he did teach him, too.
lines.zh: 嗯，这个斯迈利还养了老鼠、鸡、猫，各种这类东西。你拿出什么来跟他赌，他都能跟你配上一样。有一天他抓了一只青蛙带回家，说要教育这只青蛙。于是三个月里他什么都不干，就坐在后院教那只青蛙跳。你猜怎么着，他还真教会了。

lines.en: He would give him a little hit from behind. And the next minute you would see that frog dancing in the air and then come down all on his feet and all right, like a cat. Smiley got him so the frog was catching flies, and he would catch one of those insects every time.
lines.zh: 他从后面轻轻碰它一下，转眼你就看到那只青蛙在空中翻腾，然后四脚着地，稳稳当当，像猫一样。斯迈利还训练它抓苍蝇，每次都能抓到一只。

lines.en: Smiley said all a frog wanted was education, and he could do almost anything. And I believe him. Why, I have seen him set Dan'l Webster down here on this floor—Dan'l Webster was the name of the frog -- and sing out, "Flies, Dan'l, flies!" And quicker than you could shut your eyes that frog would jump straight up and catch a fly off the table. Then he would fall down on the floor again like a ball of dirt and start rubbing the side of his head with his back foot as if he had no idea he had been doing any more than any frog might do.
lines.zh: 斯迈利说，青蛙需要的只是教育，有了教育，它几乎什么都能做。我信他的话。哎呀，我亲眼见过他把丹尼尔·韦伯斯特放在这儿地板上——丹尼尔·韦伯斯特是那只青蛙的名字——然后大喊：“苍蝇，丹尼尔，苍蝇！”你眼睛还没来得及眨，那青蛙就笔直跳起来，从桌上抓走一只苍蝇。然后它又像一团泥巴一样落回地板上，开始用后脚挠脑袋侧面，好像根本不知道自己做了什么比别的青蛙更厉害的事。

lines.en: You never seen a frog so honest and simple as he was, for all he was so skilled. And when it come to jumping, he could get over more ground in one jump than any animal of his kind that you ever saw.
lines.zh: 你从没见过这么老实、这么朴实的青蛙，尽管它本领那么高。说到跳远，它一跳能跳得比你见过的任何同类都远。

lines.en: Smiley was very proud of his frog, and people who had traveled and been everywhere all said he was better than any frog they had ever seen.
lines.zh: 斯迈利为他的青蛙非常自豪，那些走南闯北、哪儿都去过的人都说，它比他们见过的任何青蛙都强。

lines.en: Well, one day a stranger came in and says to Smiley, "What might be that you have got in the box?"
lines.zh: 嗯，有一天一个陌生人进来，对斯迈利说：“你盒子里装的是什么？”

lines.en: And Smiley says, "It's only just a frog." And the man took it, and looked at it careful, and turned it round this way and that, and says, "Hm, so it is. Well, what is he good for?"
lines.zh: 斯迈利说：“不过是只青蛙。”那人接过盒子，仔细看了看，这样转转那样转转，说：“嗯，还真是。那它有什么用？”

lines.en: "Well," Smiley says, easy and careless, "he can out jump any frog in Calaveras county."
lines.zh: “嗯，”斯迈利满不在乎地说，“它能跳得比卡拉维拉斯县的任何青蛙都远。”

lines.en: The man took the box again, and took another long look, and gave it back to Smiley, and says, "Well, I don't see anything about that frog that is any better than any other frog."
lines.zh: 那人又拿过盒子，又看了好久，还给斯迈利，说：“嗯，我看不出这只青蛙比别的青蛙强在哪儿。”

lines.en: "Maybe you don't," Smiley says. "Maybe you understand frogs and maybe you don't. Anyways, I will risk forty dollars and bet you that he can jump farther than any frog in Calaveras County."
lines.zh: “也许你看不出，”斯迈利说，“也许你懂青蛙，也许你不懂。反正，我押四十美元跟你赌，它能跳得比卡拉维拉斯县的任何青蛙都远。”

lines.en: And the man studied a minute. "Well, I'm only a stranger here, and I do not have a frog. But if I had a frog, I would risk my money on it.
lines.zh: 那人想了一会儿。“嗯，我在这儿只是个外地人，没有青蛙。要是我有青蛙，我就跟你赌。”

lines.en: And then Smiley says, "That's all right. If you will hold my box a minute, I will go and get you a frog." And so the man took the box, and put up his forty dollars and sat down to wait.
lines.zh: 于是斯迈利说：“没关系。你帮我拿一下盒子，我去给你弄一只青蛙来。”于是那人接过盒子，押上四十美元，坐下来等。

lines.en: He sat there a long time thinking and thinking. Then he got the frog out of the box. He filled its mouth full of bullets used to kill small birds. Then he put the frog on the floor.
lines.zh: 他在那儿坐了很久，想啊想。然后他把青蛙从盒子里拿出来，往它嘴里灌满了打小鸟用的铅弹，再把青蛙放到地板上。

lines.en: Now Smiley had caught another frog and gave it to the man and said, "Now sit him next to Dan'l and I will give the word."
lines.zh: 这时斯迈利抓来了另一只青蛙，交给那人说：“好，把它放在丹尼尔旁边，我来喊口令。”

lines.en: Then Smiley says, "One-two-three-go!" and Smiley and the other man touched the frogs.
lines.zh: 然后斯迈利喊：“一——二——三——跳！”斯迈利和那人都碰了碰青蛙。

lines.en: The new frog jumped. Dan'l just lifted up his body but could not move at all. He was planted like a building. Smiley was very surprised and angry too. But he did not know what the problem was.
lines.zh: 新来的青蛙跳了出去。丹尼尔只是抬了抬身子，一点也动不了，像一栋房子一样钉在地上。斯迈利又吃惊又生气，可他不知道问题出在哪儿。

lines.en: The other man took the money and started away. And when he was going out the door, he looked back and said "Well, I don't see anything about that frog that is any better than any other frog."
lines.zh: 那人拿了钱就走。走出门时，他回头说：“嗯，我看不出这只青蛙比别的青蛙强在哪儿。”

lines.en: Smiley stood looking down at Dan'l a long time, and at last says, "I wonder what in the nation happened to that frog. I wonder if there is something wrong with him."
lines.zh: 斯迈利站着低头看了丹尼尔很久，最后说：“我真不知道这青蛙到底怎么了。不知道它是不是哪儿出了毛病。”

lines.en: And he picked up Dan'l and turned him upside down and out came a whole lot of bullets. And Smiley was the angriest man. He set the frog down and took out after that man but he never caught him.
lines.zh: 他拿起丹尼尔，把它倒过来，结果倒出了一大堆铅弹。斯迈利气坏了。他放下青蛙去追那个人，可再也没追上。

lines.en: Now Simon Wheeler heard his name called and got up to see what was wanted. He told me to wait but I did not think that more stories about Jim Smiley would give me any more information about Leonidas W. Smiley, and so I started to walk away.
lines.zh: 这时西蒙·惠勒听到有人叫他，起身去看有什么事。他让我等着，可我觉得再听吉姆·斯迈利的故事，也得不到列奥尼达斯·W·斯迈利的任何消息，于是就起身要走。

lines.en: At the door I met Mr. Wheeler returning, and he started talking again. "Well, this here Smiley had a yellow cow with one eye and no tail…"
lines.zh: 在门口我碰上了正回来的惠勒先生，他又开始讲：“嗯，这个斯迈利有头独眼、没尾巴的黄母牛……”

lines.en: However, lacking both time and interest, I did not wait to hear about the cow. I just left.
lines.zh: 可是我既没时间也没兴趣，没等着听那头牛的事，就走了。

lines.en: This story was written by Mark Twain and adapted for Learning English by Karen Leggett.
lines.zh: 本故事由马克·吐温创作，凯伦·莱格特为慢速英语改编。

qs.q: What did Jim Smiley love to do?
qs.a: bet money on anything
qs.why: "He would try to make money on anything."

qs.q: What was the frog's name?
qs.a: Dan'l Webster
qs.why: "Dan'l Webster was the name of the frog."

qs.q: Why couldn't Dan'l jump?
opts: The stranger filled him with bullets.
qs.a: The stranger filled him with bullets.
qs.why: "He filled its mouth full of bullets."

gloss: （此处）像钉在地上一样站着不动

lessons.title: The Californian's Tale
lessons.sum: 淘金热过后，加州斯坦尼斯劳山谷的小镇空无一人，只剩亨利的小屋整洁温馨。他满怀期待地等着出门探亲的年轻妻子星期六回来，两位老矿工也天天来问她的消息。故事结尾揭开了令人心碎的真相。

lines.en: Our story today is called "The Californian's Tale." It was written by Mark Twain. Here is Shep O'Neal with the story.
lines.zh: 我们今天的故事叫《加州人的故事》，作者是马克·吐温。下面请谢普·奥尼尔讲述。

lines.en: When I was young, I went looking for gold in California. I never found enough to make me rich. But I did discover a beautiful part of the country. It was called "the Stanislau." The Stanislau was like Heaven on Earth. It had bright green hills and deep forests where soft winds touched the trees.
lines.zh: 年轻时，我去加利福尼亚淘金。我从没淘到足够让我发财的金子，却发现了一片美丽的土地，叫“斯坦尼斯劳”。斯坦尼斯劳就像人间天堂：青翠的山丘，幽深的森林，和风轻抚着树梢。

lines.en: Other men, also looking for gold, had reached the Stanislau hills of California many years before I did. They had built a town in the valley with sidewalks and stores, banks and schools. They had also built pretty little houses for their families.
lines.zh: 在我之前很多年，别的淘金者就来到了加州的斯坦尼斯劳山区。他们在山谷里建起了一座小镇，有人行道和商店，有银行和学校。他们还为家人盖了漂亮的小房子。

lines.en: At first, they found a lot of gold in the Stanislau hills. But their good luck did not last. After a few years, the gold disappeared. By the time I reached the Stanislau, all the people were gone, too.
lines.zh: 起初，他们在斯坦尼斯劳山里找到了很多金子。可好运没能持续。几年后，金子没了。等我来到斯坦尼斯劳时，人也都走光了。

lines.en: Grass now grew in the streets. And the little houses were covered by wild rose bushes. Only the sound of insects filled the air as I walked through the empty town that summer day so long ago. Then, I realized I was not alone after all.
lines.zh: 街上长满了草，小房子被野蔷薇丛盖住了。很久以前的那个夏日，我穿过空荡荡的小镇时，空中只有虫鸣。后来，我发现自己并不是孤身一人。

lines.en: A man was smiling at me as he stood in front of one of the little houses. This house was not covered by wild rose bushes. A nice little garden in front of the house was full of blue and yellow flowers. White curtains hung from the windows and floated in the soft summer wind.
lines.zh: 一个男人站在一栋小房子前，对我微笑。这栋房子没有被野蔷薇覆盖。屋前一个整洁的小花园里开满了蓝色和黄色的花。白色的窗帘挂在窗前，在柔和的夏风中飘动。

lines.en: Still smiling, the man opened the door of his house and motioned to me. I went inside and could not believe my eyes. I had been living for weeks in rough mining camps with other gold miners. We slept on the hard ground, ate canned beans from cold metal plates and spent our days in the difficult search for gold.
lines.zh: 那人仍然微笑着，打开屋门，向我招手。我走进去，简直不敢相信自己的眼睛。几个星期来，我一直和别的淘金者住在简陋的矿工营地里：睡在坚硬的地上，用冰冷的铁盘子吃罐头豆子，整天辛辛苦苦地找金子。

lines.en: Here in this little house, my spirit seemed to come to life again.
lines.zh: 在这间小屋里，我的精神好像又活了过来。

lines.en: I saw a bright rug on the shining wooden floor. Pictures hung all around the room. And on little tables there were seashells, books and china vases full of flowers. A woman had made this house into a home.
lines.zh: 我看到亮闪闪的木地板上铺着一块色彩明亮的地毯，房间四周挂着画。小桌上摆着贝壳、书和插满鲜花的瓷瓶。是一个女人把这栋房子变成了一个家。

lines.en: The pleasure I felt in my heart must have shown on my face. The man read my thoughts. "Yes," he smiled, "it is all her work. Everything in this room has felt the touch of her hand."
lines.zh: 我心里的喜悦一定都写在了脸上。那人看出了我的心思。“是的，”他笑着说，“这都是她做的。屋里的每一样东西都经过她的手。”

lines.en: One of the pictures on the wall was not hanging straight. He noticed it and went to fix it. He stepped back several times to make sure the picture was really straight. Then he gave it a gentle touch with his hand.
lines.zh: 墙上有一幅画挂歪了。他注意到了，走过去扶正。他往后退了好几次，确认画真的正了，然后用手轻轻碰了它一下。

lines.en: "She always does that," he explained to me. "It is like the finishing pat a mother gives her child's hair after she has brushed it. I have seen her fix all these things so often that I can do it just the way she does. I don't know why I do it. I just do it."
lines.zh: “她总是这样做，”他向我解释，“就像母亲给孩子梳完头后，最后轻轻拍一下那样。我看她摆弄这些东西太多次了，所以能做得和她一模一样。我也不知道为什么这样做，就是这样做了。”

lines.en: As he talked, I realized there was something in this room that he wanted me to discover. I looked around. When my eyes reached a corner of the room near the fireplace, he broke into a happy laugh and rubbed his hands together.
lines.zh: 他说话时，我意识到这屋里有样东西是他想让我发现的。我四处看了看。当我的目光落到壁炉边的一个角落时，他高兴地笑起来，搓着双手。

lines.en: "That's it!" he cried out. "You have found it! I knew you would. It is her picture. I went to a little black shelf that held a small picture of the most beautiful woman I had ever seen. There was a sweetness and softness in the woman's expression that I had never seen before.
lines.zh: “就是它！”他喊道，“你找到了！我就知道你会找到的。是她的照片。”我走到一个黑色小架子前，上面放着一张小照片，照片上是我见过的最美丽的女人。她的神情里有一种我从没见过的甜美和温柔。

lines.en: The man took the picture from my hands and stared at it. "She was nineteen on her last birthday. That was the day we were married. When you see her…oh, just wait until you meet her!"
lines.zh: 那人从我手里拿过照片，凝视着它。“她上次生日满十九岁，那天也是我们结婚的日子。等你见到她……哦，等你见到她就知道了！”

lines.en: "Where is she now?" I asked.
lines.zh: “她现在在哪儿？”我问。

lines.en: "Oh, she is away," the man sighed, putting the picture back on the little black shelf. "She went to visit her parents. They live forty or fifty miles from here. She has been gone two weeks today."
lines.zh: “哦，她出门了，”那人叹了口气，把照片放回黑色小架子上，“她去看她父母了。他们住在离这儿四五十英里的地方。到今天她已经走了两个星期了。”

lines.en: "When will she be back?" I asked. "Well, this is Wednesday," he said slowly. "She will be back on Saturday, in the evening."
lines.zh: “她什么时候回来？”我问。“嗯，今天是星期三，”他慢慢地说，“她星期六晚上回来。”

lines.en: I felt a sharp sense of regret. "I am sorry, because I will be gone by then," I said.
lines.zh: 我感到一阵强烈的遗憾。“真可惜，那时我已经走了。”我说。

lines.en: "Gone? No! Why should you go? Don't go. She will be so sorry. You see, she likes to have people come and stay with us."
lines.zh: “走了？不！你为什么要走？别走。她会很遗憾的。你知道，她喜欢有人来家里住。”

lines.en: "No, I really must leave," I said firmly.
lines.zh: “不，我真的得走了。”我坚决地说。

lines.en: He picked up her picture and held it before my eyes. "Here," he said. "Now you tell her to her face that you could have stayed to meet her and you would not."
lines.zh: 他拿起她的照片，举到我眼前。“给，”他说，“你当着她的面告诉她，你本来可以留下来见她，却不肯。”

lines.en: Something made me change my mind as I looked at the picture for a second time. I decided to stay.
lines.zh: 我第二次看着那张照片时，有什么东西让我改了主意。我决定留下来。

lines.en: The man told me his name was Henry.
lines.zh: 那人告诉我，他叫亨利。

lines.en: That night, Henry and I talked about many different things, but mainly about her. The next day passed quietly.
lines.zh: 那天晚上，亨利和我聊了很多事，但主要是聊她。第二天平静地过去了。

lines.en: Thursday evening we had a visitor. He was a big, grey-haired miner named Tom. "I just came for a few minutes to ask when she is coming home," he explained. "Is there any news?"
lines.zh: 星期四晚上，来了一位客人。他是个高大的白发矿工，叫汤姆。“我就来一会儿，问问她什么时候回家，”他解释道，“有消息吗？”

lines.en: "Oh yes," the man replied. "I got a letter. Would you like to hear it? He took a yellowed letter out of his shirt pocket and read it to us. It was full of loving messages to him and to other people – their close friends and neighbors. When the man finished reading it, he looked at his friend. "Oh no, you are doing it again, Tom! You always cry when I read a letter from her. I'm going to tell her this time!"
lines.zh: “哦，有，”那人回答，“我收到一封信。你想听听吗？”他从衬衫口袋里掏出一封发黄的信，念给我们听。信里满是对他、对其他人——他们的好朋友和邻居——充满爱意的话。那人念完，看着他的朋友。“哦，不，你又这样了，汤姆！我每次念她的信，你都哭。这次我要告诉她！”

lines.en: "No, you must not do that, Henry," the grey-haired miner said. "I am getting old. And any little sorrow makes me cry. I really was hoping she would be here tonight."
lines.zh: “不，你不能那样做，亨利，”白发矿工说，“我老了，一点点伤心事都会让我掉眼泪。我真希望她今晚就在这儿。”

lines.en: The next day, Friday, another old miner came to visit. He asked to hear the letter. The message in it made him cry, too. "We all miss her so much," he said.
lines.zh: 第二天星期五，又有一位老矿工来访。他要求听那封信，信里的话也让他哭了。“我们都很想她。”他说。

lines.en: Saturday finally came. I found I was looking at my watch very often. Henry noticed this. "You don't think something has happened to her, do you?" he asked me.
lines.zh: 星期六终于到了。我发现自己频频看表。亨利注意到了。“你不会觉得她出了什么事吧？”他问我。

lines.en: I smiled and said that I was sure she was just fine. But he did not seem satisfied.
lines.zh: 我笑着说，我相信她一切都好。可他好像并不放心。

lines.en: I was glad to see his two friends, Tom and Joe, coming down the road as the sun began to set. The old miners were carrying guitars. They also brought flowers and a bottle of whiskey. They put the flowers in vases and began to play some fast and lively songs on their guitars.
lines.zh: 太阳开始落山时，我很高兴看到他的两个朋友汤姆和乔沿路走来。两位老矿工带着吉他，还带来了鲜花和一瓶威士忌。他们把花插进花瓶，开始用吉他弹起欢快的曲子。

lines.en: Henry's friends kept giving him glasses of whiskey, which they made him drink. When I reached for one of the two glasses left on the table, Tom stopped my arm. "Drop that glass and take the other one!" he whispered. He gave the remaining glass of whiskey to Henry just as the clock began to strike midnight.
lines.zh: 亨利的朋友们不停地给他倒威士忌，硬让他喝。当我伸手去拿桌上剩下的两杯中的一杯时，汤姆拦住了我的胳膊。“放下那杯，拿另一杯！”他低声说。钟开始敲响午夜时，他把剩下的那杯威士忌递给了亨利。

lines.en: Henry emptied the glass. His face grew whiter and whiter. "Boys," he said, "I am feeling sick. I want to lie down."
lines.zh: 亨利一饮而尽。他的脸越来越白。“伙计们，”他说，“我不舒服，想躺一会儿。”

lines.en: Henry was asleep almost before the words were out of his mouth.
lines.zh: 话还没说完，亨利几乎就睡着了。

lines.en: In a moment, his two friends had picked him up and carried him into the bedroom. They closed the door and came back. They seemed to be getting ready to leave. So I said, "Please don't go gentlemen. She will not know me. I am a stranger to her."
lines.zh: 转眼间，他的两个朋友把他抬起来送进卧室，关上门回来了。他们好像准备走了。于是我说：“请别走，先生们。她不认识我，我对她来说是个陌生人。”

lines.en: They looked at each other. "His wife has been dead for nineteen years," Tom said.
lines.zh: 他们对视了一眼。“他妻子已经死了十九年了。”汤姆说。

lines.en: "Dead?" I whispered.
lines.zh: “死了？”我低声说。

lines.en: "Dead or worse," he said.
lines.zh: “死了，或者更糟。”他说。

lines.en: "She went to see her parents about six months after she got married. On her way back, on a Saturday evening in June, when she was almost here, the Indians captured her.
