No one ever saw her again. Henry lost his mind. He thinks she is still alive. When June comes, he thinks she has gone on her trip to see her parents. Then he begins to wait for her to come back. He gets out that old letter. And we come around to visit so he can read it to us.
lines.zh: “她结婚大约六个月后去看她父母。回来的路上，六月的一个星期六晚上，快到家的时候，她被印第安人掳走了。从此再也没人见过她。亨利疯了。他以为她还活着。每到六月，他就以为她去探望父母了，然后开始等她回来。他会拿出那封旧信，我们就过来看他，好让他念信给我们听。

lines.en: "On the Saturday night she is supposed to come home, we come here to be with him. We put a sleeping drug in his drink so he will sleep through the night. Then he is all right for another year."
lines.zh: “到了她该回家的那个星期六晚上，我们就来这里陪他。我们在他的酒里放安眠药，让他一觉睡到天亮。这样他就又能好好过一年。”

lines.en: Joe picked up his hat and his guitar. "We have done this every June for nineteen years," he said. "The first year there were twenty-seven of us. Now just the two of us are left." He opened the door of the pretty little house. And the two old men disappeared into the darkness of the Stanislau.
lines.zh: 乔拿起帽子和吉他。“十九年来，每年六月我们都这样做，”他说，“第一年我们有二十七个人。现在只剩我们两个了。”他打开那栋漂亮小屋的门。两位老人消失在斯坦尼斯劳的夜色中。

qs.q: Why was the town in the Stanislau empty?
opts: The gold disappeared and people left.
qs.a: The gold disappeared and people left.
qs.why: "After a few years, the gold disappeared."

qs.q: When did Henry say his wife would come back?
qs.a: Saturday evening
qs.why: "She will be back on Saturday, in the evening."

qs.q: What was the truth about Henry's wife?
opts: She was lost nineteen years ago.
qs.a: She was lost nineteen years ago.
qs.why: "His wife has been dead for nineteen years."

lessons.title: Pigs Is Pigs
lessons.by: Ellis Parker Butler（埃利斯·帕克·巴特勒）
lessons.sum: 快递员弗兰纳里坚持按规章办事：豚鼠（guinea pig）也是“猪”，运费要按每只三十美分收，而不是宠物的二十五美分。收件人不肯付钱，公司上下来回写信，一拖好几个月——豚鼠却一窝接一窝地生，最后多达几千只。

lines.en: Our story today is called "Pigs is Pigs." It was written by Ellis Parker Butler.
lines.zh: 我们今天的故事叫《猪就是猪》，作者是埃利斯·帕克·巴特勒。

lines.en: Mike Flannery, the agent of the Interurban Express Company, leaned over the desk in the company's office in Westcote and shook his fist. Mr. Morehouse, angry and red, stood on the other side of the desk shaking with fury. The argument had been long and hot. At last Mr. Morehouse had become speechless.
lines.zh: 城际快递公司的代理人迈克·弗兰纳里在公司韦斯特科特营业所的柜台前探着身子，挥着拳头。莫尔豪斯先生气得满脸通红，站在柜台另一边，怒得浑身发抖。两人争得又久又凶，最后莫尔豪斯先生气得说不出话来了。

lines.en: The cause of the trouble lay on the desk between the two men. It was a box with two guinea pigs inside.
lines.zh: 麻烦的根源就放在两人之间的柜台上：一个盒子，里面有两只豚鼠。

lines.en: "Do as you like, then!" shouted Flannery. "Pay for them and take them. Or don't pay for them and leave them here. Rules are rules, Mr. Morehouse. And Mike Flannery is not going to break them."
lines.zh: “那随你便！”弗兰纳里嚷道，“付钱就把它们带走，不付钱就把它们留在这儿。规矩就是规矩，莫尔豪斯先生。迈克·弗兰纳里是不会破坏规矩的。”

lines.en: "But you stupid idiot!" shouted Mr. Morehouse, madly shaking a thin book beneath the agent's nose. "Can't you read it here – in your own book of transportation rates? 'Pets, domestic, Franklin to Westcote, if correctly boxed, twenty-five cents each.'"
lines.zh: “你这个蠢货！”莫尔豪斯先生嚷道，疯狂地在代理人鼻子底下挥着一本薄薄的册子，“你就不会看看这儿吗——你们自己的运价手册上写着：‘家养宠物，富兰克林至韦斯特科特，包装妥当者，每只二十五美分。’”

lines.en: He threw the book on the desk. "What more do you want? Aren't they pets? Aren't they domestic? Aren't they correctly boxed? What?"
lines.zh: 他把册子扔在柜台上。“你还想怎么样？它们不是宠物吗？不是家养的吗？包装得不妥当吗？啊？”

lines.en: He turned and walked back and forth rapidly, with a furious look on his face. "Pets," he said. "P-E-T-S! Twenty-five cents each. Two times twenty-five is fifty! Can you understand that? I offer you fifty cents."
lines.zh: 他转过身，脸色铁青，来回快步踱着。“宠物，”他说，“宠——物！每只二十五美分。二乘以二十五等于五十！你听得懂吗？我给你五十美分。”

lines.en: Flannery reached for the book. He ran his hand through the pages and stopped at page sixty-four.
lines.zh: 弗兰纳里伸手拿过册子，用手翻着，停在第六十四页。

lines.en: "I don't take fifty cents," he whispered in an unpleasant voice. "Here's the rule for it: 'When the agent be in any doubt about which two rates should be charged on a shipment, he shall charge the larger. The person receiving the shipment may put in a claim for the overcharge.' In this case, Mr. Morehouse, I be in doubt. Pets them animals may be. And domestic they may be, but pigs I'm sure they do be. And my rule says plain as the nose on your face, 'Pigs, Franklin to Westcote, thirty cents each.'"
lines.zh: “我不收五十美分，”他用不客气的声音低声说，“这儿有一条规定：‘代理人如对一批货物应按哪两种运价收费存有疑问，应按较高者收取。收货人可就多收部分提出索赔。’这件事上，莫尔豪斯先生，我有疑问。这些动物也许是宠物，也许是家养的，可我敢肯定它们是猪。我的规定写得清清楚楚，就像你脸上的鼻子一样：‘猪，富兰克林至韦斯特科特，每只三十美分。’”

lines.en: Mr. Morehouse shook his head savagely. "Nonsense!" he shouted. "Confounded nonsense, I tell you! That rule means common pigs, not guinea pigs!"
lines.zh: 莫尔豪斯先生狠狠地摇头。“胡说！”他嚷道，“我告诉你，简直是胡说八道！那条规定指的是普通的猪，不是豚鼠！”

lines.en: "Pigs is pigs," Flannery said firmly.
lines.zh: “猪就是猪。”弗兰纳里坚定地说。

lines.en: Mr. Morehouse bit his lip and then flung his arms out wildly. "Very well!" he shouted. "You shall hear of this! Your president shall hear of this! It is an outrage! I have offered you fifty cents. You refuse it. Keep the pigs until you are ready to take the fifty cents. But, by George, sir, if one hair of those pigs' heads is harmed, I will have the law on you!" He turned and walked out, slamming the door. Flannery carefully lifted the box from the desk and put it in a corner.
lines.zh: 莫尔豪斯先生咬着嘴唇，然后猛地张开双臂。“好极了！”他嚷道，“你等着瞧！我要让你们总裁知道这件事！这简直是暴行！我给你五十美分，你不收。那你就留着这两只猪，等你愿意收五十美分为止。可是，天哪，先生，要是这两只猪头上的一根毛受了伤，我就跟你打官司！”他转身走了出去，砰地关上门。弗兰纳里小心地把盒子从柜台上拿起来，放到角落里。

lines.en: Mr. Morehouse quickly wrote a letter to the president of the transportation express company. The president answered, informing Mr. Morehouse that all claims for overcharge should be sent to the Claims Department.
lines.zh: 莫尔豪斯先生马上给快递公司总裁写了一封信。总裁回信告诉他，所有多收费用的索赔都应寄给索赔部。

lines.en: Mr. Morehouse wrote to the Claims Department. One week later he received an answer. The Claims Department said it had discussed the matter with the agent at Westcote. The agent said Mr. Morehouse had refused to accept the two guinea pigs shipped to him. Therefore, the department said, Mr. Morehouse had no claim against the company and should write to its Tariff Department.
lines.zh: 莫尔豪斯先生又写信给索赔部。一星期后，他收到了回信。索赔部说已和韦斯特科特的代理人讨论过此事。代理人说莫尔豪斯先生拒绝接收寄给他的两只豚鼠。因此，索赔部说，莫尔豪斯先生对公司没有索赔权，应该写信给运价部。

lines.en: Mr. Morehouse wrote to the Tariff Department. He stated his case clearly. The head of the Tariff Department read Mr. Morehouse's letter. "Huh! Guinea pigs," he said. "Probably starved to death by this time." He wrote to the agent asking why the shipment was held up. He also wanted to know if the guinea pigs were still in good health.
lines.zh: 莫尔豪斯先生又写信给运价部，把自己的理由讲得清清楚楚。运价部主任读了莫尔豪斯先生的信。“哼！豚鼠，”他说，“这会儿大概已经饿死了。”他写信问代理人为什么扣着这批货，还想知道豚鼠是否仍然健康。

lines.en: Before answering, agent Flannery wanted to make sure his report was up to date. So he went to the back of the office and looked into the cage. Good Lord! There were now eight of them! All well and eating like hippopotamuses.
lines.zh: 回信之前，代理人弗兰纳里想确保自己的报告是最新的。于是他走到营业所后面，往笼子里看了看。天哪！现在有八只了！只只健康，吃起东西来像河马一样。

lines.en: He went back to the office and explained to the head of the Tariff Department what the rules said about pigs. And as for the condition of the guinea pigs, said Flannery, they were all well. But there were eight of them now, all good eaters.
lines.zh: 他回到柜台，向运价部主任说明了规定里关于猪的条文。至于豚鼠的状况，弗兰纳里说，它们都很好。只是现在有八只了，个个都很能吃。

lines.en: The head of the Tariff Department laughed when he read Flannery's letter. He read it again and became serious.
lines.zh: 运价部主任读到弗兰纳里的信时笑了。他又读了一遍，变得严肃起来。

lines.en: "By George!" he said. "Flannery is right. Pigs is pigs. I'll have to get something official on this." He spoke to the president of the company. The president treated the matter lightly. "What is the rate on pigs and on pets?" he asked.
lines.zh: “天哪！”他说，“弗兰纳里说得对。猪就是猪。这件事我得弄个正式说法。”他去找公司总裁谈。总裁没把这事当回事。“猪和宠物的运价各是多少？”他问。

lines.en: "Pigs thirty cents, pets twenty-five," the head of the Tariff Department answered. "Then of course guinea pigs are pigs," the president said.
lines.zh: “猪三十美分，宠物二十五美分。”运价部主任回答。“那豚鼠当然是猪了。”总裁说。

lines.en: "Yes," the head of the Tariff Department agreed. "I look at it that way too. A thing that can come under two rates is naturally to be charged at the higher one. But are guinea pigs, pigs? Aren't they rabbits?"
lines.zh: “是的，”运价部主任同意道，“我也这么看。一样东西能套两种运价，自然该按高的收。可豚鼠是猪吗？它们不是兔子吗？”

lines.en: "Come to think of it," the president said, "I believe they are more like rabbits. Sort of half-way between pig and rabbit. I think the question is this – are guinea pigs of the domestic pig family? I'll ask Professor Gordon. He is an expert about such things."
lines.zh: “这么一想，”总裁说，“我觉得它们更像兔子，算是介于猪和兔子之间吧。我认为问题是：豚鼠属不属于家猪科？我去问问戈登教授，他是这方面的专家。”

lines.en: The president wrote to Professor Gordon. Unfortunately, the professor was in South America collecting zoological samples. His wife forwarded the letter to him.
lines.zh: 总裁写信给戈登教授。不巧的是，教授正在南美洲采集动物标本。他的妻子把信转寄给了他。

lines.en: The professor was in the High Andes Mountains. The letter took many months to reach him. In time, the president forgot the guinea pigs. The head of the Tariff Department forgot them. Mr. Morehouse forgot them. But agent Flannery did not. The guinea pigs had increased to thirty-two. He asked the head of the Tariff Department what he should do with them.
lines.zh: 教授在安第斯山脉的高山上，信过了好几个月才送到他手里。时间一长，总裁忘了豚鼠，运价部主任忘了，莫尔豪斯先生也忘了。可代理人弗兰纳里没忘。豚鼠已经增加到三十二只了。他问运价部主任该拿它们怎么办。

lines.en: "Don't sell the pigs," agent Flannery was told. "They are not your property. Take care of them until the case is settled."
lines.zh: “别卖那些猪，”上面这样告诉代理人弗兰纳里，“它们不是你的财产。在案子解决之前好好照顾它们。”

lines.en: The guinea pigs needed more room. Flannery made a large and airy room for them in the back of his office.
lines.zh: 豚鼠需要更多空间。弗兰纳里在营业所后面给它们腾出了一间宽敞通风的屋子。

lines.en: Some months later he discovered he now had one hundred sixty of them. He was going out of his mind.
lines.zh: 几个月后，他发现现在有一百六十只了。他快要疯了。

lines.en: Not long after this, the president of the express company heard from Professor Gordon. It was a long and scholarly letter. It pointed out that the guinea pig was the cavia aparoea, while the common pig was the genus sus of the family suidae.
lines.zh: 这之后没多久，快递公司总裁收到了戈登教授的回信。那是一封又长又学术的信，信中指出，豚鼠是“豚鼠属”动物，而普通的猪是“猪科猪属”。

lines.en: The president then told the head of the Tariff Department that guinea pigs are not pigs and must be charged only twenty-five cents as domestic pets. The Tariff Department informed agent Flannery that he should take the one hundred sixty guinea pigs to Mr. Morehouse and collect twenty-five cents for each of them.
lines.zh: 于是总裁告诉运价部主任，豚鼠不是猪，只能按家养宠物收每只二十五美分。运价部通知代理人弗兰纳里，把一百六十只豚鼠送给莫尔豪斯先生，每只收二十五美分。

lines.en: Agent Flannery wired back. "I've got eight hundred now. Shall I collect for eight hundred or what? How about the sixty-four dollars I paid for cabbages to feed them?"
lines.zh: 代理人弗兰纳里发电报回复：“现在已有八百只了。按八百只收钱还是怎样？我花六十四美元买白菜喂它们，这钱怎么算？”

lines.en: Many letters went back and forth. Flannery was crowded into a few feet at the extreme front of the office. The guinea pigs had all the rest of the room. Time kept moving on as the letters continued to go back and forth.
lines.zh: 信件来来回回写了很多封。弗兰纳里被挤到营业所最前面几英尺的地方，其余的地方全归豚鼠了。信件往来不断，时间一天天过去。

lines.en: Flannery now had four thousand sixty-four guinea pigs. He was beginning to lose control of himself. Then, he got a telegram from the company that said: "Error in guinea pig bill. Collect for two guinea pigs -- fifty cents."
lines.zh: 弗兰纳里现在有四千零六十四只豚鼠了。他开始控制不住自己了。这时他收到公司的一封电报，上面写着：“豚鼠账单有误。只收两只豚鼠的钱——五十美分。”

lines.en: Flannery ran all the way to Mr. Morehouse's home. But Mr. Morehouse had moved. Flannery searched for him in town but without success. He returned to the express office and found that two hundred six guinea pigs had entered the world since he left the office.
lines.zh: 弗兰纳里一路跑到莫尔豪斯先生家，可莫尔豪斯先生已经搬走了。弗兰纳里在镇上到处找他，却没找到。他回到快递营业所，发现自他离开以来，又有两百零六只豚鼠出生了。

lines.en: At last, he got an urgent telegram from the main office: "Send the pigs to the main office of the company at Franklin." Flannery did so. Soon, came another telegram. "Stop sending pigs. Warehouse full." But he kept sending them.
lines.zh: 最后，他收到总公司发来的一封加急电报：“将猪运至富兰克林总公司。”弗兰纳里照办了。很快又来了一封电报：“停止运猪。仓库已满。”可他还是继续往那儿运。

lines.en: Agent Flannery finally got free of the guinea pigs. "Rules may be rules," he said, "but so long as Flannery runs this express office, pigs is pets and cows is pets and horses is pets and lions and tigers and Rocky Mountain goats is pets. And the rate on them is twenty-five cents."
lines.zh: 代理人弗兰纳里终于摆脱了豚鼠。“规矩也许就是规矩，”他说，“可只要这个快递营业所归弗兰纳里管，猪就是宠物，牛也是宠物，马也是宠物，狮子、老虎和落基山的山羊都是宠物。运费一律二十五美分。”

lines.en: Then he looked around and said cheerfully, "Well, anyhow, it is not as bad as it might have been. What if them guinea pigs had been elephants?"
lines.zh: 然后他看了看四周，高兴地说：“好吧，不管怎样，情况还不算最糟。要是那些豚鼠是大象，那可怎么办？”

qs.q: Why wouldn't Flannery take fifty cents?
opts: He thought guinea pigs were pigs, at 30 cents each.
He wanted to keep the animals.
qs.a: He thought guinea pigs were pigs, at 30 cents each.
qs.why: "Pigs is pigs."

qs.q: What happened while the letters went back and forth?
opts: The guinea pigs had more and more babies.
qs.a: The guinea pigs had more and more babies.
qs.why: 从 2 只变成了 4000 多只。

qs.q: What did Flannery decide at the end?
opts: All animals are pets at 25 cents.
qs.a: All animals are pets at 25 cents.
qs.why: "pigs is pets and cows is pets..."

lessons.title: The Lady, or the Tiger?
lessons.by: Frank R. Stockton（弗兰克·斯托克顿）
lessons.sum: 古时一位国王用“机会”审判犯人：犯人在竞技场里任选一扇门，一扇门后是猛虎，一扇门后是美女。公主爱上了一个平民青年，他被押上了竞技场。公主知道门后的秘密，悄悄示意他打开右边的门——门后出来的会是什么？

lines.en: Long ago, in the very olden time, there lived a powerful king. Some of his ideas were progressive. But others caused people to suffer.
lines.zh: 很久很久以前，有一位强大的国王。他的一些想法很开明，另一些却让人受苦。

lines.en: One of the king's ideas was a public arena as an agent of poetic justice. Crime was punished, or innocence was decided, by the result of chance. When a person was accused of a crime, his future would be judged in the public arena.
lines.zh: 国王的想法之一，是用一个公共竞技场来实现“天道报应”。罪行受到惩罚，还是清白得到确认，都由机会的结果来决定。一个人被指控犯罪时，他的命运就在这个公共竞技场里裁决。

lines.en: All the people would gather in this building. The king sat high up on his ceremonial chair. He gave a sign. A door under him opened. The accused person stepped out into the arena. Directly opposite the king were two doors. They were side by side, exactly alike. The person on trial had to walk directly to these doors and open one of them. He could open whichever door he pleased.
lines.zh: 所有人都会聚集在这座建筑里。国王高高坐在他的宝座上。他一示意，他脚下的一扇门就打开了，被告走进竞技场。正对着国王有两扇门，并排在一起，一模一样。受审的人必须径直走到这两扇门前，打开其中一扇。他想开哪扇都可以。

lines.en: If the accused man opened one door, out came a hungry tiger, the fiercest in the land. The tiger immediately jumped on him and tore him to pieces as punishment for his guilt. The case of the suspect was thus decided.
lines.zh: 如果被告打开的是其中一扇门，就会冲出一只饥饿的老虎，全国最凶猛的那只。老虎会立刻扑向他，把他撕成碎片，作为对他罪行的惩罚。嫌疑人的案子就这样判决了。

lines.en: Iron bells rang sadly. Great cries went up from the paid mourners. And the people, with heads hanging low and sad hearts, slowly made their way home. They mourned greatly that one so young and fair, or so old and respected, should have died this way.
lines.zh: 铁钟悲哀地敲响，雇来的哭丧人放声大哭，人们低着头，怀着悲伤的心，慢慢走回家。他们深深哀悼，一个如此年轻英俊、或如此年迈可敬的人，竟然这样死去。

lines.en: But, if the accused opened the other door, there came forth from it a woman, chosen especially for the person. To this lady he was immediately married, in honor of his innocence. It was not a problem that he might already have a wife and family, or that he might have chosen to marry another woman. The king permitted nothing to interfere with his great method of punishment and reward.
lines.zh: 但是，如果被告打开的是另一扇门，就会走出一位专门为他挑选的女子。为了表彰他的清白，他会立刻和这位女子结婚。他是否已有妻儿，或者他是否另有所爱，都无所谓。国王不允许任何事情干扰他这套伟大的赏罚办法。

lines.en: Another door opened under the king, and a clergyman, singers, dancers and musicians joined the man and the lady. The marriage ceremony was quickly completed. Then the bells made cheerful noises. The people shouted happily. And the innocent man led the new wife to his home, following children who threw flowers on their path.
lines.zh: 国王脚下的另一扇门打开，一位牧师、歌手、舞者和乐师们来到男子和女子身边。婚礼很快就完成了。接着钟声欢快地响起，人们高兴地欢呼。清白的男子领着新婚妻子回家，前面的孩子们往他们的路上撒着鲜花。

lines.en: This was the king's method of carrying out justice. Its fairness appeared perfect. The accused person could not know which door was hiding the lady. He opened either as he pleased, without having knowing whether, in the next minute, he was to be killed or married.
lines.zh: 这就是国王执行正义的方法。它看起来完全公平：被告不可能知道哪扇门后藏着美女。他随意打开一扇，根本不知道下一分钟自己是要被杀死还是要结婚。

lines.en: Sometimes the fierce animal came out of one door. Sometimes it came out of the other.
lines.zh: 有时猛兽从这扇门出来，有时从那扇门出来。

lines.en: This method was a popular one. When the people gathered together on one of the great trial days, they never knew whether they would see a bloody killing or a happy ending. So everyone was always interested. And the thinking part of the community would bring no charge of unfairness against this plan. Did not the accused person have the whole matter in his own hands?
lines.zh: 这个办法很受欢迎。在盛大的审判日聚在一起时，人们从不知道会看到一场血腥的杀戮还是一个圆满的结局，所以大家总是兴致勃勃。社会上有头脑的人也不会指责这个办法不公平——难道整件事不是掌握在被告自己手里吗？

lines.en: The king had a beautiful daughter who was like him in many ways. He loved her above all humanity. The princess secretly loved a young man who was the best-looking and bravest in the land. But he was a commoner, not part of an important family.
lines.zh: 国王有一个美丽的女儿，在很多方面都像他。他爱她胜过世上所有人。公主偷偷爱上了一个年轻人，他是全国最英俊、最勇敢的人，可他是个平民，不是出身名门。

lines.en: One day, the king discovered the relationship between his daughter and the young man. The man was immediately put in prison. A day was set for his trial in the king's public arena. This, of course, was an especially important event. Never before had a common subject been brave enough to love the daughter of the king.
lines.zh: 有一天，国王发现了女儿和这个年轻人的关系。年轻人立刻被关进监狱，国王定下日子，要在竞技场审判他。这当然是一件格外重大的事——从来没有哪个平民臣子敢爱上国王的女儿。

lines.en: The king knew that the young man would be punished, even if he opened the right door. And the king would take pleasure in watching the series of events, which would judge whether or not the man had done wrong in loving the princess.
lines.zh: 国王知道，即使年轻人打开了对的门，他也会受到惩罚。而国王会兴致勃勃地观看这一连串的事件，它们将裁决这个人爱上公主到底是不是错了。

lines.en: The day of the trial arrived. From far and near the people gathered in the arena and outside its walls. The king and his advisers were in their places, opposite the two doors. All was ready. The sign was given. The door under the king opened and the lover of the princess entered the arena.
lines.zh: 审判的日子到了。远近的人们都聚集到竞技场里和场外。国王和他的大臣们坐在各自的位置上，正对着那两扇门。一切准备就绪。信号发出，国王脚下的门打开，公主的情人走进了竞技场。

lines.en: Tall, beautiful and fair, his appearance was met with a sound of approval and tension. Half the people had not known so perfect a young man lived among them. No wonder the princess loved him! What a terrible thing for him to be there!
lines.zh: 他高大、英俊、白皙，他一出场，人群中就响起一阵赞叹又紧张的声音。一半的人都不知道他们当中竟有这样完美的年轻人。难怪公主会爱他！他站在那里，是多么可怕的事啊！

lines.en: As the young man entered the public arena, he turned to bend to the king. But he did not at all think of the great ruler. The young man's eyes instead were fixed on the princess, who sat to the right of her father.
lines.zh: 年轻人走进竞技场时，转身向国王鞠躬。可他心里根本没想着这位伟大的统治者。他的目光牢牢地盯着坐在父亲右边的公主。

lines.en: From the day it was decided that the sentence of her lover should be decided in the arena, she had thought of nothing but this event.
lines.zh: 自从决定在竞技场裁决她情人的命运那天起，她心里除了这件事，什么都没想过。

lines.en: The princess had more power, influence and force of character than anyone who had ever before been interested in such a case. She had done what no other person had done. She had possessed herself of the secret of the doors. She knew behind which door stood the tiger, and behind which waited the lady. Gold, and the power of a woman's will, had brought the secret to the princess.
lines.zh: 公主比以往任何关心此类案子的人都更有权力、影响力和魄力。她做到了别人从没做到的事：她掌握了两扇门的秘密。她知道哪扇门后站着老虎，哪扇门后等着美女。是金子和一个女人意志的力量，让公主得到了这个秘密。

lines.en: She also knew who the lady was. The lady was one of the loveliest in the kingdom. Now and then the princess had seen her looking at and talking to the young man.
lines.zh: 她还知道那位女子是谁。那是王国里最可爱的女子之一。公主不时看到她望着那个年轻人，跟他说话。

lines.en: The princess hated the woman behind that silent door. She hated her with all the intensity of the blood passed to her through long lines of cruel ancestors.
lines.zh: 公主恨那扇无声的门后的女人。她恨她，带着从一代代残忍祖先那里传下来的血液的全部强烈。

lines.en: Her lover turned to look at the princess. His eye met hers as she sat there, paler and whiter than anyone in the large ocean of tense faces around her. He saw that she knew behind which door waited the tiger, and behind which stood the lady. He had expected her to know it.
lines.zh: 她的情人转过头来看公主。他与她的目光相遇，她坐在那里，在周围一大片紧张的面孔中，脸色比谁都苍白。他看出她知道哪扇门后等着老虎，哪扇门后站着美女。他早料到她会知道。

lines.en: The only hope for the young man was based on the success of the princess in discovering this mystery. When he looked at her, he saw that she had been successful, as he knew she would succeed.
lines.zh: 年轻人唯一的希望，就寄托在公主能否成功探出这个秘密上。他看着她，就知道她成功了，正如他知道她一定会成功一样。

lines.en: Then his quick and tense look asked the question: "Which?" It was as clear to her as if he shouted it from where he stood. There was not time to be lost.
lines.zh: 接着，他用迅速而紧张的眼神问：“哪一扇？”这个问题对她来说清楚得就像他站在那里大声喊出来一样。一刻也不能耽误了。

lines.en: The princess raised her hand, and made a short, quick movement toward the right. No one but her lover saw it. Every eye but his was fixed on the man in the arena.
lines.zh: 公主抬起手，朝右边做了一个短促的小动作。除了她的情人，谁也没看见。除了他，每个人的眼睛都盯着竞技场里的那个人。

lines.en: He turned, and with a firm and quick step he walked across the empty space. Every heart stopped beating. Every breath was held. Every eye was fixed upon that man. He went to the door on the right and opened it.
lines.zh: 他转过身，迈着坚定而迅速的步子穿过空场。每颗心都停止了跳动，每个人都屏住了呼吸，每双眼睛都盯着那个人。他走到右边的门前，把它打开了。

lines.en: Now, the point of the story is this: Did the tiger come out of that door, or did the lady?
lines.zh: 那么，故事的关键是：从那扇门里出来的，是老虎，还是美女？

lines.en: The more we think about this question, the harder it is to answer. It involves a study of the human heart. Think of it not as if the decision of the question depended upon yourself. But as if it depended upon that hot-blooded princess, her soul at a white heat under the fires of sadness and jealousy. She had lost him, but who should have him?
lines.zh: 这个问题我们越想，就越难回答。它涉及对人心的研究。不要把它想成是由你自己来决定，而要想成是由那位热血的公主来决定——她的灵魂正在悲伤和嫉妒的烈火中烧得白热。她已经失去了他，可谁应该得到他呢？

lines.en: How often, in her waking hours and in her dreams, had she started in wild terror, and covered her face with her hands? She thought of her lover opening the door on the other side of which waited the sharp teeth of the tiger!
lines.zh: 有多少次，她醒着的时候、做梦的时候，惊恐万分地跳起来，用双手捂住脸？她想到她的情人打开那扇门，门的另一边是老虎锋利的牙齿！

lines.en: But how much oftener had she seen him open the other door? How had she ground her teeth, and torn her hair, when she had seen his happy face as he opened the door of the lady! How her soul had burned in pain when she had seen him run to meet that woman, with her look of victory. When she had seen the two of them get married. And when she had seen them walk away together upon their path of flowers, followed by the happy shouts of the crowd, in which her one sad cry was lost!
lines.zh: 可她又有多少次——次数多得多——看到他打开另一扇门？当她看到他打开美女那扇门时脸上幸福的表情，她是怎样咬牙切齿、撕扯头发！当她看到他奔向那个带着胜利神情的女人，看到他俩结婚，看到他俩踏上铺满鲜花的路一起离去，身后是人群欢快的呼喊，而她那一声悲哀的叫喊被淹没在其中——她的灵魂是怎样在痛苦中燃烧！

lines.en: Would it not be better for him to die quickly, and go to wait for her in that blessed place of the future? And yet, that tiger, those cries, that blood!
lines.zh: 让他快快死去，到那幸福的来世去等她，难道不更好吗？可是，那只老虎，那些惨叫，那些血！

lines.en: Her decision had been shown quickly. But it had been made after days and nights of thought. She had known she would be asked. And she had decided what she would answer. And she had moved her hand to the right.
lines.zh: 她的决定表现得很快，却是经过了几天几夜的思考才做出的。她知道他会问她，她已经决定了怎样回答。她把手指向了右边。

lines.en: The question of her decision is one not to be lightly considered. And it is not for me to set myself up as the one person able to answer it. And so I leave it with all of you:
lines.zh: 她做了怎样的决定，这个问题不能轻易下结论。我也不能自命为唯一能回答它的人。所以我把它留给你们每一个人：

lines.en: Which came out of the open door – the lady, or the tiger?
lines.zh: 从那扇打开的门里出来的——是美女，还是老虎？

qs.q: How did the king decide if someone was guilty?
opts: The person chose one of two doors.
qs.a: The person chose one of two doors.
qs.why: "The person on trial had to walk directly to these doors and open one of them."

qs.q: Why was the young man on trial?
qs.a: He loved the king's daughter.
qs.why: "Never before had a common subject been brave enough to love the daughter of the king."

qs.q: How does the story end?
opts: The writer lets the reader decide.
qs.a: The writer lets the reader decide.
qs.why: "And so I leave it with all of you."

lessons.title: A White Heron
lessons.by: Sarah Orne Jewett（萨拉·奥恩·朱厄特）
lessons.sum: 九岁的西尔维跟外婆住在佛蒙特的农场，熟悉森林里的每一只鸟。一位年轻的猎鸟人许诺：谁带他找到稀有的白鹭，就给十美元。西尔维爬上最高的松树，发现了白鹭的巢——可她该不该说出这个秘密？

lines.en: The forest was full of shadows as a little girl hurried through it one summer evening in June. It was already 8 o'clock and Sylvie wondered if her grandmother would be angry with her for being so late.
lines.zh: 六月的一个夏日傍晚，一个小女孩匆匆穿过树影重重的森林。已经八点了，西尔维不知道外婆会不会因为她回来这么晚而生气。

lines.en: Every evening Sylvie left her grandmother's house at 5:30 to bring their cow home. The old animal spent her days out in the open country eating sweet grass. It was Sylvie's job to bring her home to be milked. When the cow heard Sylvie's voice calling her, she would hide among the bushes.
lines.zh: 每天傍晚五点半，西尔维都从外婆家出发去把奶牛赶回来。这头老牛白天都在野地里吃甜甜的青草，西尔维的任务就是把它带回家挤奶。奶牛一听到西尔维喊它，就会躲进灌木丛里。

lines.en: This evening it had taken Sylvie longer than usual to find her cow. The child hurried the cow through the dark forest, following a narrow path that led to her grandmother's home. The cow stopped at a small stream to drink. As Sylvie waited, she put her bare feet in the cold, fresh water of the stream.
lines.zh: 这天傍晚，西尔维找奶牛花的时间比平常长。孩子赶着奶牛匆匆穿过黑暗的森林，沿着一条通往外婆家的小路走。奶牛在一条小溪边停下来喝水。西尔维等着的时候，把光脚伸进清凉的溪水里。

lines.en: She had never before been alone in the forest as late as this. The air was soft and sweet. Sylvie felt as if she were a part of the gray shadows and the silver leaves that moved in the evening breeze.
lines.zh: 她以前从没这么晚一个人待在森林里。空气柔和而香甜。西尔维觉得自己仿佛成了灰色树影和在晚风中摇曳的银色树叶的一部分。

lines.en: She began thinking how it was only a year ago that she came to her grandmother's farm. Before that, she had lived with her mother and father in a dirty, crowded factory town. One day, Sylvie's grandmother had visited them and had chosen Sylvie from all her brothers and sisters to be the one to help her on her farm in Vermont.
lines.zh: 她想起，一年前她才来到外婆的农场。在那之前，她和爸爸妈妈住在一个肮脏拥挤的工厂小镇。有一天，外婆来看他们，从她所有的兄弟姐妹中选了西尔维，让她到佛蒙特的农场帮忙。

lines.en: The cow finished drinking, and as the 9-year-old child hurried through the forest to the home she loved, she thought again about the noisy town where her parents still lived.
lines.zh: 奶牛喝完了水。这个九岁的孩子匆匆穿过森林，回到她热爱的家，一路上又想起了爸爸妈妈仍住着的那个吵闹的小镇。

lines.en: Suddenly the air was cut by a sharp whistle not far away. Sylvie knew it wasn't a friendly bird's whistle. It was the determined whistle of a person. She forgot the cow and hid in some bushes. But she was too late.
lines.zh: 突然，不远处一声尖锐的口哨划破了空气。西尔维知道那不是友善的鸟鸣，而是人吹的、毫不迟疑的口哨。她顾不上奶牛，躲进了灌木丛。可已经晚了。

lines.en: "Hello, little girl," a young man called out cheerfully. "How far is it to the main road?" Sylvie was trembling as she whispered "two miles." She came out of the bushes and looked up into the face of a tall young man carrying a gun.
lines.zh: “你好，小姑娘，”一个年轻人高高兴兴地喊道，“到大路还有多远？”西尔维发着抖，小声说：“两英里。”她从灌木丛里出来，抬头看到一个背着枪的高个子年轻人的脸。

lines.en: The stranger began walking with Sylvie as she followed her cow through the forest. "I've been hunting for birds," he explained, "but I've lost my way. Do you think I can spend the night at your house?" Sylvie didn't answer. She was glad they were almost home. She could see her grandmother standing near the door of the farm house.
lines.zh: 西尔维跟着奶牛穿过森林，陌生人和她一起走。“我在打鸟，”他解释说，“可我迷路了。你觉得我能在你家住一晚吗？”西尔维没回答。她很高兴快到家了，已经能看到外婆站在农舍门口。

lines.en: When they reached her, the stranger put down his gun and explained his problem to Sylvie's smiling grandmother.
lines.zh: 他们走到外婆跟前，陌生人放下枪，向笑眯眯的外婆说明了他的难处。

lines.en: "Of course you can stay with us," she said. "We don't have much, but you're welcome to share what we have. Now Sylvie, get a plate for the gentleman!"
lines.zh: “当然可以住我们这儿，”外婆说，“我们家东西不多，不过欢迎你跟我们一起吃。西尔维，给这位先生拿个盘子来！”

lines.en: After eating, they all sat outside. The young man explained he was a scientist, who collected birds. "Do you put them in a cage?" Sylvie asked. "No," he answered slowly, "I shoot them and stuff them with special chemicals to preserve them. I have over 100 different kinds of birds from all over the United States in my study at home."
lines.zh: 吃完饭，他们都坐在屋外。年轻人说他是个收集鸟类的科学家。“你把它们关在笼子里吗？”西尔维问。“不，”他慢慢地答道，“我把它们打下来，用特殊的化学药剂填充保存。我家书房里有一百多种来自美国各地的鸟。”

lines.en: "Sylvie knows a lot about birds, too," her grandmother said proudly. "She knows the forest so well, the wild animals come and eat bread right out of her hands."
lines.zh: “西尔维也很懂鸟。”外婆自豪地说，“她对森林熟得很，野生动物都会到她手里来吃面包。”

lines.en: "So Sylvie knows all about birds. Maybe she can help me then," the young man said. "I saw a white heron not far from here two days ago. I've been looking for it ever since. It's a very rare bird, the little white heron. Have you seen it, too?" he asked Sylvie.
lines.zh: “这么说西尔维对鸟无所不知。那她也许能帮我，”年轻人说，“两天前我在离这儿不远的地方看到一只白鹭。从那以后我就一直在找它。小白鹭是一种非常稀有的鸟。你也见过吗？”他问西尔维。

lines.en: But Sylvie was silent. "You would know it if you saw it," he added. "It's a tall, strange bird with soft white feathers and long thin legs. It probably has its nest at the top of a tall tree."
lines.zh: 可西尔维一声不吭。“你要是见过一定认得出，”他接着说，“那是一种又高又奇特的鸟，有柔软的白羽毛和细长的腿。它的巢大概在一棵高树的顶上。”

lines.en: Sylvie's heart began to beat fast. She knew that strange white bird! She had seen it on the other side of the forest. The young man was staring at Sylvie. "I would give $10 to the person who showed me where the white heron is."
lines.zh: 西尔维的心怦怦跳了起来。她认识那只奇特的白鸟！她在森林另一边见过它。年轻人盯着西尔维。“谁能告诉我白鹭在哪儿，我就给谁十美元。”

lines.en: That night Sylvie's dreams were full of all the wonderful things she and her grandmother could buy for ten dollars.
lines.zh: 那天晚上，西尔维梦见的全是她和外婆用十美元能买到的各种好东西。

lines.en: Sylvie spent the next day in the forest with the young man. He told her a lot about the birds they saw. Sylvie would have had a much better time if the young man had left his gun at home. She could not understand why he killed the birds he seemed to like so much. She felt her heart tremble every time he shot an unsuspecting bird as it was singing in the trees.
lines.zh: 第二天，西尔维跟着年轻人在森林里待了一整天。他给她讲了很多他们看到的鸟。要是年轻人没带枪，西尔维会玩得开心得多。她不明白，他明明那么喜欢这些鸟，为什么要打死它们。每当他开枪打下一只正在树上唱歌、毫无防备的鸟，她的心都在颤抖。

lines.en: But Sylvie watched the young man with eyes full of admiration. She had never seen anyone so handsome and charming. A strange excitement filled her heart, a new feeling the little girl did not recognize … love.
lines.zh: 可西尔维望着年轻人的眼里满是钦佩。她从没见过这么英俊迷人的人。一种奇异的激动充满了她的心，这是小女孩不认识的一种新感情……爱。

lines.en: At last evening came. They drove the cow home together. Long after the moon came out and the young man had fallen asleep Sylvie was still awake. She had a plan that would get the $10 for her grandmother and make the young man happy. When it was almost time for the sun to rise, she quietly left her house and hurried through the forest. She finally reached a huge pine tree, so tall it could be seen for many miles around. Her plan was to climb to the top of the pine tree. She could see the whole forest from there. She was sure she would be able to see where the white heron had hidden its nest.
lines.zh: 终于到了傍晚。他们一起把奶牛赶回家。月亮早已升起，年轻人早已睡着，西尔维却还醒着。她有一个计划，既能给外婆挣到十美元，又能让年轻人高兴。天快亮时，她悄悄出了门，匆匆穿过森林，终于来到一棵巨大的松树下。它高得方圆几英里都看得见。她的计划是爬到松树顶上。从那里能看到整片森林，她相信一定能看到白鹭把巢藏在哪儿。

lines.en: Sylvie's bare feet and tiny fingers grabbed the tree's rough trunk. Sharp dry branches scratched at her like cat's claws. The pine tree's sticky sap made her fingers feel stiff and clumsy as she climbed higher and higher.
lines.zh: 西尔维光着脚，用小手指抓住粗糙的树干。尖利的枯枝像猫爪一样划着她。她越爬越高，松树黏糊糊的树脂让她的手指变得僵硬笨拙。

lines.en: The pine tree seemed to grow taller, the higher that Sylvie climbed. The sky began to brighten in the east. Sylvie's face was like a pale star when, at last, she reached the tree's highest branch. The golden sun's rays hit the green forest. Two hawks flew together in slow-moving circles far below Sylvie. Sylvie felt as if she could go flying among the clouds, too. To the west she could see other farms and forests.
lines.zh: 西尔维爬得越高，松树好像就长得越高。东方的天空开始亮了。当她终于爬到最高的树枝上时，她的脸就像一颗苍白的星星。金色的阳光洒在绿色的森林上。两只鹰在西尔维脚下很远的地方一起慢慢盘旋。西尔维觉得自己也能飞到云彩中间去。往西，她能看到别的农场和森林。

lines.en: Suddenly Sylvie's dark gray eyes caught a flash of white that grew larger and larger. A bird with broad white wings and a long slender neck flew past Sylvie and landed on a pine branch below her. The white heron smoothed its feathers and called to its mate, sitting on their nest in a nearby tree. Then it lifted its wings and flew away.
lines.zh: 突然，西尔维深灰色的眼睛捕捉到一道白光，它越来越大。一只张着宽大白翅膀、长着细长脖子的鸟从西尔维身边飞过，落在她下面的一根松枝上。白鹭理了理羽毛，呼唤着正坐在附近一棵树上巢里的伴侣。然后它展开翅膀飞走了。

lines.en: Sylvie gave a long sigh. She knew the wild bird's secret now. Slowly she began her dangerous trip down the ancient pine tree. She did not dare to look down and tried to forget that her fingers hurt and her feet were bleeding. All she wanted to think about was what the stranger would say to her when she told him where to find the heron's nest.
lines.zh: 西尔维长长地叹了口气。现在她知道这只野鸟的秘密了。她开始慢慢地从这棵古老的松树上往下爬，这一路很危险。她不敢往下看，努力忘掉手指的疼和脚上的血。她心里只想着，等她告诉陌生人到哪里找白鹭的巢时，他会对她说什么。

lines.en: As Sylvie climbed slowly down the pine tree, the stranger was waking up back at the farm. He was smiling because he was sure from the way the shy little girl had looked at him that she had seen the white heron.
lines.zh: 西尔维慢慢爬下松树的时候，陌生人在农场里醒来了。他笑着，因为从这个害羞的小姑娘看他的眼神里，他确信她见过白鹭。

lines.en: About an hour later Sylvie appeared. Both her grandmother and the young man stood up as she came into the kitchen. The splendid moment to speak about her secret had come. But Sylvie was silent. Her grandmother was angry with her. Where had she been? The young man's kind eyes looked deeply into Sylvie's own dark gray ones. He could give Sylvie and her grandmother $10 dollars. He had promised to do this, and they needed the money. Besides, Sylvie wanted to make him happy.
lines.zh: 大约一小时后，西尔维出现了。她走进厨房时，外婆和年轻人都站了起来。说出秘密的美妙时刻到了。可西尔维一声不吭。外婆生她的气：她去哪儿了？年轻人那双和善的眼睛深深地望着西尔维深灰色的眼睛。他可以给西尔维和外婆十美元，他答应过的，而她们需要这笔钱。而且，西尔维也想让他高兴。

lines.en: But Sylvie was silent. She remembered how the white heron came flying through the golden air and how they watched the sun rise together from the top of the world. Sylvie could not speak. She could not tell the heron's secret and give its life away.
lines.zh: 可西尔维一声不吭。她想起白鹭穿过金色的空气飞来，想起她们一起在世界之巅看日出。西尔维说不出口。她不能说出白鹭的秘密，断送它的生命。

lines.en: The young man went away disappointed later that day. Sylvie was sad. She wanted to be his friend. He never returned. But many nights Sylvie heard the sound of his whistle as she came home with her grandmother's cow.
lines.zh: 那天晚些时候，年轻人失望地走了。西尔维很难过，她想做他的朋友。他再也没回来。可很多个夜晚，西尔维赶着外婆的奶牛回家时，都会听到他的口哨声。

lines.en: Were the birds better friends than their hunter might have been? Who can know?
lines.zh: 鸟儿们是不是比那个猎人更好的朋友呢？谁知道呢？

qs.q: What does the young man do?
qs.a: He shoots and collects birds.
qs.why: "I shoot them and stuff them with special chemicals to preserve them."

qs.q: Why did Sylvie climb the pine tree?
opts: to find the white heron's nest
to get away from the young man
qs.a: to find the white heron's nest
qs.why: "she would be able to see where the white heron had hidden its nest."

qs.q: What did Sylvie decide in the end?
opts: She left with the young man.
qs.a: She kept the heron's secret.
qs.why: "She could not tell the heron's secret and give its life away."

lessons.title: Doctor Heidegger's Experiment
lessons.sum: 古怪的海德格尔医生请四位潦倒的老朋友喝“青春泉水”。他们一杯杯喝下，重新变得年轻，却立刻重犯了年轻时的种种错误，为争夺寡妇大打出手。泉水洒了，青春也随之消失……

lines.en: We present the short story "Doctor Heidegger's Experiment" by Nathaniel Hawthorne. It has been adapted for English learners. Here is Barbara Klein with the story.
lines.zh: 我们为大家带来纳撒尼尔·霍桑的短篇小说《海德格尔医生的实验》，本故事为英语学习者改编。下面请芭芭拉·克莱因讲述。

lines.en: That very unusual man, old Doctor Heidegger, once invited four friends to meet him in his office. There were three white-bearded gentlemen, Mister Medbourne, Colonel Killigrew, and Mister Gascoigne. And, there was a thin old lady whose husband had died, so she was called the Widow Wycherly.
lines.zh: 那位非常不寻常的人——老海德格尔医生，有一次邀请四位朋友到他的诊室来。其中三位是白胡子的老先生：梅德伯恩先生、基利格鲁上校和加斯科因先生。还有一位瘦瘦的老太太，丈夫已经去世，所以人们叫她威彻利寡妇。

lines.en: They were all sad old creatures who had been unfortunate in life. As a young man, Mister Medbourne had lost all his money in a badly planned business deal. Colonel Killigrew had wasted his best years and health enjoying the pleasures of women and drink. Mister Gascoigne was a ruined politician with an evil past.
lines.zh: 他们都是一生不幸、可怜的老人。梅德伯恩先生年轻时在一笔策划不周的生意中赔光了所有钱。基利格鲁上校把最好的年华和健康都浪费在女色和酒上。加斯科因先生是个身败名裂的政客，过去劣迹斑斑。

lines.en: As for the Widow Wycherly, tradition tells us that she was once a great beauty. But shocking stories about her past had led the people of the town to reject her. So, she lived very much alone.
lines.zh: 至于威彻利寡妇，据说她曾是个大美人。可关于她过去的种种骇人传闻，让镇上的人都排斥她。所以她过着十分孤独的生活。

lines.en: It is worth stating that each of these three men were early lovers of the Widow Wycherly. And they had once been on the point of killing each other over her.
lines.zh: 值得一提的是，这三个男人当年都是威彻利寡妇的情人，还曾经为了她差点互相残杀。

lines.en: "My dear old friends," said Doctor Heidegger, "I would like your help in one of my little experiments." He motioned for them to sit down.
lines.zh: “我亲爱的老朋友们，”海德格尔医生说，“我想请你们帮我做一个小实验。”他示意他们坐下。

lines.en: Doctor Heidegger's office was a very strange place. The dark room was filled with books, cobwebs, and dust. An old mirror hanging between two bookcases was said to show the ghosts of all the doctor's dead patients.
lines.zh: 海德格尔医生的诊室是个非常奇怪的地方。昏暗的房间里堆满了书、蜘蛛网和灰尘。两个书柜之间挂着一面旧镜子，据说能照出医生所有死去病人的鬼魂。

lines.en: On another wall hung a painting of the young woman Doctor Heidegger was to have married long ago. But she died the night before their wedding after drinking one of the doctor's medicines. The most mysterious object in the room was a large book covered in black leather. It was said to be a book of magic.
lines.zh: 另一面墙上挂着一幅画，画的是海德格尔医生很久以前本要娶的年轻女子。可她在婚礼前一晚喝了医生的一种药，死了。屋里最神秘的东西是一本黑色皮面的大书，据说是一本魔法书。

lines.en: On the summer afternoon of our story, a black table stood in the middle of the room. On it was a beautiful cut-glass vase. Four glasses were also on the table.
lines.zh: 在我们这个故事发生的夏日午后，房间中央放着一张黑桌子，桌上有一只漂亮的雕花玻璃花瓶，还有四个玻璃杯。

lines.en: Doctor Heidegger was known for his unusual experiments. But his four guests did not expect anything very interesting.
lines.zh: 海德格尔医生以做奇怪的实验出名，可他的四位客人并不指望会有什么有趣的事。

lines.en: The doctor picked up his black leather book of magic. From its pages he removed a dried-up old rose.
lines.zh: 医生拿起那本黑色皮面的魔法书，从书页里取出一朵干枯的老玫瑰。

lines.en: "This rose," said the doctor, "was given to me fifty-five years ago by Sylvia Ward, whose painting hangs on this wall. I was to wear it at our wedding. Would you think it possible that this ancient rose could ever bloom again?"
lines.zh: “这朵玫瑰，”医生说，“是五十五年前西尔维娅·沃德送给我的，她的画像就挂在这面墙上。我本该在我们的婚礼上戴着它。你们觉得这朵古老的玫瑰有可能再开放吗？”

lines.en: "Nonsense!" said the Widow Wycherly with a toss of her head. "You might as well ask if an old woman's lined face could ever bloom again."
lines.zh: “胡说！”威彻利寡妇把头一甩，说，“你还不如问一个老太婆满是皱纹的脸能不能再像花一样绽放。”

lines.en: "See!" answered Doctor Heidegger.
lines.zh: “瞧！”海德格尔医生答道。

lines.en: He reached for the vase and threw the dried rose into the water it contained. Soon, a change began to appear. The crushed and dried petals moved and slowly turned from brown to red. And there was the rose of half a century looking as fresh as when Sylvia Ward had first given it to her lover.
lines.zh: 他伸手拿过花瓶，把干玫瑰扔进瓶里的水中。很快，变化出现了：压扁干枯的花瓣动了起来，慢慢从褐色变成红色。这朵半个世纪前的玫瑰，又像西尔维娅·沃德当初送给她情人时那样鲜艳了。

lines.en: "That is a very pretty trick," said the doctor's friends. "What is the secret?"
lines.zh: “这戏法真漂亮，”医生的朋友们说，“有什么秘诀？”

lines.en: "Did you ever hear of the Fountain of Youth?" asked Doctor Heidegger. "The Spanish explorer Ponce De Leon went in search of it centuries ago. But he was not looking in the right place. If I am rightly informed, the famous Fountain of Youth is in southern Florida. A friend of mine has sent me the water you see in the vase."
lines.zh: “你们听说过青春之泉吗？”海德格尔医生问，“几百年前，西班牙探险家庞塞·德莱昂去寻找过它，可他没找对地方。如果我的消息没错，著名的青春之泉在佛罗里达南部。我的一位朋友给我寄来了你们在花瓶里看到的这些水。”

lines.en: The doctor filled the four glasses with water from the Fountain of Youth. The liquid produced little bubbles that rose up to the silvery surface. The old guests agreed to drink the water, although they did not believe in its power.
lines.zh: 医生在四个杯子里倒满青春泉水。水里冒出小气泡，升到银色的水面上。老客人们同意喝这水，尽管他们并不相信它的魔力。

lines.en: "Before you drink, my friends," the doctor said, "you should draw up a few general rules as guidance before you pass a second time through the dangers of youth. You have had a lifetime of experience to direct you. Think what a shame it would be if the wisdom of your experiences did not act as a guide and teacher."
lines.zh: “喝之前，我的朋友们，”医生说，“在你们第二次经历青春的种种危险之前，应该先定几条总的规矩作为指导。你们有一辈子的经验来指引自己。想想看，如果你们的人生智慧不能成为向导和老师，那该多可惜。”

lines.en: The doctor's four friends answered him with a laugh. The idea that they would ever repeat the mistakes of their youth was very funny.
lines.zh: 医生的四位朋友笑着回答了他。认为他们会重犯年轻时的错误，这想法实在太好笑了。

lines.en: "Drink, then," said the doctor. "I am happy that I have so well chosen the subjects of my experiment."
lines.zh: “那就喝吧，”医生说，“我很高兴为我的实验选了这么合适的对象。”

lines.en: They raised the glasses to their lips. If the liquid really was magical, it could not have been given to four human beings who needed it more. They seemed as though they had never known youth or pleasure. They looked like they had always been the weak, unhappy creatures who were bent over the doctor's table.
lines.zh: 他们把杯子举到嘴边。如果这水真有魔力，那么世上再没有比这四个人更需要它的了。他们看上去仿佛从没有过青春和快乐，好像一直就是这些弯腰伏在医生桌前的虚弱、不幸的人。

lines.en: They drank the water.
lines.zh: 他们喝下了水。

lines.en: There was an almost immediate improvement among the guests. A cheerful glow like sunshine brightened their faces. They looked at one another imagining that some magic power had really started to smooth the lines on their faces.
lines.zh: 客人们几乎立刻就有了起色。一种阳光般愉快的光彩照亮了他们的脸。他们互相看着，想象着某种魔力真的开始抚平他们脸上的皱纹。

lines.en: "Quick! Give us more of this wondrous water!" they cried. "We are younger, but we are still too old!"
lines.zh: “快！再给我们一些这神奇的水！”他们喊道，“我们年轻了些，可还是太老了！”

lines.en: "Patience!" said Doctor Heidegger who watched the experiment with scientific coolness. "You have been a long time growing old. Surely you could wait half an hour to grow young!"
lines.zh: “耐心点！”海德格尔医生说，他以科学家的冷静观察着实验，“你们变老花了那么久，变年轻等半个小时总可以吧！”

lines.en: Again he filled their glasses. The four guests drank the liquid in one swallow. As the liquid passed down their throats it seemed to change their whole systems. Their eyes grew clear and bright. Their hair turned from silver to darker shades.
lines.zh: 他又倒满了他们的杯子。四位客人一口喝光。水流过喉咙，仿佛改变了他们全身。他们的眼睛变得清澈明亮，头发从银白变深了。

lines.en: "My dear widow, you are lovely!" cried Colonel Killigrew, who watched as the signs of age disappeared from her face.
lines.zh: “我亲爱的寡妇，你真可爱！”基利格鲁上校喊道，他看着衰老的痕迹从她脸上消失。

lines.en: The widow ran to the mirror.
lines.zh: 寡妇跑到镜子前。

lines.en: The three men started to behave in such a way that proved the magic of the Fountain of Youth's water.
lines.zh: 三个男人开始做出种种举动，证明了青春泉水的魔力。

lines.en: Mister Gascoigne's mind turned to political topics. He talked about nationalism and the rights of the people. He also told secrets softly to himself.
lines.zh: 加斯科因先生的心思转到了政治话题上。他谈论民族主义和人民的权利，还低声对自己说着秘密。

lines.en: All this time Colonel Killigrew had been shouting out happy drinking songs while his eyes turned towards the curvy body of the Widow Wycherly.
lines.zh: 这期间，基利格鲁上校一直在高唱欢快的饮酒歌，眼睛却瞟着威彻利寡妇曼妙的身材。

lines.en: Mister Medbourne was adding dollars and cents to pay for a proposed project. It would supply the East Indies with ice by linking a team of whales to the polar icebergs.
lines.zh: 梅德伯恩先生在算一个计划要花多少钱：用一队鲸鱼拖着极地冰山，给东印度群岛供应冰块。

lines.en: As for the Widow Wycherly, she stood in front of the mirror greeting her image as a friend she loved better than anything in the world.
lines.zh: 至于威彻利寡妇，她站在镜子前，向镜中的自己打招呼，就像对待世上她最爱的朋友。

lines.en: "My dear old doctor," she cried, "please give me another glass!"
lines.zh: “我亲爱的老医生，”她喊道，“请再给我一杯！”

lines.en: The doctor had already filled the glasses again. It was now near sunset and the room was darker than ever. But a moon-like light shined from within the vase. The doctor sat in his chair watching. As the four guests drank their third glass of water, they were silenced by the expression on the doctor's mysterious face.
lines.zh: 医生已经又把杯子倒满了。这时已近日落，房间比任何时候都暗。可花瓶里透出一道月光般的光。医生坐在椅子上看着。四位客人喝第三杯水时，医生脸上神秘的表情让他们安静了下来。

lines.en: The next moment, the exciting rush of young life shot through their blood. They were now at the happy height of youth. The endless cares, sadness, and diseases of age were remembered only as a troubled dream from which they had awoken.
lines.zh: 下一刻，年轻生命那令人激动的热流涌遍了他们的血液。他们正处在青春最美好的巅峰。老年无尽的忧虑、悲伤和疾病，只像一场刚刚醒来的噩梦般留在记忆里。

lines.en: "We are young!" they cried.
lines.zh: “我们年轻了！”他们喊道。

lines.en: The guests were a group of happy youngsters almost crazy with energy. They laughed at the old-fashioned clothing they wore. They shouted happily and jumped around the room.
lines.zh: 客人们成了一群快乐的年轻人，精力旺盛得几乎发了疯。他们嘲笑自己身上的老式衣服，高兴地大叫，在屋里蹦来蹦去。

lines.en: The Widow Wycherly - if such a young lady could be called a widow - ran to the doctor's chair and asked him to dance.
lines.zh: 威彻利寡妇——如果这样一位年轻小姐还能叫寡妇的话——跑到医生的椅子前，请他跳舞。

lines.en: "Please excuse me," answered the doctor quietly. "My dancing days were over long ago. But these three young men would be happy to have such a lovely partner."
lines.zh: “请原谅，”医生平静地答道，“我跳舞的日子早就过去了。不过这三位年轻人一定很乐意有这样一位可爱的舞伴。”

lines.en: The men began to argue violently about who would dance with her. They gathered around the widow, each grabbing for her.
lines.zh: 男人们开始激烈地争吵谁来和她跳舞。他们围着寡妇，每个人都去抓她。

lines.en: Yet, by a strange trick owing to the darkness of the room, the tall mirror is said to have reflected the forms of three old, gray men competing for a faded, old woman.
lines.zh: 然而，据说由于房间昏暗而产生的一个奇怪的错觉，那面高大的镜子里映出的，是三个灰白的老头在争夺一个憔悴的老太婆。

lines.en: As the three fought for the woman's favor, they reached violently for each other's throats. In their struggle, they turned over the table. The vase broke into a thousand pieces. The Water of Youth flowed in a bright stream across the floor.
lines.zh: 三个人为了赢得女人的青睐，凶狠地互相掐住喉咙。扭打中，他们掀翻了桌子。花瓶摔成了千万片碎片，青春泉水在地板上流成一道发亮的小溪。

lines.en: The guests stood still. A strange coldness was slowly stealing over them all. They looked at Doctor Heidegger who was holding his treasured rose. The flower was fading and drying up once more.
lines.zh: 客人们站住不动了。一股奇怪的寒意慢慢地爬上他们全身。他们看着海德格尔医生，他手里拿着他珍爱的那朵玫瑰。那朵花又在凋谢、干枯。

lines.en: The guests looked at each other and saw their looks changing back. "Are we grown old again so soon?" they cried.
lines.zh: 客人们互相看着，发现彼此的容貌正在变回原样。“我们这么快又变老了吗？”他们喊道。

lines.en: In truth they had. The Water of Youth had powers that were only temporary.
lines.zh: 确实如此。青春泉水的魔力只是暂时的。

lines.en: "Yes, friends, you are old again," the doctor said. "And the Water of Youth lies wasted on the ground. But even if it flowed in a river at my door, I still would not drink it. This is the lesson you have taught me!"
lines.zh: “是的，朋友们，你们又老了，”医生说，“青春泉水也白白洒在了地上。可就算它在我门前流成一条河，我也不会喝。这就是你们给我上的一课！”

lines.en: But the doctor's four friends had learned no such lesson. They decided at that moment to travel to Florida and drink morning, noon, and night from the Fountain of Youth.
lines.zh: 可医生的四位朋友并没有学到这样的教训。他们当场决定去佛罗里达，从早到晚地喝青春之泉的水。

qs.q: What did the water do to the old rose?
opts: It made the rose fresh again.
qs.a: It made the rose fresh again.
qs.why: "the rose of half a century looking as fresh as when Sylvia Ward had first given it."

qs.q: What did the guests do when they were young again?
opts: They repeated the mistakes of their youth.
qs.a: They repeated the mistakes of their youth.
qs.why: 他们又为寡妇争吵打架。

qs.q: What did the doctor learn?
opts: He would not drink the water even if he could.
qs.a: He would not drink the water even if he could.
qs.why: "I still would not drink it."

gloss: 青春之泉（传说中能使人返老还童的泉水）

lessons.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
lessons.sum: 纽约州的“睡谷”流传着无头骑士的传说。瘦高的乡村教师伊卡博德·克兰想娶富农的女儿卡特琳娜，和强壮的布罗姆成了情敌。一次舞会后，伊卡博德独自骑马回家，在桥边遇到了无头骑士……第二天只留下一顶帽子和一个摔碎的南瓜。

lines.en: Today's story is called "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow. It is about something strange that happened long ago in a valley called "Sleepy Hollow." It was written by Washington Irving. The story is told by Doug Johnson.
lines.zh: 今天的故事叫《睡谷传说》，讲的是很久以前在一个叫“睡谷”的山谷里发生的一件怪事。作者是华盛顿·欧文，由道格·约翰逊讲述。

lines.en: The valley known as Sleepy Hollow hides from the world in the high hills of New York state. There are many stories told about the quiet valley. But the story that people believe most is about a man who rides a horse at night. The story says the man died many years ago during the American Revolutionary War. His head was shot off. Every night he rises from his burial place, jumps on his horse and rides through the valley looking for his lost head.
lines.zh: 那个叫睡谷的山谷藏在纽约州的高山之间，与世隔绝。关于这个宁静的山谷有很多传说，但人们最相信的，是一个夜里骑马的人的故事。传说这个人多年前死于美国独立战争，他的头被炮弹打掉了。每天夜里，他从坟墓里起来，跳上马，在山谷里奔驰，寻找他丢失的脑袋。

lines.en: Near Sleepy Hollow is a village called Tarry Town. It was settled many years ago by people from Holland. The village had a small school. And one teacher, named Ichabod Crane. Ichabod Crane was a good name for him, because he looked like a tall bird, a crane. He was tall and thin like a crane. His shoulders were small, joined two long arms. His head was small, too, and flat on top. He had big ears, large glassy green eyes and a long nose.
lines.zh: 睡谷附近有个村子叫塔里镇，是很多年前荷兰人建起来的。村里有一所小学校，只有一位老师，名叫伊卡博德·克兰。“克兰”这个名字对他再合适不过，因为他长得就像一只高个子的鸟——鹤（crane）。他像鹤一样又高又瘦，窄窄的肩膀连着两条长胳膊。他的头也很小，头顶是平的。他长着一对大耳朵、一双玻璃似的绿色大眼睛和一个长鼻子。

lines.en: Ichabod did not make much money as a teacher. And although he was tall and thin, he ate like a fat man. To help him pay for his food he earned extra money teaching young people to sing. Every Sunday after church Ichabod taught singing.
lines.zh: 伊卡博德当老师挣不了多少钱。而且他虽然又高又瘦，饭量却像个胖子。为了挣饭钱，他还教年轻人唱歌，额外挣点钱。每个星期天做完礼拜，伊卡博德都教人唱歌。

lines.en: Among the ladies Ichabod taught was one Katrina Van Tassel. She was the only daughter of a rich Dutch farmer. She was a girl in bloom…much like a round red, rosy apple. Ichabod had a soft and foolish heart for the ladies, and soon found himself interested in Miss Van Tassel.
lines.zh: 他教的女士当中有一位卡特琳娜·范塔塞尔，她是一位富有的荷兰农场主的独生女。她正当妙龄……就像一只圆圆的、红扑扑的苹果。伊卡博德对女士们心肠又软又傻，很快就对范塔塞尔小姐动了心。

lines.en: Ichabod's eyes opened wide when he saw the riches of Katrina's farm: the miles of apple trees and wheat fields, and hundreds of fat farm animals. He saw himself as master of the Van Tassel farm with Katrina as his wife.
lines.zh: 伊卡博德看到卡特琳娜家农场的财富时，眼睛都瞪大了：绵延数英里的苹果树和麦田，几百头肥壮的牲畜。他想象自己成了范塔塞尔农场的主人，卡特琳娜成了他的妻子。

lines.en: But there were many problems blocking the road to Katrina's heart. One was a strong young man named Brom Van Brunt. Brom was a hero to all the young ladies. His shoulders were big. His back was wide. And his hair was short and curly. He always won the horse races in Tarry Town and earned many prizes. Brom was never seen without a horse.
lines.zh: 可是通往卡特琳娜芳心的路上障碍重重。其中之一是一个叫布罗姆·范布伦特的强壮年轻人。布罗姆是所有年轻姑娘心中的英雄。他肩膀宽大，后背宽阔，头发又短又卷。他总是赢得塔里镇的赛马，拿了很多奖。人们从没见过布罗姆离开马。

lines.en: Sometimes late at night Brom and his friends would rush through town shouting loudly from the backs of their horses. Tired old ladies would awaken from their sleep and say: "Why, there goes Brom Van Brunt leading his wild group again!"
lines.zh: 有时深夜，布罗姆和他的朋友们骑着马冲过镇子，在马背上大声叫嚷。疲惫的老太太们从睡梦中被吵醒，说：“哎，又是布罗姆·范布伦特带着他那帮野小子！”

lines.en: Such was the enemy Ichabod had to defeat for Katrina's heart.
lines.zh: 这就是伊卡博德为了赢得卡特琳娜的心必须打败的对手。

lines.en: Stronger and wiser men would not have tried. But Ichabod had a plan. He could not fight his enemy in the open. So he did it silently and secretly. He made many visits to Katrina's farm and made her think he was helping her to sing better.
lines.zh: 比他更强壮、更聪明的人都不会去试。可伊卡博德有个计划。他不能和对手公开较量，所以就悄悄地、偷偷地进行。他多次去卡特琳娜家的农场，让她以为他是在帮她把歌唱得更好。

lines.en: Time passed, and the town people thought Ichabod was winning. Brom's horse was never seen at Katrina's house on Sunday nights anymore.
lines.zh: 时间一天天过去，镇上的人都以为伊卡博德要赢了。星期天晚上再也看不到布罗姆的马出现在卡特琳娜家门口了。

lines.en: One day in autumn Ichabod was asked to come to a big party at the Van Tassel home. He dressed in his best clothes. A farmer loaned him an old horse for the long trip to the party.
lines.zh: 秋天的一天，伊卡博德被邀请去范塔塞尔家参加一个盛大的聚会。他穿上了最好的衣服。一个农民借给他一匹老马，让他骑着走那段长路去参加聚会。

lines.en: The house was filled with farmers and their wives, red-faced daughters and clean, washed sons. The tables were filled with different things to eat. Wine filled many glasses.
lines.zh: 屋里挤满了农民和他们的妻子、红脸蛋的女儿和洗得干干净净的儿子。桌上摆满了各种吃的，许多杯子里斟满了酒。

lines.en: Brom Van Brunt rode to the party on his fastest horse called Daredevil. All the young ladies smiled happily when they saw him. Soon music filled the rooms and everyone began to dance and sing.
lines.zh: 布罗姆·范布伦特骑着他最快的马“冒失鬼”来参加聚会。年轻姑娘们一看到他都开心地笑了。很快，音乐响彻屋子，大家开始跳舞唱歌。

lines.en: Ichabod was happy dancing with Katrina as Brom looked at them with a jealous heart. The night passed. The music stopped, and the young people sat together to tell stories about the revolutionary war.
lines.zh: 伊卡博德和卡特琳娜跳舞跳得很开心，布罗姆嫉妒地看着他们。夜深了，音乐停了，年轻人坐在一起讲独立战争的故事。

lines.en: Soon stories about Sleepy Hollow were told. The most feared story was about the rider looking for his lost head. One farmer told how he raced the headless man on a horse. The farmer ran his horse faster and faster. The horseman followed over bush and stone until they came to the end of the valley. There the headless horseman suddenly stopped. Gone were his clothes and his skin. All that was left was a man with white bones shining in the moonlight.
lines.zh: 很快大家讲起了睡谷的故事。最吓人的就是那个寻找丢失脑袋的骑士。一个农民讲他怎样和骑马的无头人赛跑。农民催马越跑越快，骑士翻过灌木、越过石头紧追不舍，一直追到山谷尽头。在那里，无头骑士突然停了下来。他的衣服和皮肉都不见了，只剩下一副白骨在月光下闪闪发亮。

lines.en: The stories ended and time came to leave the party. Ichabod seemed very happy until he said goodnight to Katrina. Was she ending their romance? He left feeling very sad. Had Katrina been seeing Ichabod just to make Brom Van Brunt jealous so he would marry her?
lines.zh: 故事讲完了，该离开聚会了。伊卡博德一直很开心，直到他跟卡特琳娜道晚安。她是要结束他们的恋情吗？他离开时很难过。难道卡特琳娜和伊卡博德来往，只是为了让布罗姆·范布伦特吃醋，好让他娶她？

lines.en: Well, Ichabod began his long ride home on the hills that surround Tarry Town. He had never felt so lonely in his life. He began to whistle as he came close to the tree where a man had been killed years ago by rebels.
lines.zh: 就这样，伊卡博德骑马走上环绕塔里镇的山路，开始了漫长的回家之路。他这辈子从没这么孤独过。快走到那棵多年前有人被义军杀死的树旁时，他开始吹口哨。

lines.en: He thought he saw something white move in the tree. But no, it was only the moonlight shining and moving on the tree. Then he heard a noise. His body shook. He kicked his horse faster. The old horse tried to run, but almost fell in the river, instead. Ichabod hit the horse again. The horse ran fast and then suddenly stopped, almost throwing Ichabod forward to the ground.
lines.zh: 他好像看到树上有个白色的东西在动。可不，那只是月光在树上闪动。接着他听到一个声音，浑身发抖。他踢马让它跑快点。老马想跑，却差点掉进河里。伊卡博德又抽了马一下。马飞跑起来，又突然停住，差点把伊卡博德往前甩到地上。

lines.en: There, in the dark woods on the side of the river where the bushes grow low, stood an ugly thing. Big and black. It did not move, but seemed ready to jump like a giant monster.
lines.zh: 就在那里，河边灌木低矮的黑暗树林中，站着一个丑陋的东西，又大又黑。它不动，却像一个巨大的怪物随时准备扑过来。

lines.en: Ichabod's hair stood straight up. It was too late to run, and in his fear, he did the only thing he could. His shaking voice broke the silent valley.
lines.zh: 伊卡博德头发都竖了起来。想跑已经来不及了，惊恐之中，他做了唯一能做的事：他颤抖的声音打破了山谷的寂静。

lines.en: "Who are you?" The thing did not answer. Ichabod asked again. Still no answer. Ichabod's old horse began to move forward. The black thing began to move along the side of Ichabod's horse in the dark. Ichabod made his horse run faster. The black thing moved with them. Side by side they moved, slowly at first. And not a word was said.
lines.zh: “你是谁？”那东西没回答。伊卡博德又问了一遍，还是没回答。伊卡博德的老马开始往前走，那黑东西也在黑暗中沿着马的一侧移动。伊卡博德催马快跑，那黑东西也跟着他们。他们并排前进，起初很慢，谁也没说一句话。

lines.en: Ichabod felt his heart sink. Up a hill they moved above the shadow of the trees. For a moment the moon shown down and to Ichabod's horror he saw it was a horse. And it had a rider. But the rider's head was not on his body. It was in front of the rider, resting on the horse.
lines.zh: 伊卡博德的心一沉。他们爬上一座小山，走出了树影。月光一下子洒下来，伊卡博德惊恐地看到那是一匹马，马上有个骑士。可骑士的脑袋不在身上——而是放在他身前，搁在马背上。

lines.en: Ichabod kicked and hit his old horse with all his power. Away they rushed through bushes and trees across the valley of Sleepy Hollow. Up ahead was the old church bridge where the headless horseman stops and returns to his burial place.
lines.zh: 伊卡博德使出全身力气踢打他的老马。他们冲过灌木和树林，穿过睡谷。前面就是古老的教堂桥，据说无头骑士到了那里就会停下，回到他的坟墓。

lines.en: "If only I can get there first, I am safe," thought Ichabod. He kicked his horse again. The horse jumped on to the bridge and raced over it like the sound of thunder. Ichabod looked back to see if the headless man had stopped. He saw the man pick up his head and throw it with a powerful force. The head hit Ichabod in the face and knocked him off his horse to the dirt below.
lines.zh: “只要我能先到那儿，我就安全了。”伊卡博德想。他又踢了一下马。马跳上桥，像雷鸣一样冲了过去。伊卡博德回头看无头人有没有停下。他看到那人拿起自己的脑袋，用力扔了过来。那颗头打中伊卡博德的脸，把他从马上打落到下面的泥地里。

lines.en: They found Ichabod's horse the next day peacefully eating grass. They could not find Ichabod.
lines.zh: 第二天，人们发现伊卡博德的马在悠闲地吃草，却找不到伊卡博德。

lines.en: They walked all across the valley. They saw the foot marks of Ichabod's horse as it had raced through the valley. They even found Ichabod's old hat in the dust near the bridge. But they did not find Ichabod. The only other thing they found was lying near Ichabod's hat.
lines.zh: 他们走遍了整个山谷，看到伊卡博德的马在山谷里飞奔留下的蹄印，甚至在桥边的尘土里找到了伊卡博德的旧帽子。可他们没找到伊卡博德。他们找到的唯一别的东西，就在伊卡博德的帽子旁边。

lines.en: It was the broken pieces of a round orange pumpkin.
lines.zh: 那是一个摔碎了的橙色圆南瓜。

lines.en: The town people talked about Ichabod for many weeks. They remembered the frightening stories of the valley. And finally they came to believe that the headless horseman had carried Ichabod away.
lines.zh: 镇上的人议论了伊卡博德好几个星期。他们想起山谷里那些吓人的故事，最后终于相信是无头骑士把伊卡博德带走了。

lines.en: Much later an old farmer returned from a visit to New York City. He said he was sure he saw Ichabod there. He thought Ichabod silently left Sleepy Hollow because he had lost Katrina.
lines.zh: 很久以后，一个老农民从纽约城回来，说他肯定在那里见到了伊卡博德。他认为伊卡博德是因为失去了卡特琳娜，才悄悄离开睡谷的。

lines.en: As for Katrina, her mother and father gave her a big wedding when she married Brom Van Brunt. Many people who went to the wedding saw that Brom smiled whenever Ichabod's name was spoken. And they wondered why he laughed out loud when anyone talked about the broken orange pumpkin found lying near Ichabod's old dusty hat.
lines.zh: 至于卡特琳娜，她嫁给布罗姆·范布伦特时，父母为她办了一场盛大的婚礼。许多参加婚礼的人发现，每当有人提起伊卡博德的名字，布罗姆就会微笑。人们也纳闷，为什么只要有人说起伊卡博德那顶落满灰尘的旧帽子旁边那个摔碎的橙色南瓜，他就会哈哈大笑。

qs.q: What is the headless horseman looking for?
qs.a: his lost head
qs.why: "rides through the valley looking for his lost head."

qs.q: Why did Ichabod want to marry Katrina?
opts: He loved her and wanted her family's rich farm.
qs.a: He loved her and wanted her family's rich farm.
qs.why: "He saw himself as master of the Van Tassel farm."

qs.q: What was found near Ichabod's hat?
qs.a: a broken pumpkin
qs.why: "the broken pieces of a round orange pumpkin."

gloss: 埋葬；（此处 burial place）坟墓
起义者（此处指独立战争中的美国义军）

lessons.title: The Tell-Tale Heart
lessons.sum: 爱伦·坡的经典心理恐怖小说。叙述者坚称自己没有疯，却因为受不了老人那只“秃鹫般的眼睛”而杀了他，把尸体藏在地板下。警察来调查时，他耳边响起越来越大的心跳声……

lines.en: Today we present the short story "The Tell-Tale Heart" by Edgar Allan Poe. Here is Shep O'Neal with the story.
lines.zh: 今天我们为大家带来爱伦·坡的短篇小说《泄密的心》。下面请谢普·奥尼尔讲述。

lines.en: True! Nervous -- very, very nervous I had been and am! But why will you say that I am mad? The disease had sharpened my senses -- not destroyed them.
lines.zh: 没错！紧张——我以前非常、非常紧张，现在也是！可你们为什么要说我疯了？这病让我的感官更敏锐了——并没有毁掉它们。

lines.en: Above all was the sense of hearing. I heard all things in the heaven and in the earth. I heard many things in the underworld. How, then, am I mad? Observe how healthily -- how calmly I can tell you the whole story.
lines.zh: 最敏锐的是听觉。天上地下的一切我都听得见，阴间的许多事我也听得见。那我怎么会疯呢？听着，我能多么清醒地——多么冷静地——把整个故事讲给你们听。

lines.en: It is impossible to say how first the idea entered my brain. I loved the old man. He had never wronged me. He had never given me insult. For his gold I had no desire. I think it was his eye! Yes, it was this! He had the eye of a bird, a vulture -- a pale blue eye, with a film over it. Whenever it fell on me, my blood ran cold; and so -- very slowly -- I made up my mind to take the life of the old man, and free myself of the eye forever.
lines.zh: 我说不清这个念头最初是怎么钻进我脑子里的。我爱那个老人。他从没亏待过我，从没侮辱过我。我也不贪图他的金子。我想是因为他的眼睛！对，就是它！他长着一只鸟的眼睛，秃鹫的眼睛——一只浅蓝色的、蒙着一层膜的眼睛。每当它落到我身上，我的血就发冷。于是——非常缓慢地——我下定决心要了老人的命，永远摆脱那只眼睛。

lines.en: Now this is the point. You think that I am mad. Madmen know nothing. But you should have seen me. You should have seen how wisely and carefully I went to work!
lines.zh: 关键就在这里。你们以为我疯了。疯子什么都不懂。可你们真该看看我，看看我干活时是多么聪明、多么小心！

lines.en: I was never kinder to the old man than during the whole week before I killed him. And every night, late at night, I turned the lock of his door and opened it – oh, so gently! And then, when I had made an opening big enough for my head, I put in a dark lantern, all closed that no light shone out, and then I stuck in my head. I moved it slowly, very slowly, so that I might not interfere with the old man's sleep. And then, when my head was well in the room, I undid the lantern just so much that a single thin ray of light fell upon the vulture eye.
lines.zh: 杀他之前的那整整一星期，我对老人比任何时候都好。每天夜里，深夜，我转动他门上的锁，把门打开——哦，那么轻！等打开的缝够伸进我的头了，我先伸进一盏遮得严严实实、一点光也不透的提灯，然后再把头伸进去。我慢慢地、非常慢地移动，免得惊扰老人的睡眠。等我的头完全进了房间，我把提灯打开一点点，刚好让一缕细细的光落在那只秃鹫眼上。

lines.en: And this I did for seven long nights -- but I found the eye always closed; and so it was impossible to do the work; for it was not the old man who was a problem for me, but his Evil Eye.
lines.zh: 我这样做了整整七个漫长的夜晚——可那只眼睛总是闭着，所以没法动手。因为让我难受的不是老人，而是他那只邪恶的眼睛。

lines.en: On the eighth night, I was more than usually careful in opening the door. I had my head in and was about to open the lantern, when my finger slid on a piece of metal and made a noise. The old man sat up in bed, crying out "Who's there?"
lines.zh: 第八个晚上，我开门时比平常更加小心。我的头已经伸进去了，正要打开提灯，手指却在一块金属上滑了一下，发出了声响。老人在床上坐了起来，喊道：“谁在那儿？”

lines.en: I kept still and said nothing. I did not move a muscle for a whole hour. During that time, I did not hear him lie down. He was still sitting up in the bed listening -- just as I have done, night after night.
lines.zh: 我一动不动，什么也没说。整整一个小时，我连一块肌肉都没动。这期间，我没听见他躺下。他还坐在床上听着——就像我一夜又一夜所做的那样。

lines.en: Then I heard a noise, and I knew it was the sound of human terror. It was the low sound that arises from the bottom of the soul. I knew the sound well. Many a night, late at night, when all the world slept, it has welled up from deep within my own chest. I say I knew it well.
lines.zh: 接着我听到一个声音，我知道那是人在恐惧中发出的声音。那是从灵魂深处升起的低沉声音。我太熟悉这声音了。多少个深夜，全世界都睡着时，它也曾从我自己的胸口深处涌上来。我说，我太熟悉它了。

lines.en: I knew what the old man felt, and felt sorry for him, although I laughed to myself. I knew that he had been lying awake ever since the first noise, when he had turned in the bed. His fears had been ever since growing upon him.
lines.zh: 我知道老人的感受，也替他难过，尽管我心里在暗笑。我知道，自从第一声响动、他在床上翻身起，他就一直醒着躺在那里，恐惧一直在他心里越积越多。

lines.en: When I had waited a long time, without hearing him lie down, I decided to open a little -- a very, very little -- crack in the lantern. So I opened it. You cannot imagine how carefully, carefully. Finally, a single ray of light shot from out and fell full upon the vulture eye.
lines.zh: 我等了很久，没听见他躺下，就决定把提灯打开一条小缝——非常、非常小的一条缝。于是我打开了。你们想象不到我有多小心、多小心。终于，一缕光射了出去，正好落在那只秃鹫眼上。

lines.en: It was open -- wide, wide open -- and I grew angry as I looked at it. I saw it clearly -- all a dull blue, with a horrible veil over it that chilled my bones; but I could see nothing else of the old man's face or person. For I had directed the light exactly upon the damned spot.
lines.zh: 它睁着——睁得大大的——我看着它，怒火中烧。我看得清清楚楚——一片暗淡的蓝色，上面蒙着一层可怕的膜，让我寒彻骨髓。可老人的脸和身体别的部分我什么也看不见，因为我把光正好对准了那个可恶的地方。

lines.en: And have I not told you that what you mistake for madness is but a kind of over-sensitivity? Now, there came to my ears a low, dull, quick sound, such as a watch makes when inside a piece of cotton. I knew that sound well, too. It was the beating of the old man's heart. It increased my anger.
lines.zh: 我不是跟你们说过吗？你们误以为是疯狂的东西，只不过是一种过度的敏感。这时，我耳边传来一个低沉、沉闷、急促的声音，就像一块表裹在棉花里发出的声音。这声音我也很熟悉。那是老人的心跳声。它让我更加愤怒。

lines.en: But even yet I kept still. I hardly breathed. I held the lantern motionless. I attempted to keep the ray of light upon the eye. But the beating of the heart increased. It grew quicker and quicker, and louder and louder every second. The old man's terror must have been extreme! The beating grew louder, I say, louder every moment!
lines.zh: 可我仍然一动不动，几乎不敢呼吸。我握着提灯纹丝不动，努力让那道光一直照在眼睛上。可心跳声越来越大，每一秒都更快、更响。老人一定害怕到了极点！我说，心跳声越来越响，每时每刻都更响！

lines.en: And now at the dead hour of the night, in the horrible silence of that old house, so strange a noise as this excited me to uncontrollable terror. Yet, for some minutes longer I stood still. But the beating grew louder, louder! I thought the heart must burst.
lines.zh: 此刻正是死一般寂静的深夜，在那座老房子可怕的寂静中，这样奇怪的声音让我陷入了无法控制的恐惧。可我又一动不动地站了几分钟。心跳声却越来越响，越来越响！我以为那颗心一定要炸开了。

lines.en: And now a new fear seized me -- the sound would be heard by a neighbor! The old man's hour had come! With a loud shout, I threw open the lantern and burst into the room.
lines.zh: 这时一种新的恐惧抓住了我——邻居会听见这声音的！老人的末日到了！我大喊一声，猛地打开提灯，冲进了房间。

lines.en: He cried once -- once only. Without delay, I forced him to the floor, and pulled the heavy bed over him. I then smiled, to find the action so far done.
lines.zh: 他只叫了一声——只有一声。我立刻把他按倒在地，把沉重的床拖过来压在他身上。看到事情进展到这一步，我笑了。

lines.en: But, for many minutes, the heart beat on with a quiet sound. This, however, did not concern me; it would not be heard through the wall. At length, it stopped. The old man was dead. I removed the bed and examined the body. I placed my hand over his heart and held it there many minutes. There was no movement. He was stone dead. His eye would trouble me no more.
lines.zh: 可是好几分钟里，那颗心仍在轻轻地跳。不过这并不让我担心，隔着墙是听不见的。最后，它停了。老人死了。我把床挪开，检查了尸体。我把手放在他心口，按了好几分钟，没有任何跳动。他死透了。他的眼睛再也不会折磨我了。

lines.en: If still you think me mad, you will think so no longer when I describe the wise steps I took for hiding the body. I worked quickly, but in silence. First of all, I took apart the body. I cut off the head and the arms and the legs.
lines.zh: 如果你们还认为我疯了，等我讲完我为藏尸采取的聪明步骤，你们就不会这么想了。我干得很快，但悄无声息。首先，我把尸体肢解了。

lines.en: I then took up three pieces of wood from the flooring, and placed his body parts under the room. I then replaced the wooden boards so well that no human eye -- not even his -- could have seen anything wrong.
lines.zh: 然后我撬起三块地板，把尸块放到房间地板下面，再把木板装回去，装得那么好，任何人的眼睛——连他的眼睛也算上——都看不出任何异样。

lines.en: There was nothing to wash out -- no mark of any kind -- no blood whatever. I had been too smart for that. A tub had caught all -- ha! ha!
lines.zh: 没什么需要清洗的——没有任何痕迹——一滴血也没有。我太聪明了，早就想到了。一只桶接住了一切——哈！哈！

lines.en: When I had made an end of these labors, it was four o'clock in the morning. As a clock sounded the hour, there came a noise at the street door. I went down to open it with a light heart -- for what had I now to fear? There entered three men, who said they were officers of the police. A cry had been heard by a neighbor during the night; suspicion of a crime had been aroused; information had been given at the police office, and the officers had been sent to search the building.
lines.zh: 等我干完这些活，已经是凌晨四点了。钟声报时的时候，临街的门口传来了声音。我心情轻松地下楼去开门——因为我现在还有什么可怕的呢？进来了三个人，说他们是警官。夜里有邻居听到一声叫喊，怀疑发生了罪案，报了警，警官们就被派来搜查这栋房子。

lines.en: I smiled -- for what had I to fear? The cry, I said, was my own in a dream. The old man, I said, was not in the country. I took my visitors all over the house. I told them to search -- search well. I led them, at length, to his room. I brought chairs there, and told them to rest. I placed my own seat upon the very place under which lay the body of the victim.
lines.zh: 我笑了——因为我有什么可怕的呢？我说，那声叫喊是我自己做梦时喊的。我说，老人到乡下去了。我领着客人们把整栋房子看了个遍，让他们搜——好好地搜。最后我领他们到了他的房间，搬来椅子，请他们歇歇。我把自己的座位就放在受害者尸体正上方的那个地方。

lines.en: The officers were satisfied. I was completely at ease. They sat, and while I answered happily, they talked of common things. But, after a while, I felt myself getting weak and wished them gone. My head hurt, and I had a ringing in my ears; but still they sat and talked.
lines.zh: 警官们很满意。我也完全放松下来。他们坐着，我愉快地回答问题，他们聊着家常。可过了一会儿，我觉得自己虚弱起来，希望他们快走。我头疼，耳朵里嗡嗡作响，可他们还坐着聊天。

lines.en: The ringing became more severe. I talked more freely to do away with the feeling. But it continued until, at length, I found that the noise was not within my ears.
lines.zh: 嗡嗡声越来越厉害。我说得更起劲，想摆脱这种感觉。可它一直不停，最后我发现，那声音不在我耳朵里。

lines.en: I talked more and with a heightened voice. Yet the sound increased -- and what could I do? It was a low, dull, quick sound like a watch makes when inside a piece of cotton. I had trouble breathing -- and yet the officers heard it not. I talked more quickly -- more loudly; but the noise increased. I stood up and argued about silly things, in a high voice and with violent hand movements. But the noise kept increasing.
lines.zh: 我说得更多，声音也更高。可那声音越来越大——我能怎么办？那是一种低沉、沉闷、急促的声音，就像一块表裹在棉花里发出的声音。我喘不过气来——可警官们却没听见。我说得更快、更响，可那声音还在变大。我站起来，高声争论一些无聊的事，手舞足蹈。可那声音还在不断变大。

lines.en: Why would they not be gone? I walked across the floor with heavy steps, as if excited to anger by the observations of the men -- but the noise increased. What could I do? I swung my chair and moved it upon the floor, but the noise continually increased. It grew louder -- louder -- louder! And still the men talked pleasantly, and smiled.
lines.zh: 他们为什么还不走？我迈着沉重的步子在地板上走来走去，好像被他们的话激怒了——可那声音越来越大。我能怎么办？我抡起椅子在地板上拖来拖去，可那声音不停地变大。它越来越响——越来越响——越来越响！而那几个人还在愉快地聊天、微笑。

lines.en: Was it possible they heard not? No, no! They heard! They suspected! They knew! They were making a joke of my horror! This I thought, and this I think. But anything was better than this pain! I could bear those smiles no longer! I felt that I must scream or die! And now -- again! Louder! Louder! Louder!
lines.zh: 难道他们真的没听见？不，不！他们听见了！他们起疑了！他们知道了！他们在拿我的恐惧开玩笑！我当时这么想，现在也这么想。可什么都比这种痛苦强！我再也受不了那些笑容了！我觉得我必须尖叫，否则就会死！听——又来了！更响了！更响了！更响了！

lines.en: "Villains!" I cried, "Pretend no more! I admit the deed! Tear up the floor boards! Here, here! It is the beating of his hideous heart!"
lines.zh: “恶棍们！”我喊道，“别再装了！我承认是我干的！撬开地板！这儿，这儿！是他那颗可怕的心在跳！”

qs.q: Why did the narrator kill the old man?
opts: He hated the old man's eye.
qs.a: He hated the old man's eye.
qs.why: "I think it was his eye!"

qs.q: Where did he hide the body?
qs.a: under the floor boards
qs.why: "placed his body parts under the room."

qs.q: Why did he admit the crime?
opts: He could not stand the sound of the beating heart.
qs.a: He could not stand the sound of the beating heart.
qs.why: "It is the beating of his hideous heart!"

lessons.title: To Build a Fire
lessons.sum: 零下六十度的阿拉斯加，一个初来乍到的男人不听老人劝告，带着一条狼狗独自赶路。他不小心踩破冰层弄湿了双脚，必须生火自救——第一堆火被树上落下的积雪压灭了，冻僵的手指再也划不着火柴……

lines.en: Our story today is called "To Build a Fire." It was written by Jack London and adapted by Dona de Sanctis. Here is Harry Monroe with the story.
lines.zh: 我们今天的故事叫《生火》，作者是杰克·伦敦，由多娜·德桑克蒂斯改编。下面请哈里·门罗讲述。

lines.en: The man walked down the trail on a cold, gray day. Pure white snow and ice covered the Earth for as far as he could see. This was his first winter in Alaska. He was wearing heavy clothes and fur boots. But he still felt cold and uncomfortable.
lines.zh: 一个寒冷灰暗的日子，那人沿着小路走着。放眼望去，大地被洁白的冰雪覆盖。这是他在阿拉斯加度过的第一个冬天。他穿着厚衣服和毛皮靴子，可还是觉得又冷又难受。

lines.en: The man was on his way to a camp near Henderson Creek. His friends were already there. He expected to reach Henderson Creek by six o'clock that evening. It would be dark by then. His friends would have a fire and hot food ready for him.
lines.zh: 那人要去亨德森溪附近的一个营地，他的朋友们已经在那里了。他预计当天傍晚六点能到亨德森溪，那时天已经黑了。朋友们会为他准备好火和热饭。

lines.en: A dog walked behind the man. It was a big gray animal, half dog and half wolf. The dog did not like the extreme cold. It knew the weather was too cold to travel.
lines.zh: 一条狗跟在那人后面。那是一只灰色的大狗，一半是狗，一半是狼。这狗不喜欢这种严寒。它知道天气太冷，不适合赶路。

lines.en: The man continued to walk down the trail. He came to a frozen stream called Indian Creek. He began to walk on the snow-covered ice. It was a trail that would lead him straight to Henderson Creek and his friends.
lines.zh: 那人沿着小路继续走，来到一条叫印第安溪的冰冻小溪。他开始在覆盖着雪的冰面上走。这条路能直接把他带到亨德森溪，带到朋友们身边。

lines.en: As he walked, he looked carefully at the ice in front of him. Once, he stopped suddenly, and then walked around a part of the frozen stream. He saw that an underground spring flowed under the ice at that spot. It made the ice thin. If he stepped there, he might break through the ice into a pool of water. To get his boots wet in such cold weather might kill him. His feet would turn to ice quickly. He could freeze to death.
lines.zh: 他边走边仔细看着前面的冰面。有一次，他突然停下，绕开了冰冻溪流的一段。他看出那里冰下有一股地下泉水在流，让冰变薄了。要是踩上去，他可能会踩破冰层掉进水坑。在这么冷的天气里弄湿靴子可能会要了他的命：他的脚会很快冻成冰，他可能会被冻死。

lines.en: At about twelve o'clock, the man decided to stop to eat his lunch. He took off the glove on his right hand. He opened his jacket and shirt, and pulled out his bread and meat. This took less than twenty seconds. Yet, his fingers began to freeze.
lines.zh: 大约十二点，那人决定停下来吃午饭。他摘下右手的手套，解开外套和衬衫，掏出面包和肉。这只用了不到二十秒，可他的手指已经开始冻僵了。

lines.en: He hit his hand against his leg several times until he felt a sharp pain. Then he quickly put his glove on his hand. He made a fire, beginning with small pieces of wood and adding larger ones. He sat on a snow-covered log and ate his lunch. He enjoyed the warm fire for a few minutes. Then he stood up and started walking on the frozen stream again.
lines.zh: 他用手在腿上拍打了好几下，直到感觉到一阵刺痛。然后他赶紧戴上手套。他生了一堆火，先用小木片，再加大块的木头。他坐在一根盖着雪的木头上吃午饭，享受了几分钟温暖的火。然后他站起来，又开始在冰冻的溪面上走。

lines.en: A half hour later, it happened. At a place where the snow seemed very solid, the ice broke. The man's feet sank into the water. It was not deep, but his legs got wet to the knees. The man was angry. The accident would delay his arrival at the camp. He would have to build a fire now to dry his clothes and boots.
lines.zh: 半小时后，事情发生了。在一个雪看起来很结实的地方，冰裂开了。那人的脚陷进了水里。水不深，可他的腿湿到了膝盖。那人很生气。这个意外会耽误他到营地的时间。他现在得生火烘干衣服和靴子了。

lines.en: He walked over to some small trees. They were covered with snow. In their branches were pieces of dry grass and wood left by flood waters earlier in the year. He put several large pieces of wood on the snow, under one of the trees. On top of the wood, he put some grass and dry branches. He pulled off his gloves, took out his matches, and lighted the fire. He fed the young flame with more wood. As the fire grew stronger, he gave it larger pieces of wood.
lines.zh: 他走到几棵小树旁边。树上盖着雪，树枝间夹着年初洪水留下的干草和干木头。他把几大块木头放在一棵树下的雪地上，在木头上面放了些草和干树枝。他脱下手套，拿出火柴，点着了火。他往小火苗上添更多的木头。火越烧越旺，他就加更大的木块。

lines.en: He worked slowly and carefully. At sixty degrees below zero, a man with wet feet must not fail in his first attempt to build a fire. While he was walking, his blood had kept all parts of his body warm. Now that he had stopped, cold was forcing his blood to withdraw deeper into his body. His wet feet had frozen. He could not feel his fingers. His nose was frozen, too. The skin all over his body felt cold.
lines.zh: 他干得又慢又小心。在零下六十度，一个湿了脚的人第一次生火绝不能失败。走路的时候，他的血液让身体各处都保持着温暖。现在他停了下来，寒冷正把他的血液逼向身体深处。他湿透的脚已经冻住了，手指也没了知觉，鼻子也冻了，全身的皮肤都冰凉。

lines.en: Now, however, his fire was beginning to burn more strongly. He was safe. He sat under the tree and thought of the old men in Fairbanks. The old men had told him that no man should travel alone in the Yukon when the temperature is sixty degrees below zero. Yet here he was. He had had an accident. He was alone. And he had saved himself. He had built a fire.
lines.zh: 不过现在，他的火开始烧得更旺了。他安全了。他坐在树下，想起了费尔班克斯的那些老人。老人们告诉过他，气温零下六十度时，谁也不该一个人在育空地区赶路。可他还是来了。他出了意外，他孤身一人，可他救了自己。他生起了火。

lines.en: Those old men were weak, he thought. A real man could travel alone. If a man stayed calm, he would be all right. The man's boots were covered with ice. The strings on his boots were as hard as steel. He would have to cut them with his knife.
lines.zh: 他想，那些老人太软弱了。真正的男子汉可以一个人赶路。只要保持冷静，就不会有事。他的靴子上结满了冰，鞋带硬得像钢丝。他得用刀把它们割断。

lines.en: He leaned back against the tree to take out his knife. Suddenly, without warning, a heavy mass of snow dropped down. His movement had shaken the young tree only a tiny bit. But it was enough to cause the branches of the tree to drop their heavy load. The man was shocked. He sat and looked at the place where the fire had been.
lines.zh: 他往后靠在树上去掏刀。突然，毫无预兆地，一大团沉重的雪掉了下来。他的动作只是轻轻晃动了一下这棵小树，却足以让树枝上沉重的积雪落下。那人惊呆了。他坐着，望着刚才火堆所在的地方。

lines.en: The old men had been right, he thought. If he had another man with him, he would not be in any danger now. The other man could build the fire. Well, it was up to him to build the fire again. This time, he must not fail.
lines.zh: 他想，那些老人说得对。要是他身边还有一个人，现在就不会有危险了，那个人可以生火。好吧，现在只能靠他自己重新生火了。这次，他绝不能失败。

lines.en: The man collected more wood. He reached into his pocket for the matches. But his fingers were frozen. He could not hold them. He began to hit his hands with all his force against his legs.
lines.zh: 那人又收集了些木头。他把手伸进口袋去拿火柴，可他的手指冻僵了，拿不住。他开始用全身力气在腿上拍打双手。

lines.en: After a while, feeling came back to his fingers. The man reached again into his pocket for the matches. But the tremendous cold quickly drove the life out of his fingers. All the matches fell onto the snow. He tried to pick one up, but failed.
lines.zh: 过了一会儿，手指恢复了知觉。那人又把手伸进口袋拿火柴。可极度的寒冷很快又让他的手指失去了生气。火柴全掉在了雪地上。他想捡起一根，却没成功。

lines.en: The man pulled on his glove and again beat his hand against his leg. Then he took the gloves off both hands and picked up all the matches. He gathered them together. Holding them with both hands, he scratched the matches along his leg. They immediately caught fire.
lines.zh: 那人戴上手套，又用手拍打腿。然后他把两只手的手套都脱下来，把所有火柴都捡了起来，聚成一把。他用两只手握着火柴，在腿上一划，火柴立刻全着了。

lines.en: He held the blazing matches to a piece of wood. After a while, he became aware that he could smell his hands burning. Then he began to feel the pain. He opened his hands, and the blazing matches fell on to the snow. The flame went out in a puff of gray smoke.
lines.zh: 他把燃烧的火柴凑到一块木头上。过了一会儿，他意识到自己闻到了手被烧焦的味道。接着他开始感到疼。他张开手，燃烧的火柴掉在雪地上，火焰化作一缕灰烟熄灭了。

lines.en: The man looked up. The dog was still watching him. The man got an idea. He would kill the dog and bury his hands inside its warm body. When the feeling came back to his fingers, he could build another fire. He called to the dog. The dog heard danger in the man's voice. It backed away.
lines.zh: 那人抬起头。那条狗还在看着他。那人想到一个主意：他要杀了这条狗，把手埋进它温暖的身体里。等手指恢复了知觉，他就能再生一堆火。他叫狗过来。狗从他的声音里听出了危险，往后退了。

lines.en: The man called again. This time the dog came closer. The man reached for his knife. But he had forgotten that he could not bend his fingers. He could not kill the dog, because he could not hold his knife.
lines.zh: 那人又叫了一声。这次狗走近了些。那人伸手去拿刀，可他忘了自己的手指弯不了。他杀不了狗，因为他握不住刀。

lines.en: The fear of death came over the man. He jumped up and began to run. The running began to make him feel better. Maybe running would make his feet warm. If he ran far enough, he would reach his friends at Henderson Creek. They would take care of him.
lines.zh: 对死亡的恐惧笼罩了他。他跳起来开始跑。跑起来让他感觉好了些。也许跑步能让他的脚暖和起来。如果跑得够远，他就能到亨德森溪找到朋友们，他们会照顾他。

lines.en: It felt strange to run and not feel his feet when they hit the ground. He fell several times. He decided to rest a while. As he lay in the snow, he noticed that he was not shaking. He could not feel his nose or fingers or feet. Yet, he was feeling quite warm and comfortable. He realized he was going to die.
lines.zh: 跑着却感觉不到脚落地，这感觉很奇怪。他摔倒了好几次。他决定休息一会儿。躺在雪地上时，他发现自己不发抖了。他感觉不到鼻子、手指和脚，可他却觉得相当温暖舒服。他明白自己快要死了。

lines.en: Well, he decided, he might as well take it like a man. There were worse ways to die.
lines.zh: 好吧，他想，那就像个男子汉一样面对吧。还有比这更糟的死法。

lines.en: The man closed his eyes and floated into the most comfortable sleep he had ever known.
lines.zh: 那人闭上眼睛，飘进了他这辈子最舒服的一场睡眠。

lines.en: The dog sat facing him, waiting. Finally, the dog moved closer to the man and caught the smell of death. The animal threw back its head. It let out a long, soft cry to the cold stars in the black sky.
lines.zh: 狗坐在他对面，等着。最后，狗走近那人，闻到了死亡的气味。它仰起头，对着漆黑天空中寒冷的星星，发出一声长长的、轻柔的嚎叫。

lines.en: And then it turned and ran toward Henderson Creek…where it knew there was food and a fire.
lines.zh: 然后它转身朝亨德森溪跑去……它知道那里有食物，有火。

qs.q: What did the old men in Fairbanks tell him?
opts: No man should travel alone at sixty below zero.
qs.a: No man should travel alone at sixty below zero.
qs.why: "no man should travel alone in the Yukon when the temperature is sixty degrees below zero."

qs.q: What put out his first big fire?
opts: Snow fell from the tree onto it.
qs.a: Snow fell from the tree onto it.
qs.why: "a heavy mass of snow dropped down."

qs.q: What did the dog do at the end?
opts: It ran to the camp where there was food and fire.
qs.a: It ran to the camp where there was food and fire.
qs.why: "it turned and ran toward Henderson Creek."
